# Micro-Checklist — Archive

Built and verified work, filed under the same modules and sub-modules as the live tracker **[docs/micro_checklist.md](../micro_checklist.md)**. An item moves from a sub-module there to the same sub-module here once it is `[x]`; the module skeleton is identical in both files. Item ids never change, so search by id (e.g. `47.11.4`).

**Background notes** at the bottom keep the stage write-ups with their items lifted out: closed stages whole, and the closed parts of open ones. Arranged by module 2026-11-10; before that this file was arranged by stage. Read it only when you need the history of built work.

## PIM — Products & Item Master

### PIM › Item master & item form

- [x] **46.1** Item code/SKU charset allowlist, closing the durability audit's finding 6 (`itemCodePattern` in `validateItemMasterRules`, forward-only gate).
- [x] **35.7** Bundles, kits and virtual SKUs — **built and dev-applied 2026-08-22**
  - [x] **35.7.1** `ProductBundle` definition with an explicit `Virtual` vs `Stocked` fulfillment mode and three pricing modes: `Parent Price` (channel/manual order price allocated over components), `Fixed Price` (bundle master price), and `Component Price` (configured component unit prices). Components carry SKU, positive whole quantity and optional price weight/unit price. Generic-document validation requires active Item masters, rejects repeated/self/nested components and prevents two active definitions for one bundle SKU. This is deliberately a commercial OMS object beside manufacturing `BOM`: a BOM produces a controlled finished good through Production/VAS; a ProductBundle decides how a sellable SKU is priced, made available and picked.
  - [x] **35.7.2** Virtual bundle ATS is never stored. `ComputeSellableSKUATS` computes each component bucket through the existing `computeATS`, divides by component quantity and takes the scarcest ratio. Per-location ATS is exact; network ATS conservatively sums complete per-location bundle capacity, so stock stranded across incompatible facilities cannot form a fictitious bundle. `GetAvailableToSell` and Stage 35.6 channel inventory sync both use this seam. Stocked kits read their own assembled inventory instead of double-counting components.
  - [x] **35.7.3** `CreateSalesOrder` expands every active Virtual bundle before validation, sourcing and reservation. Warehouse lines therefore contain real component SKUs/quantities and preserve `bundle_sku`, ordered bundle quantity, component-per-bundle quantity and pricing mode. Parent/fixed prices are allocated across child lines with the final line taking the remainder; component-price mode ignores an untrusted inbound parent price. The SalesOrder retains a commercial `bundle_lines` summary and exact total. Stocked kits deliberately remain one pickable line.
  - [x] **35.7.4** Stocked-kit Assemble/Disassemble operations create immutable `BundleAssembly` evidence and apply component + kit availability changes and one `StockLedgerEntry` per movement in a **single database transaction**. Consumption checks real ATS (including reservations/holds/buffers), not merely `available`; any shortage rolls back the operation record, every stock mutation and every ledger row. Optional request keys are unique/idempotent. Virtual bundles refuse physical assembly.
  - **Surface/UI/schema**: additive multi-tenant migration `migrations_stage35_7_bundles_kits.sql` (applied + ledger-recorded on dev only), new `engines/bundles.go` and regression suite, ProductBundle validation hook, two gated API routes (OMS availability; WMS assemble/disassemble), and an OMS Bundles and Kits panel with per-location ATS, definition management and stocked-kit operations. No new dependency.
  - **Verified**: real-Postgres test covers all three pricing modes, nested-bundle refusal, derived location/network ATS, virtual order explosion/reservation and exact revenue, stocked-kit non-explosion, atomic assembly, request replay, disassembly, shortage rollback and stock ledger evidence. `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`, `node --check public/app.js`, and `go test ./... -p 1 -count=1` fully green on the combined shared tree. Both current tenant schemas have the two doctypes; Stage 42.6 migration remains unapplied.

- [x] **86.3 The ERP's own item attributes, separate from PIM's.** Cause found first: `ProductAttributeDef` is entitled by `pim`, so a client without PIM got no attribute list and no variant options on the Item form or the PO design panel. User, 2026-10-18, on separate lists: *"Yes. PIM attribute is diff and erp is diff ... I can sell different app to client one or the another ... PIM will map it and have more attribute but ERP will have very basic attribute."* (An interim fix that re-entitled `ProductAttributeDef` to `inventory` was replaced before commit; local DB put back.)
  - **New doctype `ItemAttribute`** (module Inventory / `inventory`, Master) - Setup → *Inventory* → **Item Attribute**: code (numbered, format asked once, prefix `IA`), label, value type, values (chips form, as PIM's), unit, status, library id. Read by the Item's variant options (`view-pickers.js`), the PO design panel and `GetDesignMatrix` (so Stage 87's PO attribute columns and print fields follow), and `AddDesignAttributeValue` (a PO's + value / + attribute; new ones get id `IA-<code>`). Delete guard and kept identity (PIM-0690) cover both lists; PIM-0691 now points at Setup → Item Attribute.
  - **PIM keeps `ProductAttributeDef`** (unchanged entitlement), plus `erp_attribute` - the ERP attribute it maps onto.
  - **Migration `db/migrations_stage86_3_item_attributes_core.sql`** (additive, idempotent, every schema): doctype + fields + role permissions copied from `ProductAttributeDef`'s (who could see / change attributes keeps exactly that); every live PIM attribute the ERP already used (Used for *Variant* or blank) is **copied** - never moved - to an `ItemAttribute` with the **same code** (id `IA-<code>`, because ids are unique across record types), so every item and design keeps finding its values under the key it stored; the PIM record gains `erp_attribute`. Product-information attributes are not copied. Re-run: no change.
  - **Library apply** (Control Panel → Attributes): a Variant pick goes to the ERP list, and - for a client with PIM - to PIM's list as well, mapped (`erp_attribute`); a Product information pick goes to PIM's list only, and is skipped for a client without PIM. "Has it" shows which list; the client's other attributes show their list.

### PIM › Designs, combinations & variants

- [x] **51.5** Jewellery Item Master attributes + Design ID / Combination ID (SKU) generation. **Decision (user, 2026-09-22): standard jewellery attribute set.** Added to `Item` via `public/profiles/jewelry.json`'s existing additive overlay mechanism (module/document_type set to Item's real current values, `Inventory`/`Master`, so the overlay is a no-op on those two columns — checked first, since an industry switch overwrites them unconditionally and Item is used far outside PIM): metal type, purity/karat, gross weight, net weight, stone type, stone weight, making-charge type & value, size. Design ID / Combination ID turned out to be a wiring gap, not new infrastructure, once traced fully: `engines.GenerateVariantCode` (parent code + attribute map → child code) already existed with **zero callers anywhere**, and `ValidateItemVariantUniqueness` already groups sibling variants by the existing `parent_product_code`/`variant_option_values` fields — not `family`/ProductFamily, a separate, orthogonal concept (attribute-completeness policy). New `engines.PrepareItemVariantCode` (Item create, no explicit `code`) bridges `family` → `parent_product_code` when the latter is blank (so ProductFamily, already auto-numbered like any Master doctype, serves as the real "Design ID" record), merges a small fixed set of variant-differentiating fields (`metal_type`, `purity_karat`, `stone_type`, `size` — deliberately excluding continuous/measured fields like weight) into `variant_option_values`, and calls `GenerateVariantCode` for the Combination ID/SKU. Fixed a real latent bug in `GenerateVariantCode` while making it live for the first time: its no-pattern fallback iterated a Go map directly, which is iteration-order-randomized — the same attribute set could render as a differently-ordered code between calls; now sorted. Frontend: Item's `code` field skips the `/api/v1/sequence` pre-fill when `family` is set, so the server generates the combination code instead (`public/app.js`). Also seeded `ProductFamily` a friendlier "Design" prefix via `db/migrations_stage51_5_design_numbering.sql` (51.4's same mechanism). **Verified**: `TestGenerateVariantCodeIsDeterministic`/`TestGenerateVariantCodeCustomPattern`/`TestPrepareItemVariantCodeFromFamily`/`TestPrepareItemVariantCodeExplicitOptionsWinOverFields`/`TestPrepareItemVariantCodeNoOpCases` all pass (pure unit tests, no DB); `go build`/`node --check` clean.
- [x] **80.2 Variant options as Option + Value rows.** `attachVariantOptionsEditor` turns the `variant_option_values` box into rows: Option = the Active `ProductAttributeDef` records (stored by code, as PO designs store them) plus **Other…** for a typed name; Value = the attribute's Select options, else text; **+ Add option**, **×**. Writes the same `Key:Value;Key:Value` string into the same (now hidden) input; `:`/`;` typed into a name or value are folded to a space. Existing values round-trip byte-identical (verified on `COL41566:Red;SIZ41566:M`). Parent Product Code placeholder on create: *Same as the design if left blank* (`PrepareItemVariantCode` bridges it). `db/migrations_stage80_1_item_form_labels.sql` relabels *Variant Options (Key:Value;Key:Value)* → *Variant Options* and drops *(optional)* from five Item labels, only where the shipped wording is unchanged.
- [x] **117.1 A Combination ID is a running number, not the design plus its values** (user, 2026-10-19: *"D00001-Red-S No I want sequnce for that as well."*). A new combination takes the next number from the Item series (one series for every item; the prefix is set on Prefix Configurations), as a single-item design already does (94.16). Existing combinations keep their IDs. Built: `PrepareItemVariantCode` records the values and refuses a duplicate by design + values before any number is drawn (moved ahead of `PrepareMasterNumber` in the save handler); `PrepareMasterNumber` and CSV import no longer skip combinations; the unused `GenerateVariantCode` / `itemHasVariantValues` and the 94.16 skip test removed. *Verified 2026-10-19:* scratch server (5490 DB) - two combinations under a new design got I00010, I00011, the same values again refused naming I00010, earlier refused saves left no gap; engines + server suites pass. *Status: Done*

### PIM › Barcodes & item lookup

- [x] **24.23** `crypto/rand` for barcode generation (was `math/rand`).
- [x] **30.1.1 Resolve POS SKU by code/barcode, not just internal id — closed 2026-07-31.** New `ResolveItemBySKU` (`engines/item_lookup.go`) is the one shared Item lookup: one query, deterministic `code` → `barcode` → `id` priority, soft-deleted rows excluded, typed `ErrItemNotFound`. Adopted by `GetItemGSTInfo` (so checkout *and* PurchaseOrder GST both inherit it), `validateOrderChain` (`engines/orders.go`, which had the mirror-image bug — matched only `code`, so a channel sending a barcode/id was held as an unmapped SKU) and sticker printing (`engines/stickers.go`, which printed blank name/HSN for any code-keyed run). Covered by `engines/item_lookup_test.go` — all three identifiers, a soft-deleted item, an empty SKU, and a code-vs-another-item's-barcode collision (Code must win, or a collision sells the wrong product at the wrong tax rate). **Live-verified** (scratch server :8147, real `custom_erp`): before, Code and Barcode returned "item not found"; after, all three resolve identically and a sale completes by Code end-to-end.
- [x] **51.6** Automatic barcode generation at GRN. **Decision (user, 2026-09-22): fully automatic.** New `engines.EnsureItemBarcodes(tenantID, items)`, called from the GRN receipt-posting success path in `handlers_core_doc_engine.go` (after `PostGRNReceiptWithQC` succeeds, so a barcode failure never blocks or reverses a receipt that already posted stock — best-effort by design, logged via `LogSystemError` on failure). For each distinct SKU in the receipt with no existing `barcode`, generates one via the existing `GenerateEANBarcode` (previously reachable only through a standalone manual PIM action, zero automatic callers) and writes it onto the Item record; an Item that already has a barcode, or doesn't exist, is left alone; idempotent across repeated calls/duplicate SKUs in the same receipt. Print-on-receipt (physical printer trigger) was explicitly left out of this pass pending a scope confirmation, per the original plan's own caution about wiring a printer into a posting transaction — barcode *generation* is what was decided as fully automatic; printing still uses the existing manual sticker/label path. **Verified**: `TestEnsureItemBarcodesGeneratesOnlyWhenMissing` (own throwaway tenant schema) covers generate-when-missing, preserve-existing, unknown-SKU-is-a-no-op, and idempotency across a second call; `go build` clean.

  identity and is not a small change. Check overlap with the Stage 51 GRN-barcode item.
  — *2026-10-06: built and verified.* An Item already is the SKU/variant here (the parent design is a Product Family, which never has a barcode), so: Item.barcode no longer mandatory (all tenants); settings `inventory.barcode_generate_at` (sku_create default / grn / off) and `inventory.barcode_per_receipt_date` (no / yes); `PrepareItemBarcode` on Item create; `EnsureReceiptBarcodes` at GRN (permanent code unless off; one dated EAN-13 `02`+YYMMDD+NNNN per SKU per day in the new **ItemBarcode** register, daily `PIMDatedBarcodeSeq`); `ResolveItemBySKU` and pick/pack scans resolve registered codes; GRN stickers print the receipt's dated code. Tests `TestDatedEANFromParts`, `TestEnsureReceiptBarcodesPerDate` (caught a same-day second-receipt gap, fixed by recording every receipt on the register row) plus existing barcode/lookup/sticker suites green; live: an Item saved without a barcode was issued `0200000000011`. ### PIM › Pricing, MRP & market prices

- [x] **34.1** `CompetitorPrice` doctype + CSV ingestion — built 2026-08-07. `db/migrations_stage34_1_competitor_price.sql`: 12 fields (`code`, `our_item` Link→Item, `competitor_product`, `competitor_sku`, `platform` Select, `competitor_price`, `mrp`, `rating`, `review_count`, `observed_at` Date, `source_url`, `status`), `role_permissions` for HR/Admin (full) and Store Manager (read/create/update), and the standard backfill loop over already-provisioned tenant schemas. Zero Go code and zero JavaScript: registered as **Master** (not Transaction) deliberately, because the Setup flyout and the generic doctype table both filter on `document_type = 'Master'` — Master is what gets the generic list, the New form and the **Bulk Import** button for free, and a Transaction doctype would have been unreachable from the UI, which is exactly the trap `CycleCountLine` had to be worked around (`app.js:6505`). `our_item` is deliberately **not** mandatory so an unmatched competitor listing is still recordable. Validation is entirely `ValidateDocument`'s metadata-driven path as planned — live-verified that it rejects a missing mandatory field, an out-of-list `platform`, and a dangling `our_item` Link.
  - **Found and fixed a real bug affecting 89 doctypes, not just this one.** `GenerateCSVTemplate` (`import.go:377`) deliberately omits `id`/`status` from the header row it emits, and `ValidateDocument` (`doctype.go:314`) skips the mandatory check for those same two system fields — but `missingMandatoryColumns` (`import.go:137`) did neither, so **any** doctype declaring a mandatory `status` field rejected its own generated template with `DATAIM-0164 "missing mandatory column(s): status"`. That is 89 doctypes including Brand, Color, Customer, Vendor, Location, Employee and `CycleCountLine`, whose bulk import is the only way it is meant to be filled at all. Fixed at the shared choke point (skip `id`/`status`, matching the other two functions) rather than by making `CompetitorPrice.status` optional, so every affected doctype is repaired at once. Found by literally following the documented download-template-then-upload path instead of hand-writing a CSV that happened to include `status`.
- [x] **34.2** Price-gap report via `RegisterReport` — built 2026-08-07 as `competitor-price-gap` (Category "Sales") in `engines/market_intelligence.go`. Picks the **cheapest** current observation per SKU (best for the shopper, worst for us) and columns out our price, best competitor price, platform, gap in ₹ and %, above/at/below, observation count and source URL, with optional platform / SKU / observed-since / position filters. Live-verified over HTTP end to end: CSV import → catalog listing → run → correct cheapest-wins pick → correct gap math (599 vs 499 → ₹100, 20.04%, "Above") → platform filter changing which competitor row wins.
  - **⚠️ The item's own premise was wrong and the implementation departs from it deliberately.** 34.2 was written as "joins `CompetitorPrice` to our `Item`/price list". **There is no price list, and `Item` has no price field of any kind** — verified against `doctype_fields` (`code`/`name`/`barcode`/`weight`/`volume`/`category`/`hsn_code`/`gst_rate`/`family`/`parent_product_code`/`variant_option_values`), and the POS cashier types the sale price by hand per line (`app.js` pushes `salePrice: 0` and renders an editable input). So "our price" is resolved at report time as the **last price we actually transacted at**, newest wins across `SalesOrderLine.unit_price` and `POSCart items[].sale_price`. This needs no schema change and invents no pricing architecture — price lists per channel/customer-group with effective dates is a real feature and a real product decision, not something to slip in under a competitor-pricing item. Cost: a SKU never sold has no our-price, and reports `Position = "No price on file"` with null gap columns rather than a fabricated zero that would rank top of the gap list. **If a real price master is ever wanted, that is a new item; `competitorOurPriceCTE` is the single place to repoint.** (Also: `POSCart.items` is stored as a real JSON array by some writers and a JSON-encoded *string* by others — both shapes exist in the dev DB and both are normalised.)
- [x] **34.3** Undercut alert worker — built 2026-08-07 as `StartCompetitorUndercutWorker(ctx, 1h)` (`engines/market_intelligence.go`, started in `routes.go` alongside the other ten workers). Fires the **existing** `DispatchNotification` path with a new `Competitor Undercut` event added to `NotificationTemplate.event`'s Select options, so an admin authors the alert body in the existing Setup UI rather than the event being a magic string only Go knows. Threshold is the new `market.undercut_threshold_pct` setting, **default 0 = disabled**, so a tenant that never loads competitor prices is never alerted about them; bounded at 90 because "a competitor is 95% cheaper" is a data-entry error, not a pricing signal. De-duplicated through `public.competitor_undercut_state.last_run_at` (same single-row shape as `patch_intake_state`), so one observation alerts at most once no matter how often the worker ticks or how long the undercut persists — without that it would re-alert on the same standing undercut every hour. Reads only; never changes a price, document or configuration. `db/migrations_stage34_3_undercut_alert.sql`.

- [x] **26.4.11** AI content-assist — **decision taken and built 2026-08-06.** Scope decision (user): **local/offline only**, no third-party model API. New `engines/pim_content_assist.go` composes a draft (`title`/`seo_title`/`short_desc`/`long_desc`/`tags`) from the product's **own** data — Item fields plus family attribute values resolved through the existing `ResolveAttributeValue` (26.4.1), so locale/channel overrides apply here exactly as they do to completeness scoring and the outbound publish payload, rather than via a second resolution path. Deterministic templates, no network call, no API key.
  - **The four governance questions `go_live_decisions.md` §11 asks are answered by construction, not by policy.** (1) *What leaves the server*: nothing — no provider. (2) *Human-in-the-loop*: `GenerateContentSuggestion` **returns** a suggestion and has no code path that writes `ProductContent`; whoever accepts it saves an ordinary Draft, which still passes the existing Stage 15.1/26.4.5 approval gate. There is a test asserting zero `ProductContent` rows are created, so a future refactor that "helpfully" persists the draft fails the build rather than silently removing the guarantee. (3) *Audit*: every generation writes a `ContentAssistLog` row (generated text + the source fields it rested on + user + `generator: local-template-v1` — names the generator, not a model, so rows stay unambiguous if a real model is ever introduced). (4) *Prompt injection*: no prompt exists, but the related risk is real because supplier-submitted attribute values (26.4.10) can reach published copy — `sanitizeAssistInput` strips angle brackets and control characters from every value before composition, with a test asserting no angle bracket can survive.
  - **Storage follows the `ReportRunLog`/`StockLedgerEntry` precedent** — a plain row in `documents`, no bespoke table. Chosen specifically because a bespoke table needs an entry in `ProvisionTenantSchema`'s clone list, which is exactly the drift 26.11.2 caught after it had already cost every new tenant its GL/approvals/WMS tables. Read-only for HR/Admin via the generic API; `writeContentAssistLog` inserts directly.
  - **Quality caveat, stated plainly**: deterministic templates restate known attributes. ## PROC — Procurement & Vendors

### PROC › Vendors

- [x] **13.9 Vendor/Customer masters** — registered as real Master doctypes, full generic CRUD for free.
- [x] **26.4.10** Supplier portal — **built and live-verified 2026-08-05.** Product decision taken 2026-08-05: **limited-role login, not a separate portal.** A second app would mean a second auth system, session story, deployment and set of security rules to keep in step, for what is in substance "an outside party fills in a form an internal reviewer approves" — all of which this ERP already has. So a supplier is a user whose role reaches exactly one doctype.
  - New `SupplierSubmission` doctype (module `pim`, Transaction), whose field set deliberately mirrors `ProductContent`'s so an approved submission is a field-for-field copy rather than a translation table that would drift. Plus `media_url`, the one field with no counterpart — suppliers have no DAM access, so they submit a URL for a reviewer to judge. **Not** auto-fetched on approval: a server that downloads arbitrary supplier-supplied URLs is an SSRF surface this stage does not need.
  - QC reuses the existing maker-checker engine (`approval_rules` row, HR/Admin as checker) — no bespoke review flow. Rejection comments were already mandatory there (APPROV-0159), so "why was my submission rejected" needed no new storage.
  - **Row-level scoping is what makes the limited-role shape safe**, and is the real work: doctype-level RBAC alone would let every supplier read every other supplier's submissions. New `users.supplier_code` ties a login to a Vendor; `handleGenericDoc` — the one choke point every document read and write already passes through — enforces it in three places: the list query, the single-document read, and the write path. On create `supplier_code` is **overwritten** from the session rather than validated (a supplier never picks whose name a submission is filed under); on update the **stored** code is checked, not the payload's, since the payload is attacker-controlled. A Supplier account with no vendor linked fails closed.
  - On approval the submission becomes `ProductContent` as **Draft**, never Approved — QC approval here means "this copy is acceptable to work with", not "publish it". ProductContent has its own approval gate, and short-circuiting it from an outside party's submission would let a supplier's text reach a live sales channel with no internal publish decision.
  - Frontend cost was one PIM tab ("Supplier Submissions"); suppliers reach the same doctype through the existing generic table screen, so there is no second list/table implementation either.
  - **Live-verified** by two handler-level tests against the real dev DB (`internal/server/supplier_portal_test.go`, both passing): a submission filed by supplier A while *claiming* vendor B is stored under A; B cannot list it, cannot read it by id, and cannot overwrite it by posting to its id (A's title verified unchanged); and an approved submission produces a Draft `ProductContent` carrying the supplier's title.

### PROC › Purchase orders

- [x] **4.1** `PurchaseOrder` metadata + status/cancellation tracking.
- [x] **30.5.6 Purchase Order's duplicate fields de-duplicated — closed 2026-08-01.** The remaining half was `vendor`/`vendor_id`: both mandatory, registered independently at different points in this project's history (`db/migration.sql` declared `vendor` as a Link, `db/migrations_phase3.sql` later declared `vendor_id` as Data), and **read by different consumers today** — `GetVendorLedgerReport` reads `vendor`, the payment-file and vendor-invoice paths read `vendor_id` — so neither can simply be dropped.
  - New `engines/document_mirror_fields.go` holds a doctype → mirror-pair registry and `PrepareMirroredFields`, attached at the same create/update choke point that numbers documents (and for the same reason: both halves are mandatory, so the copy must land before `ValidateDocument` runs). `FieldMeta.Mirrored` is derived from that same registry, so the generic form drops the duplicate box without a second doctype list in JavaScript.
  - **Deliberately a mirror, not a rename.** Renaming would need a data migration over every historical PO plus a sweep of every reader, for a pair whose only real cost is a confusing form. This removes the cost today and leaves the schema cleanup available later. It copies in **whichever direction has a value**, so an API caller that has always sent only `vendor_id` keeps working — the contract widens rather than narrows.

Screenshot taken, scratch server/fixtures torn down after.
  - **Real bug found and fixed, not specific to the PO composer: `internal/server/middleware.go`'s CSP had `connect-src 'self'` with no exception for QZ Tray's own WebSocket endpoints** (`ws://localhost:{8182,8283,8384,8485}`, `wss://localhost.qz.io:{8181,8282,8383,8484}` - Stage 31.1.1's own documented port list). Every `qzTryPrint` call in the entire app - receipts, invoices, shipping labels, and now POs - has been silently CSP-blocked from ever reaching QZ Tray in any CSP-enforcing browser since Stage 31.1 shipped, always falling straight to the browser fallback with no visible error. Nobody had caught this because every prior live-browser QZ pass (Stage 45, this one until the CSP fix) deliberately tested only "QZ Tray absent" - the fallback path - never a real connection attempt. Fixed by scoping `connect-src` to add exactly those two loopback hosts (`ws://localhost:*`, `wss://localhost.qz.io:*` - `:*` covers the exact 4 ports each without hardcoding them a second place to drift from `qz-print.js`), both of which resolve to `127.0.0.1` per that file's own comment, so this is not a new attack surface. This does not make 31.1.8's still-open physical-hardware verification any less genuinely blocked (no printer/QZ install on this machine), but it removes a defect that would have silently blocked it even once that hardware is available.

- [x] **5.1-5.2** GRN callback hooks, barcode generation, append-only availability read model, item returns.
- [x] **30.2.1 GRN can close a PO while posting zero stock — closed 2026-07-31.** Three halves, because one alone wasn't enough: (a) `db/migrations_stage30_2_1_grn_location.sql` declares `location` as a real mandatory GRN field, so the generic form renders it and `ValidateDocument` enforces it; (b) `engines.PrepareGRNReceipt` (`engines/transactional_validation.go`) defaults it from the referenced PO's `target_warehouse` (falling back to the PO's own `location`) *before* validation runs — same ordering and reasoning as `PreparePurchaseRequisition` — so an API/import caller that names a `po_id` keeps working unchanged; (c) a failed ledger post is no longer a bare `log.Printf` returning HTTP 200 "saved". The document row is already committed by then and can't be rolled back into the same transaction, so the receipt is reversed the way the domain already expresses it — status `Cancelled`, which is exactly what `fetchGRNReceivedQuantities` excludes, leaving the PO open for a real receipt — and the caller is told. Covered by `engines/grn_location_test.go` (including an assertion that the field is declared mandatory, so a missing migration fails loudly). **Live-verified**: a GRN posted through the generic API with no `location` at all took stock from 0 → 10 at the PO's warehouse; the same request previously returned 200 and posted nothing.
- [x] **26.3.1** GRN workbench screen — built and live-verified 2026-07-24. New **Goods Receipt (GRN)** screen (`renderGRNWorkbenchView`, `public/app.js`, Buying sidebar flyout) — the first UI GRN has ever had; it's a Transaction (not Master) doctype so it was never even reachable from the Setup submenu the generic doctype form relies on. PO Reference typeahead + "Load Items from PO" pre-fills lines from the PO's own `items` JSON (Received Qty defaulting to ordered, for the common no-variance case); manual "Add Line" for POs with no recorded items (most of them today — the PO create screen only ever saves `items: '[]'`, tracked separately as 26.3.6). Line shape matches `engines/transactional_validation.go`'s `grnReceivedLine` exactly (`sku`, `qty`, `accepted_qty`, `rejected_qty`, `rejection_reason`) so it inherits every existing server-side rule for free — GOODSR-0089/0090 accepted/rejected-qty checks and the PURCHA-0082/0084/0086/0087/0088 PO cross-checks — rather than a parallel validation path; `accepted_qty` is auto-derived as `qty − rejected_qty` client-side so it can never violate GOODSR-0089 by construction. Barcode preview: a best-effort `GET /api/v1/doc/Item/{sku}` lookup per line renders the Item's real barcode (falling back to the SKU itself on a miss, same degrade-gracefully behavior `engines.PrintStickers` already uses server-side) — not a new backend endpoint. No new backend route; posts through the existing `POST /api/v1/doc/GRN`. Two real bugs found and fixed during live verification: (1) `internal/server/handlers_core_doc_engine.go`'s GRN inventory-posting hook ran unconditionally on every save including edits (not just creates) — silently double-posting the same received qty into `inventory_availability` if a GRN were ever re-saved; gated to `id == ""` (create-only), same convention as the pre-existing Item/PIM-profile create-only check just above it in the same function. This was real but dormant (GRN had no UI at all before this screen, so nothing could trigger it) — closed before shipping a screen that could have newly triggered it, confirmed via a direct re-POST against a live-posted GRN that stock stayed at 10 instead of doubling to 20. (2) A race in `loadGRNItemsFromPO`: it fires from both the PO field's own `change` event (typeahead pick) and the explicit "Load Items from PO" button, so picking a PO and immediately clicking the button could launch two overlapping calls that duplicated every line (each resets `grnLineItems` then awaits a barcode lookup per line, so an interleaved second call's reset/pushes land on the same array the first call resumes into) — fixed with a reentrancy guard. Live-verified end-to-end via a throwaway-port server + Playwright (scratch HR/Admin token minted via a repo-internal `cmd/` program, deleted after) against a real seeded PO/Item/Vendor: loaded 1 line from a PO correctly (post-fix), posted a GRN, confirmed `inventory_availability` incremented by exactly the received qty, confirmed a same-content re-save did not double it, and confirmed the client-side rejected-qty guards and a real server-side PURCHA-0084 rejection ("PO already fully received") both surface cleanly in the form's error banner rather than a raw error. All test fixtures removed after (including two soft-deleted rows and one auto-created PIM profile that needed a direct SQL cleanup, since Approved transactional documents correctly refuse API-level deletion). `go build`/`go vet`/`node --check` clean.

## INV — Inventory & Planning

### INV › Stores & stock locations

- [x] **17.9 Location & organizational masters** — Location/LegalEntity/Department/CostCenter masters; existing free-text location fields kept as-is (validated against active masters, not migrated to Link fields) — 103 legacy codes seeded so validation never breaks existing data.
- [x] **21.13** "Stores" master fix — 3 compounding bugs: zero fields, zero role_permissions, a singular/plural sidebar typo.
- [x] **30.5.5 Resolved — `Stores` retired, its fields folded into `Location`. Closed 2026-08-02.**
  - **User's call (2026-08-02)**, chosen from three options put to them: retire `Stores` and fold its fields into `Location`, rather than keeping it and merely scrubbing it from the menu and docs. The deciding fact was that the four fields only `Stores` had — `address`, `city`, `contact_phone`, `manager` — were **write-only by construction**: there was nowhere else in the product to record a shop's address or phone at all, so "just hide it" would have left a real gap behind a removed menu entry.
  - `db/migrations_stage30_5_5_retire_stores.sql` does it in three steps, and **the order is load-bearing**. Both `documents` and `doctype_fields` declare `REFERENCES doctype_meta(name) ON DELETE CASCADE`, so dropping the `Stores` doctype row before its documents have moved would silently cascade-delete every one of them. So: add the columns to `Location`, move the data, and only then remove the doctype — with the removal **guarded** on `NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM documents WHERE doctype = 'Stores')`. A partial migration therefore leaves the doctype standing (visible, fixable) rather than taking the data with it.
  - **The data move is an `UPDATE`, not an `INSERT` + `DELETE`.** `documents.id` is the table's primary key and so is unique across *all* doctypes in the schema — which means a `Stores` row's id cannot already be taken by a `Location`, no id remapping is possible or needed, and re-pointing `doctype` in place preserves `created_by`/`created_at` and the row's history. The four fieldnames were kept byte-identical to the `Stores` ones specifically so not a single key inside a `data` blob needed rewriting. `type` (mandatory on Location) is set to `Store` via `COALESCE`, so a record that somehow already had one keeps it.
  - The new `Location` fields are all optional, so **every one of the 103 existing Location records stays valid** — `ValidateDocument` only enforces mandatory fields. `manager` is labelled "Manager" rather than Stores' "Store Manager" because a Location may be a Warehouse or the HO; the fieldname is unchanged, so no stored data moves.
  - Frontend: the `menu-stores` sidebar entry, its click handler and its `MENU_PERMISSION_MAP` row are gone, and four stale comment references to `Stores` were corrected so nobody follows a dead pointer. Both removal sites carry a "do not restore this" comment.
  - Docs: USER_SOP **§21 was repurposed from "Stores" to "Locations"** rather than deleted, so the section number stays stable and the module index still resolves; it now documents creating a Location properly and carries a note for anyone following an older printout. USER_GUIDE §3/§8/§13 and UAT_CHECKLIST §1/§17 updated — **the UAT check is now the *absence* of Stores**, so an older build fails it rather than quietly passing. `PERMISSION_MATRIX.md` regenerated (its `Stores` row is gone; `-Check` exits 0).
  - **Verified**: the dev DB held **zero** `Stores` documents, so applying the migration there exercised only the "nothing to move" path. The move itself was therefore tested separately against a real Postgres — a throwaway program built a scratch schema with the same FK/CASCADE declarations, seeded a `Stores` doctype with documents (including one that already had a `type`, plus a pre-existing `Location` so the id-uniqueness assumption was actually present), ran the real migration file against it and asserted the outcome: **15/15**, covering all four fields surviving the move, the pre-existing Location untouched, cascade cleanup of fields/grants, idempotence on re-run, and — the important one — **the guard refusing to cascade-delete an unmoved document**. Scratch schema and program removed afterwards. Plus 8 live browser checks: no `Stores` in the sidebar or the Setup list, the Stock flyout intact at 11 entries, and the Location list showing the four folded-in columns over its existing records. - [x] **35.3.7** [carried out of R1] Per-line reservation attribution + an expiry sweeper — **built 2026-08-12.** Additive `db/migrations_stage35_3_7_reservation_attribution.sql` adds nullable `order_id`/`line_id` plus three partial indexes; `CreateReservation` takes a variadic `ReservationAttribution` so the four order paths attribute their rows while cart holds, the manual reservation API and the load-test harness keep writing honestly unattributed ones. `releaseLineReservation` now releases **this line's** row, falling back to the old (sku, location, quantity) heuristic only for pre-migration rows. The OMS console's reservation panel matches by `order_id` first and flags each row `attributed` so the screen no longer presents an approximation as fact.
  - **The sweeper deliberately does not expire an order's reservation on time alone**, and that is the whole safety argument. `inventory.reservation_ttl_seconds` is a *cart-hold* TTL; applying it to a confirmed order would release stock out from under a live order the moment it sat in a queue longer than the TTL — a far worse bug than the leak being fixed. So: an **unattributed** hold is released when `expires_at` passes; an **attributed** one is released only when its line is gone, deleted or no longer in a stock-holding status (`Reserved`/`Allocated`/`Picking`/`Picked`/`Packed`). One statement, one snapshot, `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`, batched at 500 per tick, `StartReservationSweeper(ctx, 5m)`. A side benefit: it also repairs reservations orphaned by any pre-35.3.7 path that cancelled a line without releasing.
  - **Verified**: new `engines/reservation_sweeper_test.go` asserts the negative case first (a live line's reservation must survive a sweep even 48h past its nominal expiry), plus the cancelled-line release, the expired-hold release, availability arithmetic, sweep idempotence, and that releasing by line id takes the line's own row rather than an older lookalike. The test asserts per-SKU rather than on the sweep's global counts — the sweep is schema-wide by design and this suite shares one database, so global counts are not any one test's to own.
  - **Proven on real accumulated data 2026-08-13**, once the UTF-8 conversion above let the migration apply to `custom_erp`: that database held **5,395 sweepable reservations** against a total of 5,419 — i.e. 99.6% of every reservation in it was holding stock for a line that no longer wanted it. Drained to 0, with `inventory_availability.reserved < 0` still empty afterwards. **This also caught a wrong assumption in the test itself**: the sweep is batched at 500 rows per call (deliberately — one long transaction against a backlog would hold locks the live order path needs), so a single call on a real database never reaches a freshly-inserted fixture. The test now drains in a bounded loop, which is what the 5-minute worker does over successive ticks; it fails rather than hangs if the sweep ever stops converging.

### INV › Costing & valuation

- [x] **37.3** Costing & valuation, incl. **landed cost allocation** — **built 2026-09-01.** Pre-build audit found this codebase had NO costing method anywhere: `StockLedgerEntry`/`bin_stock`/`inventory_availability` track quantity only, POS checkout's "COGS" used whatever `cost_price` the client's cart JSON sent (never verified), and `PostGRNFinanceBooking` (the intended Dr 1200/Cr 2100 GRN-receipt posting) was dead code with zero callers — meaning **nothing had ever credited 2100 GRN Suspense**, while `PayVendorInvoice`'s debit to it has been running the whole time, driving the account further into an incorrect balance on every vendor payment this system has ever posted. This closes both gaps.
  - [x] **37.3.1** Single company-wide (not per-location) moving-weighted-average unit cost per item, `item_cost` (`engines/costing.go`) — the Ind AS 2/AS 2 acceptable method, avoiding FIFO/LIFO layer-tracking this codebase has no infrastructure for. Stores CUMULATIVE received qty/value (not a live "remaining pool"): the average only moves on receipt, never on issue, so nothing needed to intercept this codebase's many stock-out paths (sales, transfers, returns, disassembly, wastage...) to stay correct.
  - [x] **37.3.2** Landed cost allocation. New `LandedCostVoucher` doctype (Draft → Applied, one-shot) references a GRN and spreads its charge lines (Freight/Customs/Duty/Insurance/Other) proportionally by each received line's own base value across `item_cost`, posting `Dr 1200 Inventory / Cr 2110 Landed Cost Clearing` (new account).
  - [x] **37.3.3** Real COGS at sale. `ResolveCOGSUnitCostPaise` wired into `FinalizePOSCheckout` (`engines/pos_checkout.go`) — a real recorded moving-average cost wins over the client-submitted `cost_price`; an item with no receipt history yet falls back to the client's own figure unchanged, so a tenant that has never used GRN-based receiving sees byte-identical behaviour to today.
  - [x] **37.3.4** `GetInventoryValuation` (report `inventory-valuation`) — real on-hand qty (`inventory_availability`, summed across locations) × the current moving-average rate, computed fresh at report time rather than tracking a parallel "current pool" that every stock-out path would need to keep in step.
  - [x] **37.3.5** Real GRN → GL posting. `RecordGRNReceiptCosting`, called from `PostGRNReceiptWithQC` (`engines/wms_receiving.go`), resolves each accepted line's ex-GST base cost from the GRN's own PO (reusing `PreviewPurchaseOrder`'s existing GST-aware taxable-amount computation, not re-derived) and posts `Dr 1200 Inventory / Cr 2100 GRN Suspense` — the missing credit side of the 2100 gap above. Best-effort/logged, never unwinding stock that has already posted, the same posture the batch/serial registration loops in that function already take.
  - **Surface/schema**: additive `db/migrations_stage37_3_costing_valuation.sql` (applied to dev only — surgical single-file apply, the same pre-existing unrelated `migrations_stage42_6_labour_billing_depth.sql` still pending, untouched). New `engines/costing.go` + `costing_test.go`, one new handler file (`internal/server/handlers_costing.go`), 2 new routes, 1 new GL account (2110 Landed Cost Clearing), 1 new report. No dependency, no dedicated frontend screen — reachable via the dedicated create/apply endpoints (the `JournalVoucher`/`IntercompanyTransaction` split), the generic DocType form for read/list, and the generic report screen.

- [x] **59.1 Bin stock tracks reality: bin-level reservation and consumption.** Built and verified 2026-10-08.
  - **Schema:** `db/migrations_stage59_1_bin_allocation.sql` adds a new `bin_allocation` table. Each row is one (task, sku, bin, lot, owner) slice of stock a FulfillmentTask has been given. An `Open` row reserves `qty - picked_qty`; the row moves to `Picked` or `Released` and keeps `picked_qty` as the record of what left which bin. `owner_id` is carried now and stays empty until 59.3. The migration is additive only: existing drifted bins are **reported, not corrected** (see the report below).
  - **New engine `engines/wms_bin_allocation.go`:**
    - `ReserveTaskBinStock[Tx]` tops a task up to its unpicked demand through the existing `AllocateFromStock` FIFO/FEFO path.
    - `ConsumeTaskBinStockTx` takes units off the reserved bin, lot and owner rows.
    - `ReleaseTaskBinStockTx` hands back what a task no longer needs.
    - `BinReservedQty` reports how much of a bin is reserved.
    - `BinStockReconciliation` backs the new report `bin-stock-reconciliation` (columns: on hand, in bins, picked-not-dispatched, difference).
  - **Changes to existing code:**
    - **Allocation** (`traceability.go`: `allocateByOrder`/`allocateFEFO`, now querier-aware via `allocateFromStockQ`) subtracts other tasks' Open reservations. Only reservations of **live** tasks count (Pending/Picking/Packed). A crashed, deleted, cancelled or test-debris task can never strand stock.
    - **`GenerateBinPickList`** reserves, then reads the task's own reservation back, so a second call shows the same bins and lines show what is still to pick.
    - **`GenerateWavePickList`** reserves each task oldest-first (keeping the old "older order is not starved" rule) and builds the walk from those reservations.
    - **`ScanPickItem`** is now one transaction under the task's row lock: reserve the task, take one unit off its bin, save. Before this it did an unlocked load-and-save.
    - **`ShortPickLine`** releases that SKU's reservation, then re-reserves from the saved task, in case the same SKU sits on a second line.
    - **`TransitionTaskStatus`:** on Dispatched, units shipped without being scanned leave their bins; Dispatched and Rejected both release whatever is still reserved.
    - **`MoveBinStock`** (Stage 57.9) and **`TransitionBinStockCondition`** refuse to move, or turn non-Good, stock reserved for an open pick.
  - **Lock order:** every path takes the per-(location, sku) advisory lock **before** a `bin_stock` row lock. The move and condition paths had to be changed to match, otherwise a move and a pick on the same bin could deadlock.

    - Dispatch takes off the unscanned units: 8 − 6 = 2 left.
    - A short pick releases stock for the next task; a rejection releases too.
    - The reconciliation report flags an over-stated bin.
    - A binless location is unaffected.
    - 10 concurrent one-unit tasks racing for 5 units get exactly 5 promised (passes on 3 repeated runs).
    - Move and condition change are refused on reserved stock and allowed once the stock is released.
    - Existing pick-list, wave, traceability, A-05, 42.5 and single-owner tests stay green.

Read-only report (`3pl-storage-billing`), no invoice/GL document auto-created. Verified: `TestWMSP2/StorageBillingReport`.
- [x] **47.5 Mixed-owner 3PL isolation across the inventory lifecycle—or enforced de-scope** — closes A-05. **Closed 2026-09-09 by the second of the two closures the item offered: "the system makes the unsupported configuration impossible."** Decision taken by the user on evidence, not preference — the entire development database held **two `bin_stock_owner` rows and both were the A-05 red-team fixture itself** (`OWNER-A-TEST`/`OWNER-B-TEST` in `WH-OWN-TEST`, one at qty 0). No tenant has ever segregated real stock by owner, so building owner-awareness through receive → allocate → pick → pack → ship → adjust → count → bill would have been a multi-session feature for zero users, while the *claim* of isolation stood unproven in the meantime. The claim was the risk; the missing feature was not.
  - [x] **47.5.1** `db/migrations_stage47_5_single_owner_guard.sql` + `engines/wms_single_owner.go`. **The guard is structural, not procedural**: a `warehouse_owner` table whose PRIMARY KEY *is* `location_code`, so a second owner for a warehouse cannot be stored. `AssertSingleOwnerForLocation` is called from `RecordOwnerStock` — the one API in this codebase that can put a second owner in a building — rather than repeated per call site. An **unassigned** warehouse adopts its first owner (so a tenant that never thought about ownership is unaffected; the rule blocks the *second* owner, not the first), and reassignment is refused while the incumbent still holds stock, or the guard would be cosmetic. New setting `wms.stock_ownership_mode` defaults to `single_owner`; `mixed_unsupported` exists so a real 3PL pilot can opt in **knowingly** — it is labelled unsupported because allocation and picking genuinely are owner-blind. New routes `POST /api/v1/wms/owner/assign-warehouse` and `GET /api/v1/wms/owner/mixed-locations`.
    **The migration deliberately does not "fix" pre-existing mixed data.** It backfills `warehouse_owner` only for locations already holding exactly one owner, and for genuinely mixed ones it `RAISE WARNING`s and leaves them alone. Aborting would block every later migration on such a database; silently picking a winner would re-attribute somebody's stock without being asked. Naming them is the only honest option, and `ListMixedOwnerLocations` surfaces the same list through the API. **Verified on the dev DB: it correctly detected `WH-OWN-TEST`, refused to guess, and warned.** This matters because production could not be inspected from here — the migration is safe there regardless of what it finds.
    **Claim removed** from `docs/ERP_BLUEPRINT.md`: "multi-owner (3PL) stock segregation and billing" → single-owner-per-warehouse attribution, with mixed-owner isolation explicitly *not* claimed.
  - [x] **47.5.2–47.5.6** — **not built, by decision.** These are the "if supported" branch (owner mandatory through every transition, owner on `SalesOrder`/allocation demand, removal of every owner-agnostic fallback in sourcing/availability/wave/picking, FK+uniqueness constraints, owner reconciliation with an exception queue, adversarial two-owner lifecycle). They remain the real thing if a 3PL pilot ever signs; the guard above is what makes their absence safe rather than merely undocumented.

It also checks the refusal is a coded `ValidationError` naming the incumbent owner, that nothing partial was written, and that only one owner ends up at the location. `engines/wms_single_owner_test.go` covers the guard's own behaviour: first-owner adoption, same-owner top-ups allowed, second owner refused, takeover-while-stocked refused, the unsupported mode really disabling the guard, and mixed locations being reported once it does.
    **One pre-existing test needed updating for a real reason:** Stage 42.5.5's `MultiOwnerStockSegregation` sub-test asserts one bin holding two owners — precisely the configuration now guarded. It opts into `mixed_unsupported` explicitly, which is what a real 3PL pilot would also have to do; its billing maths is unchanged and still covered.

### OMS › Allocation & fulfilment

- [x] **6.1** Location-scoped reservations; rule-driven picking + re-routing on reject.
- [x] **13.6 Fulfillment/reservation workbench** — status-driven task actions.
  - **Bug fixed**: the location filter only checked a field literally named `location`; `FulfillmentTask` actually stores `location_code` — non-admins got zero results. Fixed with a `COALESCE`.
- [x] **26.12.2** Allocation/Sourcing — built and live-verified 2026-07-25. New `engines.ResolveAllocationPlan` (`engines/sourcing.go`) runs every Active `AllocationRule` (26.12.9) scoped to a channel (or the global blank-channel rules) in ascending-priority order, trying each rule's strategy until one produces a usable plan — the first to succeed wins. Five strategies beyond the pre-existing default: **Highest ATS** (the old `FindBestFulfillmentNode` logic, re-expressed over a new shared `qualifyingLocations` scan so all single-location strategies share one implementation instead of repeating it), **Nearest Pincode** (`abs(orderPincode−locationPincode)`, per the design note's own validated proxy shape — needed a new additive `pincode` field on the Location master, `db/migrations_stage26_12_2_allocation_sourcing.sql`, since none existed), **Lowest Workload** (fewest open `FulfillmentTask` rows, status not Dispatched/Rejected), **Oldest Stock** (earliest `inventory_availability.updated_at` among a location's relevant SKU rows — a documented proxy, same "proxy not a real port" caveat the design note gives Nearest Pincode, since no per-batch received-date exists), and **Split Shipment** (the only strategy allowed to spread lines across more than one location — each line sourced independently by its own highest-ATS location; every other strategy requires one location to cover every line or produces no plan at all, so split-shipment only ever happens when a rule explicitly authorizes it). A **Manual** strategy always fails to produce a plan and stops the search immediately (routes to a human, not "skip me") — configure it as the lowest-priority catch-all. Falls back to the exact pre-26.12.2 Highest-ATS/HO-fallback behavior when a tenant has configured zero `AllocationRule` rows at all (same "usable before any admin config" precedent as `isCancellationBlocked`); once at least one rule *is* configured, exhausting every rule without a plan is the **allocation-exception** case — `CreateSalesOrder`/`ReleaseOrderHold` (`engines/orders.go`) hold the order with a new `HoldAllocationFailed` (`ALLOCATION_FAILED`) code instead of erroring, mirroring `validateOrderChain`'s existing "return a routable code, don't reject" contract. No new table for the "exception queue" the checklist item calls for — the resulting On-Hold `SalesOrder` rows filtered by `hold_reason` *are* the queue, same "reuse the doctype list view" precedent 26.12.1's hold routing and 26.12.7's planned dashboard both use. `CreateSalesOrder`/`ReleaseOrderHold` were also changed to reserve **per line** (`plan.LineLocations[i]`) instead of one shared location for the whole order — the schema already supported this (`SalesOrderLine.location_code` is per-line), it just wasn't being used; `ReleaseOrderHold` now also correctly scopes re-allocation to only the lines still `Pending` rather than re-sourcing already-Reserved/Dispatched lines too (a small pre-existing correctness gap fixed as a side effect of the per-line rework, not separately scoped). Reallocation-on-reject (`fulfillment.go`'s `TransitionTaskStatus`, the design note's other §12 callout) was deliberately left untouched — its existing single DB transaction already gives it the "rollback to the old reservation on failure" property the design note asks for (a release-then-reserve sequence inside one `tx.Commit()`/`defer tx.Rollback()` boundary already rolls back both halves atomically on any failure), so there was no real gap to close there. **Verified**: new `TestEngines/AllocationSourcing` subtest — all 5 non-default strategies exercised directly via `ResolveAllocationPlan` (Nearest Pincode, Lowest Workload, Oldest Stock, and a combined Split-Shipment-plus-priority-fallthrough case where a higher-priority Highest-ATS rule correctly fails first), plus a full `CreateSalesOrder` HTTP-shaped call proving a Manual rule holds a genuinely-in-stock order with `ALLOCATION_FAILED` — `go test ./... -p 1` green (whole suite, no new failures). Live-verified over real HTTP against the dev DB (throwaway port 8237, scratch HR/Admin token minted via a repo-internal `cmd/` program, deleted after): seeded two real `Location` docs with different pincodes, created a `SalesOrder` through the real `POST /api/v1/orders` endpoint, confirmed it reserved at the nearer location and `inventory_availability.reserved` moved correctly; then seeded a channel-scoped Manual rule and confirmed a second real order on that channel went On Hold with `ALLOCATION_FAILED` despite the SKU being fully in stock. All fixtures (including one auto-created PIM profile side effect of creating a test Item) removed after. `go build`/`go vet` clean.
- [x] **26.12.3** Fulfillment Pick/Pack — built and live-verified 2026-07-25. New `engines/fulfillment_pickpack.go` (deliberately a separate file from `fulfillment.go`'s existing `CreateFulfillmentTasks`/`TransitionTaskStatus`, which are untouched — additive, not a rewrite) layers distinct scan-validated Pick and Pack stages on top of a `FulfillmentTask`'s existing `items` array via three new per-line fields (`picked_qty`/`packed_qty`/`short_qty`, additive JSON keys — no schema/table change). `ScanPickItem`/`ScanPackItem` resolve a scanned barcode (falling back to SKU/code on a miss, same degrade-gracefully convention as the 26.3.1 GRN barcode preview) and match it to the *first* task line for that SKU still short of its target — a scan for a product not on the task, or a line already fully picked/packed, is rejected naming the actual product involved (§12), not a bare "invalid scan". The blueprint's hard rule that packed quantity can never exceed picked quantity (§6) falls directly out of `ScanPackItem`'s own match condition (`packed_qty < picked_qty`) rather than being separately enforced. `ShortPickLine` marks a line's entire remaining shortfall as short in one action (§12: "no partial-short-then-more-picking modeled"), requiring a mandatory, category-matched `ReasonCode` — reused the exact Stage 26.12.1 Hold/Cancel convention, extending `ReasonCode.category`'s Select options with a new "Short Pick" value (`db/migrations_stage26_12_3_pick_pack.sql`, additive) rather than a bespoke reason field. `CompletePackTask` is the explicit, blockable completion action (§12: "any exact-qty mismatch, not just a shortfall") — hard-blocks unless *every* line has both fully resolved its pick (picked_qty+short_qty == qty) and packed exactly what was picked (packed_qty == picked_qty), only then moving the task to `Packed`. Task status otherwise stays within the FulfillmentTask doctype's own pre-existing Select vocabulary (`Pending,Picking,Packed,Dispatched,Rejected`, `db/migration.sql` — already anticipated exactly this granularity, so no status-list migration was needed): first pick or short-pick action flips `Pending`→`Picking`, and both the pick and pack stages live under `Picking` until `CompletePackTask` explicitly sets `Packed`. **Deliberately cross-checked `engines/wms.go` first per the design note's own warning, and deliberately layered alongside it rather than merging**: `GenerateBinPickList` answers "which bin do I walk to for this SKU" (a `bin_stock`-backed, warehouse-internal concern that doesn't apply to every FulfillmentTask location); this item answers "did the picker/packer actually gather and box the right units" against the task's own line items — orthogonal concerns, forcing them together would have been exactly the kind of duplication the design note flags. **Deliberately out of scope**: auto-generating an invoice from a completed pack task (the retired prototype did this, §12 "worth preserving" note) — this repo's Order Engine has no Order→Shipment→Invoice wiring yet for `SalesOrder` to generate one from; revisit once 26.12.4/26.12.5 add that chain. New endpoints (`internal/server/handlers_wms.go`, `routes.go`): `POST /api/v1/wms/pick-scan`, `.../pack-scan`, `.../short-pick`, `.../pack-complete`, same `moduleGate("wms",...)` and role-open convention as the sibling putaway/pick-list/condition-transition floor-ops routes. **Verified**: new `TestEngines/PickPack` subtest — unknown-scan rejection, not-part-of-this-task rejection naming the real product, partial pick, both distinct `CompletePackTask` block reasons exercised separately (unresolved pick shortfall vs. packed≠picked), short-pick's mandatory-reason-code enforcement, duplicate-scan rejection after a line is fully picked+short-picked, packing structurally capped at picked_qty, and a scan rejected once the task is Packed — `go test ./... -p 1` green, whole suite, no new failures. Live-verified over real HTTP against the dev DB (throwaway port 8241): a real seeded task's full pick→(blocked early completion)→short-pick→pack→complete lifecycle through the real endpoints, confirmed the final document's `picked_qty`/`short_qty`/`packed_qty`/`status` all landed exactly as expected. All fixtures removed after. `go build`/`go vet` clean.

### OMS › Shipping & couriers

- [x] **35.4** Shipping package, invoice generation from pack, gate pass, credit note — **built 2026-08-15.** New `engines/shipping_package.go` + `pack_invoice.go` + `gate_pass.go` + `cancellation_credit_note.go`, `internal/server/handlers_shipping_package.go`, 12 routes, additive `db/migrations_stage35_4_shipping_package.sql` (applied).
  - **Why the entity had to exist first.** The chain ran FulfillmentTask → LogisticsBooking, which assumes one task ships as exactly one parcel — false the moment a packer needs two boxes — and left nothing to hang an invoice off. That is the same reason 26.12.3 gave for deferring invoice-from-pack ("nothing real to generate the invoice from"); R1 built the order chain and 35.4.1 built the pack object, so the reason has expired.
  - [x] **35.4.1** `ShippingPackage` (Draft → Invoiced → Shipped, Cancelled as the exit; only Draft is mutable). Created from a **Packed** task using `packed_qty`, not `qty` — a short-picked line ships short, and invoicing the ordered quantity for a parcel that does not contain it is the most expensive mistake available here. Creation is idempotent on the task (the pack screen's "done" is exactly the button an operator double-taps). Split refuses two things rather than clamping: moving *every* unit out (that is a rename, and leaves an empty package that still looks shippable) and moving more than a line holds; duplicate SKU rows in one split request are summed **before** validation, or 5+5 passes against a holding of 8. Both halves are written in one transaction, and the source's weight/dimensions are cleared because they now describe neither box.
  - [x] **35.4.2** Invoice from a completed pack — closes 26.12.3's deferral. Invoices **the package, not the order**, so a split order's two parcels each carry their own correct tax document. Prices come from the order's own `SalesOrderLine.unit_price`, never from today's item master — re-reading `sale_price` would silently re-price a shipment mid-flight. Produces a **Draft**; posting stays an explicit finance action, matching the split `CreateSalesInvoiceFromOrder` already keeps.
    - **A real defect fell out of this, and it is fixed in the new code only.** The shared `ComputeGSTForLinesMode` is not internally consistent to the paisa: CGST and SGST are each `round2(lineTax/2)` per line and then summed, so a plain two-line 18% order totalling 900 produced **CGST+SGST = 137.30 against its own TotalTax of 137.28**, and `TaxableAmount` accumulates unrounded (stored as `762.7118644067798`). New `reconcileInvoiceAmounts` makes the document add up in both directions — components sum to the tax total exactly (the second absorbs the half-paisa, the `ConvertPostingToFunctional` technique), and taxable is derived as total − non-taxable − tax so exempt/nil/zero-rated turnover stays **out** of the filed GSTR-3B 3.1(a) figure while still reconciling. Deliberately **not** applied to the shared engine: its contract is that every existing sale-side caller stays byte-identical, and POS checkout is one of them.
    - **Also load-bearing**: `CreateSalesInvoiceFromOrder`'s existence check was widened from its own `INV-<orderID>` to *any* invoice with that `sales_order_id`. Without it, the handover cascade calls it on the Shipped transition and **every package-invoiced order would be invoiced a second time, in full**.
  - [x] **35.4.3** Invoice → label → manifest ordering enforced (Uniware's hard rule: no label before invoice). A label is what authorises a parcel to move, so this refuses rather than warns. The manifest half is a `WHERE` clause, not a post-filter, so an unlabelled parcel is never grouped and then silently dropped — it simply waits for the next manifest; the "nothing to ship" and "everything is waiting on a label" cases are now distinguished in the message, because they send an operator to completely different places. **The rule binds only a booking that has a package**: `CreateLogisticsBooking` gained a variadic package id (all six call sites unchanged, the 37.1.2 `PostingOptions` precedent) and auto-links its task's package when none is given — otherwise the guard would only apply to callers who already knew about packages, which is exactly the set that does not need guarding. A pre-35.4 or manual booking labels exactly as it did.
  - [x] **35.4.4** `GatePass` (Draft → Issued → Completed, Discarded as the exit) — create/update/issue/complete/discard/search. Hangs off the **Manifest**, not a package: a pass is issued per vehicle and a vehicle carries a manifest's worth of parcels. Carrier/location/count are taken **from** the manifest rather than trusted from the caller — the gate desk is transcribing, and a pass whose count disagrees with the manifest it references is worse than no pass at all. A vehicle number is required at *issue*, not at creation: raising the pass is paperwork, issuing it is the moment something departs, and a departure record with no vehicle cannot be reconciled later. Every transition goes through Stage 29.8's rule map (the 35.3.6 consolidation).
  - [x] **35.4.5** Credit note on cancellation-after-invoice. `CreditNote`/`PostCreditNote` already existed (Stage 20c) and are reused, not re-implemented; this works out which invoices a cancellation affects. **A Draft invoice is voided, not credited** — nothing was posted, recognised or declared, so crediting it would reverse a transaction that never happened. Wired into `CancelOrder` (variadic `actor`, four call sites unchanged) after the order is durably Cancelled, so a failure leaves the reversal visibly outstanding rather than an order credited while still live. Cancelling also voids any non-shipped package on the order — a Draft package left behind still looks bookable, and a booking against it would ship goods for an order nobody will pay for.
  - **Verified**: `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...` clean and `go test ./... -p 1` fully green, including 12 new tests in `engines/shipping_package_test.go` (packed-vs-ordered quantity, idempotent creation, all four split refusals plus conservation, exact invoice reconciliation in both directions, the interstate override, both ordering refusals **and** the legacy-booking exemption, the double-invoice guard, the credit-note draft/posted/idempotent cases, and the gate-pass lifecycle). Then the whole chain over HTTP on a throwaway server (port 8093, stopped and released, fixtures removed): package → split (3+1=4, lineage recorded) → label refused → manifest refused → invoice (`635.59 + 114.41 = 750.00`, CGST `57.21` + SGST `57.20` = `114.41`) → label → manifest → gate pass (issue refused with no vehicle) → handover → package `Shipped` → credit note, idempotent on the second call.
  - **Test-suite note worth keeping**: `db.InitDB` reassigns the global pool without closing the previous one, so every call leaks up to `dbMaxIdleConns` for `ConnMaxIdleTime`. The package convention is one `InitDB` per test, which was already close enough to Postgres's `max_connections` that adding this file tipped `go test ./... -p 1` into `sorry, too many clients already` — a connection ceiling, not a logic failure. This file reuses a live pool (`spInitDB`); the other files' convention was left alone.
  - **Known limitation, stated rather than hidden**: `SalesOrder` has no state field (only free-text `shipping_address`), so inter-state cannot be reliably derived. Parsing the address would be wrong often enough to be worse than useless *on a tax document*, so the resolution order is explicit override → the order's `shipping_state`/`custom_shipping_state` if present → **default intra-state**, and the basis used is recorded on the invoice as `gst_basis` rather than left for an auditor to guess. A real `shipping_state` on SalesOrder is the fix, and belongs with 35.6's channel adapters, which are where the value would actually come from.

Extended `CreateLogisticsBooking` (`engines/marketplace.go`) from a bare manual carrier/tracking/charge record (hardcoded `status="Shipped"` at creation, before anything had actually shipped) into a real Shipment engine: **serviceability check** — a new `CourierServiceArea` master (Active rows with a `pincode_prefix`/blank-means-everywhere/`priority`, config-table stand-in for a "Courier Provider connector") backs `CheckCourierServiceability`, which a blank `carrier` auto-selects the top-priority match from, and an explicit `carrier` is validated against unless zero rows are configured yet (same "usable before any admin config" precedent `isCancellationBlocked`/`ResolveAllocationPlan` already use). **AWB assignment** — a locally-generated placeholder AWB number (real courier API deliberately out of scope, per this item's own "internal engine first, credentials-gated API later" note, same pattern as 26.2.1-26.2.5), status now starts at `AWB Assigned`. **Manifest grouping** — new `Manifest` doctype; `GenerateManifest(courier, location)` groups every `AWB Assigned` booking whose linked `FulfillmentTask` (`fulfillment_task_id`, additive optional field) is at that location. **Handover cascade** (design note §12's concrete split-shipment-aware closure rule) — `HandoverManifest` flips every grouped booking to `Handed Over`, dispatches its `FulfillmentTask` (reusing `TransitionTaskStatus` rather than duplicating its stock-deduction logic — the CLAUDE.md choke-point principle), then evaluates each affected `SalesOrder`: `Shipped` only once *every* `FulfillmentTask` under that order code has reached `Dispatched`, otherwise `Partially Fulfilled`. New intermediate `ReturnRequest` status `Pickup Scheduled`, and `ReceiveReturnRequest` now accepts a manual receive from it too (the operator may physically have the parcel before the webhook catches up).
  - [x] **35.9.2** Exchange / alternate item. `ApplyReturnQC` gained an optional trailing `exchangeFor` (originalSKU → exchangeSKU) map — variadic, so every existing call site is unchanged. An exchanged line's returned stock still lands in its disposition's bucket exactly as before, but the exchange SKU's stock is deducted from the **same** `return_location`, in the **same transaction** (reusing `engines/bundles.go`'s own ATS-check-then-`StockLedgerEntry` shape), so a shortage on the exchange side rolls back the whole QC call — nothing is received without its replacement being available, and nothing is issued without the original actually coming back. That line is excluded from the refund total. **Deliberately same-value-only**: no Item-master cost/price field exists to price a different-value swap correctly (same gap as 35.8's own note), so a different-value exchange is refused with a message pointing at return + new sale instead; the exchange leg's own COGS entry reuses the returned line's own cost basis (correct for the common same-family size/colour swap this targets).

An explicit `return_location` always wins unchanged. A Customer Return's original order is a POSCart/SalesInvoice (`resolveOriginalSale`), neither of which carries a shipping address, so that path has no pincode to route from and keeps requiring an explicit location, same as before this stage.

All of 35.9's three sub-items are built and tested at the API layer; a full Returns management screen (the natural home for a Schedule Reverse Pickup button and an exchange-SKU picker in the QC step) is a separate, larger undertaking not attempted here — out of this item's own "3 sub-items" scope.
- [x] **26.12.5** Returns/RTO/QC/Refund — built and live-verified 2026-07-25. New `engines/returns.go` (deliberately separate from `fulfillment.go`'s `ProcessReturnAnywhere`, left untouched — that stays the POS in-store walk-in-return path; this is the OMS/e-commerce path) adds new `ReturnRequest`/`RefundRequest` Transaction doctypes (`db/migrations_stage26_12_5_returns_rto_qc_refund.sql`, module_key `oms`) and a request/approval-gated state machine: `CreateReturnRequest` (Requested) → `ApproveReturnRequest`/`RejectReturnRequest` (mandatory 'Return'-category `ReasonCode`, 26.12.9) → `ReceiveReturnRequest` (Received) → `ApplyReturnQC` (per-SKU disposition → QC Complete/Closed). Two `request_type`s share one workflow: **Customer Return** (reuses `resolveOriginalSale`'s SALESR-0129/0130/0131 window/qty checks plus a new `sumPriorReturnRequests` pool so a customer can't over-return by mixing the instant POS path and this one against the same original order) and **RTO** (requires the linked `LogisticsBooking`, 26.12.4, to already be `RecordRTO`'d, and is idempotent on `booking_id`). **QC disposition buckets** (Sellable/Damaged/Repairable/Missing/Wrong-Item/Rejected) — an explicit documented decision (design note §12's "decide explicitly, don't inherit silently"): Sellable/Damaged/Repairable all physically receive stock (into `available`/`damaged`/`qc_hold` respectively, 26.12.6's buckets) and refund in full; Missing/Wrong-Item/Rejected receive nothing and refund nothing — **per-line**, not "one QC-failed line holds the whole refund" like the retired prototype. Refund amount is always resolved from the **original order line's price** (POSCart's own stored `sale_price` for a Customer Return, `SalesOrderLine.unit_price` for an RTO), never from any return-time input — the create/QC APIs don't even accept a price field. **Refund distinct from the immediate GL post**: the inventory/COGS-side reversal posts in `ApplyReturnQC` when stock is actually received; the revenue-side reversal (debit Sales Revenue/credit Cash-Bank) only posts in a separate `ProcessRefundRequest`, gated behind its own `RefundRequest` Pending→Approved→Processed (or Rejected) lifecycle. ### OMS › OMS reports & SLAs

- [x] **SLA breach detection never fired.** `documents.created_at` is a bare `TIMESTAMP` holding the DB server's *local* wall clock, but `lib/pq` hands it back tagged UTC — so `GetSLABreaches`' `time.Since(created_at)` (`engines/optimization.go`) reported every open task as **330 minutes in the future** on this Asia/Calcutta deployment, and `elapsed > threshold` was false for anything younger than 5.5h + the threshold. Elapsed time is now computed in SQL (`NOW() - created_at`), which is correct in any time zone. Live proof: the console's SLA tile reads **230** where it would previously have read 0. The `TestEngines/AdvancedOptimizationAndForecasting` fixture was inserting `time.Now().UTC()`, a frame nothing else in the app writes — it only ever agreed with the buggy reader, and is now written the way real rows are.
- [x] **26.12.7** Exception/reconciliation dashboard — built and live-verified 2026-07-25. Rather than a new dashboard-widget mechanism, both pieces are registered as ordinary `ReportDefinition` catalog entries (`engines/oms_reports.go`), reusing the Stage 20 Track B.4 "register a function, not a new endpoint" framework — reachable via the existing `GET /api/v1/reports/catalog`/`run/{id}` with no new routes needed. **`oms-exception-queue`**: reads `integration_event_outbox`/`integration_event_log` (`engines/outbox.go`) directly for `Failed` events or `Pending` ones stuck past a 30-minute staleness window — no new retry/DLQ mechanism, matching the checklist item's own "just OMS-scoped visibility" scope (retry itself already exists via `RetryIntegrationEvent`). **`oms-reconciliation-variance`**: flags a `Shipped`/`Delivered` `SalesOrder` whose linked `LogisticsBooking`(s) (26.12.4) status doesn't actually support that claim yet (or has none at all) — a real "OMS vs courier" check over this repo's own stored data, not a synthetic channel feed. **Verified**: `TestEngines/ReturnsRTOQCRefund` exercises both report queries directly (a seeded `Failed` outbox event; a `SalesOrder` forced to `Shipped` with only an `RTO` booking) — `go test ./... -p 1` green. Live-verified over real HTTP: confirmed both ids appear in the live `/api/v1/reports/catalog` under category `OMS`.
- [x] **26.12.8** OMS reports — built and live-verified 2026-07-25. Seven new `ReportDefinition` entries (`engines/oms_reports.go`), same catalog framework as 26.12.7, category `OMS`. **Order Aging**/**Return Aging** reuse the exact `PayablesAgeingBucket` shape and 0-30/31-60/61-90/90+ bucket boundaries as the existing Payables/Receivables Ageing reports (Stage 20.33), with a matched drill-down; Return Aging deliberately omits an amount column (a return's refund total isn't known until QC completes). **SLA Breach** wraps the pre-existing `GetSLABreaches` (Stage 17.10, `engines/optimization.go`) as a catalog entry with a `threshold_minutes` param, rather than a new SLA engine, per the checklist's own "reuses Stage 17.10's SLA-breach monitor pattern" instruction. **Allocation Pending** lists `SalesOrder` rows On Hold with 26.12.2's `HoldAllocationFailed` code — the same "the hold-reason-filtered list view IS the queue" precedent 26.12.2's own build note established. **Stock Mismatch** flags every SKU/location where 26.12.6's shared `computeATS` formula is negative (over-committed past what's physically available) — a real correctness signal, not a Stock Ledger reconciliation (26.10.1's ledger wiring isn't built yet). **Reserved Stock** is a direct `inventory_availability` read for every `reserved > 0` row. **Courier Performance** aggregates `LogisticsBooking` (26.12.4) by carrier: shipment volume, delivered/RTO counts and rate, and an average Handed-Over-to-Delivered turnaround proxied from each booking's own `created_at`/`updated_at` (no separate per-status-change timestamp history exists yet). **Verified**: `TestEngines/ReturnsRTOQCRefund` exercises all 7 (a backdated `FulfillmentTask` for SLA Breach, a seeded On-Hold order for Allocation Pending, an artificially over-reserved SKU for Stock Mismatch, the RTO fixture's own `LogisticsBooking` for Courier Performance, etc.) — `go test ./... -p 1` green. One real environment quirk found+worked around during test-writing: this dev Postgres session's naive `timestamp without time zone` columns round-trip through lib/pq several hours off from Go's `time.Now()` (a pre-existing characteristic of every `created_at`-based age calculation in this codebase, not introduced here) — the SLA Breach test fixture backdates by 25 hours rather than a small margin so the assertion isn't swallowed by that skew. Live-verified over real HTTP: `courier-performance` and `return-aging` both confirmed returning correct real data against live fixtures (a real RTO showed up at 100% RTO rate for its carrier).

New engine `engines/pos_quote.go` (`ResolvePOSQuote`) is now the only thing that decides what a line costs; `db/migrations_stage47_2_server_authoritative_pricing.sql` adds `Item.sale_price`/`mrp`/`standard_cost`, `Customer.price_list_code`, and the `POSPriceOverride`/`POSCostingGap` evidence doctypes.
  - [x] **47.2.1** `ResolvePOSQuote` takes item/location/customer/channel/qty/date/currency/tax-basis/coupons and returns a quote whose `quote_version` is an HMAC digest of its own priced content, keyed with the server signing secret — both the rule version and the tamper-evident identity, in one field. Price precedence: approved `POSPriceOverride` → `Customer.price_list_code` → `pos.default_price_list` → `Item.sale_price` → `Item.mrp`. Reuses Stage 37.6.4's `ResolvePriceForSKU`, which had **no production caller at all** before this stage. New `POST /api/v1/pos/quote`.
