Consumed by the sale it priced, so a replayed cart cannot inherit it. **The A-02 bypass itself is closed by the gate now keying on `max(client discount_pct, quote.ManualDiscountPct)`** — the server-measured deviation from master price — so declaring a discount honestly and hiding it in the unit price produce the identical requirement. A crash between any two left a sale genuinely half-posted, and a retry under a **new** cart number sailed past the guard entirely.
  - [x] **47.3.1** `engines/command_idempotency.go` + `tenant_default.command_idempotency`. Claimed before any mutation (the INSERT is the lock), completed **inside the sale's own transaction** — which is what makes taking over an expired lease provably safe rather than a gamble: an abandoned InProgress claim proves nothing was committed. Outcomes: acquired / replay (original response returned verbatim, INT-0222 semantics) / in-progress / payload-mismatch (409) / retry-after-failure. Key namespaced by user + command. When the client supplies its own key, `cart_number` is excluded from the request digest, so a retry that mints a fresh cart number is recognised as the same command — the exact gap the cart-row guard had. Settled claims age out after 7 days on the reservation sweeper's existing tick (no second worker).
  - [x] **47.3.2** `FinalizePOSCheckout` is now ONE transaction: cart row locked `FOR UPDATE`, availability decrement, loyalty burn, revenue/COGS, GST, exempt reclass, cart → Paid, override consumption, idempotency completion and the **outbox event** all commit together. Required splitting six engines into `…Tx` forms (`PostDoubleEntryTx`, `PostSalesFinanceBookingTx`, `PostSalesGSTBookingTx`, `PostExemptSalesReclassTx`, `PostInventoryLedgerWithVoucherTx`, `RedeemLoyaltyPointsTx`); every existing caller keeps the original function, now a wrapper that opens and commits a transaction. Deliberately still post-commit, with reasons recorded in the code: stock-ledger rows (append-only + idempotency-keyed), loyalty earn, offline-sync variance, costing gaps — all additive records that must never undo a completed sale.
  - [x] **47.3.3** `engines/pos_payment.go` — `Initiated → Authorized → Posted` plus `Failed`/`Voided`, as one `paymentStateTransitions` map so no two call sites can disagree. `authorize_only` on `/checkout` reserves stock and stops; `POST /api/v1/pos/payment/confirm` (provider reference doubles as the provider idempotency handle) and `/void` finish it. **No DB transaction is held across the network** — that is the whole reason the posting waits for the authorization instead of racing it. Reservation expiry needed no new mechanism: Stage 35.3.7's sweeper already reclaims a TTL'd hold.
  - [x] **47.3.4** Deterministic lock order (cart row → availability rows sorted by SKU → loyalty ledger), applied in `PostInventoryLedgerWithVoucherTx` and mirrored by `AuthorizePOSSale`'s reservation order. New `InsufficientStockError` type + `IsRetryableDBConflict` so a **business shortage** (INVENT-0101, 422) and a **retryable serialization/deadlock conflict** (409, "nothing was charged, try again") are different answers — reporting either as the other tells the cashier a lie about their own inventory.
  - [x] **47.3.5** `internal/server/pos_atomic_checkout_stage47_3_test.go` — clean sale reconciles; a failure injected after the stock decrement leaves availability untouched and posts nothing (and retrying compounds nothing); 100 identical retries under one key post exactly one sale (the per-session 60/min rate limiter is counted as a refusal rather than a failure, documented in the test); 8 concurrent tills against 10 units sell exactly what stock allows, with no negative availability and no 500s; key reuse with a different payload is refused; authorize → void releases the hold and posts nothing; 5 concurrent confirms of one authorization post exactly one sale. **The A-03 red-team test now passes and was promoted out of the build tag**, with its sanity check rewritten — it used to *require* availability to have dropped after a failed attempt, because that was the bug it was freezing.
  - [x] **47.3.6** `engines/pos_sale_reconciliation.go` + the `pos-sale-reconciliation` report (Finance). One row per sale comparing cart qty/value against stock ledger, revenue, COGS, tax, tender and loyalty, plus whether the outbox event exists, with a verdict. Deliberately independent reads rather than a join (a join lets one missing side hide another) and deliberately reports **Balanced** rather than only exceptions, so an empty exception list can be told apart from a report that never ran. Used by the 47.3.5 tests as the shared definition of "balanced", so a test cannot pass while the operator's own report calls the same sale broken.

### POS › Offline sales & sync

- [x] **24.36** Offline POS Idempotency/traceability risk — **DONE**, with an honestly-scoped residual limit. Root cause: the offline queue lived only in `localStorage`, so a gap between what was queued and what synced left zero server-side trace. Added a best-effort heartbeat (`sendOfflineQueueHeartbeat()` in `app.js`, fired on every queue mutation plus `visibilitychange`/`pagehide`) POSTing currently-queued `cart_number`s to a new `POST /api/v1/pos/offline-heartbeat`, stored in a new `pos_offline_heartbeats` table (`engines.RecordOfflineHeartbeat`). `ClosePOSSession` now diffs the last heartbeat against what actually synced (`detectOfflineQueueGap`) and, on a mismatch, writes a new browsable `POSOfflineQueueGap` doctype record (HR/Admin + Store Manager read, new "Offline Queue Gaps" sidebar entry) plus an audit-log entry and a `DispatchNotification` alert — shown to the closing cashier too, not just reviewers. **Residual, stated honestly**: a device with truly zero connectivity from the moment an item is queued until storage is wiped can still leave no trace — no client-server architecture can close that specific case, since the server was never contacted at all. This converts "always untraceable" into "untraceable only in that one narrow window," a materially real improvement. Live-verified end-to-end over real HTTP: heartbeat → never-synced-cart → gap correctly detected/recorded/logged on close; a second run confirmed no false positive shape (an actually-synced cart produces no gap check failure in the underlying `EXISTS` logic). Migration: `db/migrations_stage24_addendum_offline_heartbeat.sql`, applied to `tenant_default` + `tenant_new_schema`.
- [x] **20.13** Offline-first queue — deferred here pending a decision, **built later** (see Stage 20.13 entry below).
- [x] **20.13 Offline-first POS queue** — **DONE (2026-07-22).** Decisions: offline window = one shift (tied to the cashier's open session); an offline sale always posts once synced (goods already left) and may push stock negative, flagged for review. `localStorage`-backed queue, replays on reconnect, reuses the existing `cart_number` idempotency key.
  - **Bug fixed**: the session-close success handler referenced an undefined variable — would throw on every successful close.

### POS › Returns & exchanges at the till

- [x] **20.11** POS-side return entry point.
- [x] **47.4 One atomic, replay-safe return/refund/exchange model and operator surface** — closes A-04 and Stage 35.9's stated missing management UI. **Built and green 2026-09-06.** Stage 35.9 already had the right *shape* (one `ReturnRequest` aggregate, a real state machine, prices from the original sale); what it lacked was the four properties that make it safe, plus any UI at all. All four are now in `engines/returns_atomic.go`, and the workflow endpoints — which had **zero caller anywhere in `app.js`** — finally have one.
  - [x] **47.4.1** The legacy path is retired twice over: `POST /api/v1/fulfillment/return` is a hard **410** naming its replacement, and `engines.ProcessReturnAnywhere` itself is a coded refusal, because it was an exported engine function as well as a route. Its `sumPriorReturns` helper is deleted. Why it could not be repaired in place: it took price and cost from the caller, incremented stock with an unlocked upsert, committed, and only then posted two GL reversals with **no idempotency key at all**; its "already returned" pool came from one `SalesReturn` document keyed `RET-<orderID>` whose repeat INSERT conflicted and whose error the HTTP handler discarded — so the recorded total never advanced past the first call while stock and GL for every later call still went through. Four calls of 3 against a sale of 10 returned 12.
  - [x] **47.4.2** Eligible price and cost basis come from the immutable original sale lines. The request shape carries no price at all, so there is nowhere for a client to put one. **A real regression 47.2 introduced was caught here by 47.4.7's own test**: `resolveOriginalSaleLinePrices` read `cost_price` from the stored cart, which 47.2.2 had removed — so every returned line resolved to a zero cost basis and silently posted no COGS reversal. Cost is now resolved through the same `ResolveQuoteUnitCostPaise` the sale used.
  - [x] **47.4.3** The cumulative-quantity check runs **inside** a transaction holding the original sale's own document row `FOR UPDATE` (`assertReturnEligibleTx`) — the natural serialization point: every return against one sale contends on exactly one row, returns against different sales never contend. Plus a tenant-scoped idempotency key through the *same* `command_idempotency` mechanism 47.3.1 built for checkout, completed inside the return's transaction, and stored on the document as its own evidence identity.
  - [x] **47.4.4** Both QC GL legs moved **inside** the QC transaction (they ran after `tx.Commit()` — the A-03 shape applied to returns) and both gained real posting keys (the COGS leg had none). `ProcessRefundRequest` is now one transaction — row-locked status re-check, cash leg, refund status, return closure — because it previously posted the GL and saved the status separately, leaving cash credited against a refund still marked `Approved` and therefore immediately processable again. **New: output-GST reversal** (`PostReturnGSTReversalTx`), which nothing did before — a refund debited 4100 for the full tax-inclusive amount and left the payable accounts untouched, so a tenant kept reporting output tax on goods that had come back. That is a filing error, not a cosmetic one.
  - [x] **47.4.5** Receipt return, partial return, same-value exchange, damaged/quarantine/reject dispositions and supervisor approval already existed. The two genuinely missing ones are built: **No Receipt** (no original bill; priced from the item master and labelled as such, never presented as if it came from a receipt) and **Goodwill** (accepts a return past the window — and *only* the window: cumulative eligibility still holds, because "we will take this back as a gesture" is not "you may return more than you bought"). Both require a written reason, record the authoriser from the session rather than the request body, and are gated on a new `returns.exception` capability held by Administrator + Store Supervisor. Gated in the handler rather than by route, deliberately: the exceptions are two *actions* on a route that must stay open to ordinary returns, and splitting them onto their own route would duplicate the handler (`engines.RoleHasCapability` reads the same templates `checkRouteCapability` does).
  - [x] **47.4.6** The management UI, which Stage 35.9's own entry recorded as missing. Two surfaces: the **POS return panel rebuilt** — the clerk types the bill number and the server says what is still returnable and at what price, instead of the old form that asked the clerk to type SKU, quantity, sale price *and* cost price; and a new **Returns screen** (sidebar, under Sales) listing every return with per-row actions derived from the aggregate's own state machine, plus the inspection dialog (per-line disposition + optional exchange) and the two-step refund (approve, then pay). New `GET /api/v1/returns/eligibility` is what both render from — cumulative quantities and a plain-English reason per line, so a refusal can be repeated to the customer at the counter.
  - [x] **47.4.7** `internal/server/returns_stage47_4_test.go` — legacy endpoint retired (410 + names its replacement); prices come from the sale not the caller; 6 repeated submissions raise one return and report the replay; 6 concurrent clerks against 4 sold units accept exactly 2 with no 500s and no over-claim; return-window boundary with an explained refusal; eligibility reflects prior claims; inspection posts stock + COGS + tax atomically and reconciles; 4 concurrent refund processings pay exactly once. **The A-04 red-team test now passes and was promoted out of the build tag** — the closure taken was the audit's first option (remove the legacy path), so the four replayed calls are refused four times over, which is stronger than the "at most 10 of 10" the test demanded; the assertion still holds it to that. Two pre-existing tests updated for real reasons, recorded inline.
  - **Acceptance: met.** Total returned quantity cannot exceed original eligibility under concurrency (proven, not asserted); stock/refund/GL/tax/evidence reconcile via `engines.ReconcileReturn`, which the tests and the operator share; no duplicate-evidence error is ignored. **Known limitation, unchanged from Stage 35.9 and still true:** an RTO-sourced line has no cost basis (`SalesOrderLine` carries only `unit_price`), so its inventory-side reversal posts zero — and an exchange reuses the returned line's cost as the exchange leg's basis, correct for the same-family swap this feature targets.
- [x] **73.1.1 A POS return appears to refund the full line price, ignoring the bill-level offer discount and redeemed points: reproduce, then fix.** `resolveOriginalSaleLinePrices` (`engines/returns.go:86-130`) refunds each line at its stored `sale_price`. The offer discount is bill-level (`pos_quote.go:389-396`, `Total = Subtotal - OfferDiscount`) and so is loyalty redemption (`pos_checkout.go:234-256`); neither is stored per line, and `returns.go` reads neither. Returning one line of a discounted or points-funded bill therefore likely over-refunds, in cash. **First** a failing test (offer bill + redeemed points, return one line, assert refund = that line's net share). **Then** persist the per-line allocation on the sale at checkout - offer share, points and their money value, tender share, a deterministic rounding remainder (PDF §6 "Partial return allocation", §6.1 step 2) - and refund from it. Foundation for 73.1.2, 73.1.3 and 73.1.6. [rows: Sale return P0, Partial return allocation P0] **Built 2026-10-17 (Batch A) - and the sale side was worse than this item says:** the offer discount never reached the GL or the tax. Every offer sale credited 4100 and debited cash at the list total and backed GST out of the list price (reproduced: 3,000 revenue / 2,730 cash / 457.62 GST on a bill that collected 2,430). Now `EvaluatePOSOffers` splits each offer across its lines (`LineDiscounts`, largest remainder by what is left of each line); the quote carries `offer_share` / `net_total` per line and backs GST out of the net; finalize posts the net (`PostSalesFinanceBookingTx` accepts a wholly free bill), caps points at the net in points not rupees, earns on the money paid, and stores the per-line `allocation` (offer, points, gift card, each money tender) on the cart (`engines/sale_allocation.go`). A return prices its units from that allocation under the sale's lock, cumulatively (`unitShare`; the net is the sum of the tender parts so a refund journal always balances), so a line returned in pieces refunds exactly what it collected; a bill sold before this rebuilds its allocation from what it recorded. **Also fixed:** `RedeemLoyaltyPointsTx` ran `FOR UPDATE` on an aggregate, so every till sale that redeemed points failed (Postgres 0A000) - now a per-customer transaction advisory lock (`lockedLoyaltyBalanceTx`). Receipt prints the posted points; POS Sale Reconciliation holds sales to the net, with tenders measured net. **Historic sales are not re-posted** (release data-safety rule): past offer sales will now read BROKEN in POS Sale Reconciliation, which is accurate - finance decides whether to journal the difference. Verified: `TestStage778CentralisedReturn` + `TestStage1484*` / `TestStage14845` pass; Returns cell checked in Chromium at 1366 and 390 (no overflow, no console errors). Bug found in the build: a TO's Purpose accepts only its fixed list, so the return number goes in `source_return_no`. *Status: Done*

### POS › Discounts, promotions & salesmen

- [x] **30.7.6 POS offer engine, configured in the ERP and applied at the till — closed 2026-08-01.** No offers/promotions engine existed (`campaign.go` is CRM messaging); POS had a single manual "Discount %" box. `Offer` is a flat-schema Master (`db/migrations_stage30_7_pos_offers.sql`) so create/list/edit come free from the generic doctype machinery — the only new engine code is the evaluator, `engines/pos_offers.go`. One doctype covers all four families via `offer_type` (the same shape Campaign's `trigger_type` uses): **Percentage Off**, **Flat Off**, **Buy X Get Y** (cheapest qualifying units free), **Bundle Price** (most-expensive units bundled first, so adding an item can never raise the bill). Conditions AND together: `min_bill_amount`/`min_qty` (thresholds), `coupon_code` (blank = auto-apply), `customer_tier`, `valid_from`/`valid_to`, `max_discount_amount` cap, `priority`, `stackable`. 16 tests (`pos_offers_test.go`).
  - **Evaluated server-side at checkout, not trusted from the client.** `POST /api/v1/pos/offers/preview` is display-only; `handleCheckout` re-runs the same evaluator against the tenant's own `Offer` rows. So a tampered client can't invent a discount, and an offline-replayed cart is priced against the rules as they stand when it lands. Applied offers + total are persisted onto the cart (`applied_offers`/`offer_discount`) for the receipt and audit trail, the same reason `gst_breakdown` is stored rather than recomputed.
  - **A non-stackable offer ends the stack**, and the running total is floored at the bill, so no combination can drive a sale negative. Unmatched coupon codes are reported back rather than silently dropped.
  - **`module_key` is `sales`, not a new `pos` key** — caught live, not in review: POSCart/POSSession are both mapped to `sales`, and the module gate 403s any doctype whose key no plan grants, so a new key would have made every Offer request fail with SAAS-0191 on every existing tenant.
- [x] **20.10** Discount-approval gate — routes through the existing approval engine.
  - **Bug fixed**: `POSCart.created_by` was hardcoded to `'system'` for every sale ever — would have silently defeated the maker-checker self-approval block.
- [x] **85.E3** Salesman per store (77.6): doctype **Salesman** (name, store, phone, default of the store, Active / Left) and Location **Ask the salesman at the till** (Off / Optional / Mandatory). The till shows the picker with the default chosen; Mandatory is enforced on the server (POSOFF-0876); report **Salesman-wise Sales**. Live: picker shown with the default.
- [x] **85.E7** Manual discount (77.13). **Found:** the till's Discount % only triggered approval - it never reduced the price. Now the bill discount (% or Rs) comes off in the server quote like a voucher (shared across lines, GST on the discounted value, on the receipt, netted on returns); above `pos.manual_discount.reason_above_pct` (5%) and below every approval slab it needs a reason (POSOFF-0877); above a slab a manager approves, as before. The applied discount travels as `manual_discount_pct` / `manual_discount_amount`; `discount_pct` keeps its old meaning (a declaration the approval gate reads), so an integration that declares the discount of a price it already lowered is not discounted twice - caught by the A-02 red-team tests. Line level stays the approval-gated price Override. `TestPOSManualDiscountInTheQuote`. Live: 10% -> reason asked -> manager approval.
- [x] **72.7 Gift With Purchase** (10, FR-014, UAT-14/15). Offer type *Gift With Purchase* (gift item, gift qty per bill or per Buy Qty units), evaluated on paid lines only, never using a discount slot; the till prompts "Gift eligible ... scan it"; the scanned gift is billed at 0 with the offer as `promotion_ref`; its cost to the gift profile's expense account. *Reports -> Gift With Purchase Register*. - [x] **73.2.10 Issued vouchers at the till.** The Voucher API redeems atomically (`voucher.go:122`, row lock + max uses), but the POS code box matches offers only (`pos_offers.go:159-204`, `view-pos.js:1316`). Resolve issued vouchers in the same box (owner, value, dates, channel) and redeem them inside the checkout transaction. [row: Voucher POS use P1] **Built 2026-10-17 (Batch A).** The quote (`applyTillVoucher`, `engines/pos_quote.go`) tries the coupon codes no offer claimed as issued vouchers: the first usable one (status, new optional **Valid From**, expiry, max uses, the customer it is restricted to, new optional **channel** Any / POS / Online - `db/migrations_stage73_2_10_voucher_till.sql`) is applied after the offers on what they left, shared across the lines by remaining value like an offer (so it reaches the net, the GST, the GL and any later return - 73.1.1), listed with the applied offers as type *Voucher*; one per bill; a refused voucher gets its reason (`coupon_messages`, shown in the till's coupon line). Checkout redeems it in the sale's own transaction (`redeemVoucherTx`, row-locked, re-checked, counted, Exhausted at max uses) - spent if and only if the sale posts; used up since the quote -> POSOFF-0613 and nothing posts. `RedeemVoucher` (the API) now goes through the same function. ### CRM › Loyalty, gift cards & stored value

- [x] **13.13d CRM/Loyalty (scoped MVP)** — append-only point ledger, earn at checkout / burn via a separate redeem endpoint. No campaigns/segmentation/vouchers.
- [x] **30.2.5 Loyalty redemption burns points without applying the discount — closed 2026-07-31.** The burn is now deferred to checkout and the discount applied automatically. "Redeem Points" checks the balance, caps against the cart total, and records an *intent* on the cart (`posRedeemPoints`) shown as its own line in the POS totals — it no longer calls the burn endpoint. `redeem_points` travels with the checkout request; `handleCheckout` rejects an over-redemption before claiming the cart (so the common case fails with no side effect), and `FinalizePOSCheckout` burns only once the sale is really going through, re-checking the balance against the ledger. Anything that can fail after the burn reverses it first via new `ReverseLoyaltyRedemption` — a compensating `Earn` row, since the ledger is append-only by design, leaving both the burn and its reversal in the customer's history. The cart clears the intent on completion, offline-queue, and approval-pending. GL: revenue is still credited at the full sale value (so the GST posting on top is unchanged and no tax judgement call was needed); the debit side splits between the payment clearing account and new account **5250 Loyalty Points Redeemed** (`db/migrations_stage30_2_5_loyalty_redemption_account.sql`). Loyalty earn now nets off the redeemed portion, which `EarnLoyaltyPoints`' own contract already asked for. Receipt and the completion dialog show the points line and the real amount to collect. Covered by `engines/loyalty_redemption_deferral_test.go`. **Live-verified**: a 210 sale redeeming 50 points returned `amount_due: 160`, moved the balance 300 → 251 (50 burned, 1 earned on the net 160), and posted a balanced entry — cash 160 / loyalty 5250 50 / revenue 210 / GST 5+5.
  - **Near miss worth recording**: the first draft used account code `5300`, which is already **Loss on Asset Disposal**. The migration's `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` prevented the overwrite, but every loyalty redemption would have posted to the asset-disposal account. Caught by reading the seeded chart of accounts back after applying. Always list `gl_accounts` before claiming a new code.
- [x] **26.7.2** Voucher/coupon issuance + redemption — new doctype, reuses the loyalty ledger's earn/burn pattern (Stage 13.13d). Built `engines/voucher.go`: `Voucher` is a flat-schema Master doctype (`db/migrations_stage26_7_crm_loyalty.sql`) — create/list/edit/bulk-CSV-issuance come free from the existing generic doctype/`BulkImportCSV` machinery, zero bespoke code for those. `RedeemVoucher` is the one bespoke action: row-locked (`SELECT...FOR UPDATE`, same pattern as `DecideApproval`) so two concurrent redemptions of a `max_uses=1` voucher can't both succeed; validates expiry/max-uses/customer-restriction and computes Percentage/Flat discount capped at the cart amount. New endpoints `POST /crm/voucher/validate`(preview)/`redeem` — deliberately standalone, not deep POS-checkout integration, mirroring the existing `handleRedeemLoyaltyPoints`'s own shallow-integration shape. Verified: new `TestVoucherRedemption` (discount math both types, expiry, customer-restriction, max-uses exhaustion) plus live HTTP create→validate→redeem; `go build`/`go vet`/`go test ./... -p 1` clean.
- [x] **26.7.3** Loyalty tiering + accrual/expiry rules — additive fields on the existing loyalty ledger. Built `engines/loyalty_tiering.go`: `loyalty_tier_rules` self-service config table (same pattern as `approval_rules`, seeded Bronze/Silver/Gold/Platinum thresholds/multipliers); additive `Customer.loyalty_tier` field, recomputed (`RecomputeLoyaltyTier`) after every earn off lifetime Paid-POSCart spend; `EarnLoyaltyPoints` (`engines/loyalty.go`) now scales base points by the customer's tier multiplier and stamps the earned lot with an `expires_at` (additive column on `loyalty_point_ledger`, `loyaltyPointExpiryDays=365`). Expiry uses a documented approximation, not full FIFO lot-consumption (this ledger has no per-lot remaining-balance tracking to consume against): `StartLoyaltyExpiryWorker` (hourly) expires `min(newly-lapsed, current balance)` per customer via a normal `Burn` row tagged `reference_doctype='LoyaltyExpiry'` — deliberately *not* a new `transaction_type` value, so every existing balance query (`GetLoyaltyBalance`, loyalty-summary/points-liability/RFM reports) already treats it correctly with zero changes to any of them. Verified: new `TestLoyaltyTieringAndExpiry` (tier-rule CRUD, tier selection + earn-multiplier application end-to-end, expiry sweep capped-at-balance + idempotent-on-repeat-tick) plus live HTTP; `go build`/`go vet`/`go test ./... -p 1` clean.

### FIN › Currencies & multi-company

- [x] **37.1** Multi-currency: rate table, dual-currency posting, realised/unrealised FX, revaluation (5 sub-items) — **COMPLETE 2026-08-16** (37.1.1/37.1.2 built 2026-08-11/12; 37.1.3-37.1.5 built 2026-08-16, which also fixed a live correctness bug 37.1.2 had shipped — see 37.1.3)

Existing generic forms, CSV import, permissions and audit paths are reused.
  - [x] **37.1.2** Store transaction currency and functional currency on financial documents — **built 2026-08-12.**
    - **The invariant everything else rests on**: `gl_postings.debit`/`credit` keep meaning exactly what they mean today — an amount in the tenant's functional currency. Every report, trial balance, P&L, GST return and reconciliation in this codebase sums those two columns and none of them is being taught about currency, so the transaction-currency amounts arrive in **new** columns beside them (`currency`, `exchange_rate`, `transaction_debit`, `transaction_credit`, all NULL for a functional-currency posting). A single-currency tenant's rows stay byte-identical to what they are today, and so does every pre-37.1.2 row.
    - **Documents**: new `engines/currency_documents.go` stamps `currency`, `functional_currency`, `exchange_rate` and `base_<amount>` twins, attached at `ValidateDocument` — the one choke point the generic API, CSV import and every engine already pass through — so a doctype added later participates by being listed, not by someone remembering to call a function. An operator-entered rate wins over the resolved one (contract rates exist); otherwise `ResolveExchangeRate` is consulted on the **document's own date**, not today, so a back-dated invoice does not quietly pick up this morning's rate. New `finance.functional_currency` setting, default INR, with a hard INR fallback if it is ever misconfigured.
    - **A real correctness fix falls out of this**: approval slabs are written in the tenant's own currency, and `extractAmount` would have compared a USD 100 invoice against an INR slab. The three approval call sites now use `DocumentBaseAmount`, which returns the base twin and falls back to the raw amount for pre-stamp documents (correct — those were all functional-currency by definition).
    - **Postings**: `PostingOptions` gains `Currency`/`ExchangeRate`/`TransactionDebits`/`TransactionCredits` (variadic, so all 28 existing call sites needed zero changes). `ConvertPostingToFunctional` scales a foreign entry and **absorbs the rounding difference into the largest line on the short side** — without that, per-line rounding can leave the two sides a rupee apart and `PostDoubleEntry` correctly refuses a legitimate voucher as unbalanced. `postApprovedJournalVoucher` is the first real caller.
    - **Verified**: `engines/currency_documents_test.go` covers the stamp, normalisation (`usd`→`USD`), rejection of non-ISO codes, the base-amount approval comparison, the legacy fallback, balance preservation under adverse rounding, rate-1 pass-through, and a real dual-currency posting read back from `gl_postings`. Migration applied and the full suite green.
  - [x] **37.1.3** Realised FX gain/loss on settlement — **built 2026-08-16.** New `engines/currency_fx.go`; additive `db/migrations_stage37_1_fx_revaluation.sql` seeds four accounts (4200 Realised FX Gain, 4210 Unrealised FX Gain, 5600 Realised FX Loss, 5610 Unrealised FX Loss) and backfills every existing tenant schema. No new table, no new column: the revaluation state lives as engine-written JSON keys on the document.
    - **⚠️ THIS FOUND AND FIXED A LIVE CORRECTNESS BUG THAT 37.1.2 SHIPPED.** `PostSalesInvoice` read `total_amount` — which for a USD invoice is 1000, in *dollars* — and posted it straight to Accounts Receivable. **A USD 1,000 invoice at 83.00 booked a 1,000-rupee receivable instead of an 83,000 one**, so the receivable, the ageing report, the credit exposure and the trial balance were all understated by 98.8% for any tenant that used the feature 37.1.2 shipped. The posting sites now read the `base_*` twin. Same class of fix on `PayVendorInvoice`.
    - **The model, recorded once so it is not re-litigated.** A receivable is booked at the invoice-date rate and carried at that rupee value; the cash later received is worth a different number of rupees, and that difference is *realised* (4200/5600). While the invoice sits open across a period end its carrying value is stale, so revaluing it recognises the movement so far as *unrealised* (4210/5610), tracked cumulatively on the document. **At settlement the realised figure is measured against the REVALUED carrying amount, not the original one** — total P&L across every period is then exactly (cash received − amount booked), however it splits. Measuring against the original would double-count every rupee already recognised at a period end. There is deliberately no reversing entry on day one of the next period: this codebase has no automatic reversal machinery, and a cumulative carrying amount reaches the identical answer with one fewer moving part.
    - **The sign convention differs by side and that is not a bug**: when the foreign currency strengthens a receivable is worth MORE (gain) and a payable costs MORE to settle (loss). `resolveSettlementFX` is *told* which side it is on rather than inferring it, and `TestRealisedFXSignConventions` asserts both directions on the same numbers.
    - `SettlementOptions` (settlement date + the rate the bank actually gave) is **variadic**, the `PostingOptions`/`CreateLogisticsBooking` precedent, so all six existing callers of the four settlement engines needed zero changes. An operator-supplied rate beats the table — a bank confirmation states the rate it converted at, and booking a table rate instead just moves the error into the cash account where it is harder to find.
    - **`FXSettlement.PostingDate()` returns empty unless the caller named a date**, which keeps the closed-period check on Postgres's `CURRENT_DATE`. `SettlementDate` defaults to the Go process's *UTC* date, and on this Asia/Calcutta deployment that is yesterday until 05:30 local — a settlement run at 02:00 on the 1st would otherwise be refused by the previous month's just-closed period. Same lesson as the Stage 14 lockout bug and Stage 35's SLA bug: reckon a window against one clock, never a mix.
  - [x] **37.1.4** Period-end revaluation posting to configured FX accounts — **built 2026-08-16.** `RevalueOpenForeignItems` restates every open foreign-currency balance at the closing rate and books the movement to 4210/5610. New setting `finance.fx_revaluation_rate_type` (default Closing).
    - **`GET /api/v1/finance/fx-revaluation` previews and `POST` commits** — the split is the HTTP verb, not a `dry_run` flag on one POST, so a preview can never post and a retry/prefetch/double-click cannot book a second adjustment. A period-end entry a controller cannot preview before it hits the ledger will not be trusted, and this one moves numbers on the face of the P&L.
    - **What gets revalued is a closed list** (`revaluableOpenItems`): `SalesInvoice` while Approved and `VendorInvoice` while Matched/Pending Approval — balances that are actually booked in 1300/2100. Deliberately **not** every currency-bearing doctype: PurchaseOrder, SalesOrder, RFQ and PurchaseRequisition are *commitments*, and revaluing one posts a gain against a control account holding no matching balance, unbalancing the very report this exists to make correct.
    - **Idempotent by refusal, not by silent no-op**: a document already revalued on or after the as-of date is skipped *with a named reason*. "Nothing to do" and "already done" send a controller to completely different places at close. One rate lookup per currency, not per document. The as-of date is passed as the transaction date so a revaluation into a closed period is refused by the check that exists for exactly that.
  - [x] **37.1.5** Multi-currency reporting by selected rate type — **built 2026-08-16.** Three `ReportDefinition`s in `engines/currency_reports.go` (`fx-open-item-exposure`, `fx-gain-loss-register`, `trial-balance-presentation-currency`), so they inherit the generic report screen, CSV/PDF export, scheduled delivery, column masking and the role gate with **no new frontend code**. The register reads `gl_postings` directly — the postings *are* the record and a second store could only disagree with them.
    - **Known limitation, stated rather than hidden**: the presentation trial balance applies **one rate to every line**. A full IAS 21 translation uses closing for balance-sheet items, average for P&L and historical for equity, which needs an equity movement schedule and a cumulative translation reserve this codebase does not have; a half-version would look authoritative and balance to nothing. This is an honest single-rate convenience translation and says so in a `rate_type` column on every row. Real consolidation is 37.2's job.
  - **Two further pre-existing bugs found in live verification and fixed** (neither reachable from a unit test — both are on the document path):
    - **An `ExchangeRate` with no end date was unsaveable.** `ValidateExchangeRateDocument` spelled every read as `fmt.Sprintf("%v", payload[key])`, and `fmt.Sprintf("%v", nil)` is the four-character string `"<nil>"`, not `""` — so an omitted optional field arrived as a *non-empty* value that then failed its format check. An open-ended rate is how essentially every rate table is really maintained, and the message blamed a field the user had never filled in. New `currencyField` helper delegates to the existing `payloadString`.
    - **A `Currency` whose document id was not its ISO code broke every invoice that selected it.** `SalesInvoice.currency` is a `Link`, so the generic check (META-0198) resolves against `documents.id`, while `ApplyDocumentCurrency` requires a three-letter ISO code — the only value satisfying both is one where id == code. The seeded INR row happens to be keyed that way, which is why nothing had noticed. Created any other way the currency saved happily and then every invoice failed with *"Linked Currency record with ID \"USD\" does not exist"*, naming a record sitting right there. Now refused at authoring time by `ValidateCurrencyDocument` with a message naming the id to use.
  - **A defect in this stage's own first cut, caught by live verification and not by the tests**: `PostDoubleEntry` derives a missing per-account transaction amount as `functional / rate`, which is right for a plain foreign posting but *invents* a number on an FX line. A 1,000-rupee revaluation at 84.00 recorded itself as **USD 11.90**, so summing `transaction_debit` for the document reported an exposure of USD 1,011.90 against a real one of USD 1,000. `postingOptionsFor` now zeroes every account in the entry that does not genuinely carry the foreign amount — an FX gain/loss line has no foreign value *by construction*, and a revaluation moves no foreign currency at all. Pinned by `TestFXLinesCarryNoInventedForeignAmount`.
  - **Verified**: `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...` clean; migration applied to dev (`1 applied; 95 already up to date`, `-migrate-status` clean after); 22 new subtests in `engines/currency_fx_test.go` plus `go test ./... -p 1` **fully green**. **Live over HTTP** on a throwaway server (port 8151, stopped and released, **every fixture deleted afterwards and residue confirmed zero**): the whole AR lifecycle — post at 83 (**83,000, not 1,000** — the bug fix), revalue at Closing 84 (+1,000 to 4210, preview-then-commit, and the re-run skipped with its reason), settle at Spot 85 → cash 85,000, AR cleared at the 84,000 *carrying* amount, realised gain **1,000 not 2,000**, AR netting exactly to zero; the AP mirror paying at 85 → DR 2100 83,000 + DR 5600 **2,000 loss** = CR 1100 85,000, the opposite sign on the same numbers; both authoring-time refusals; and all three reports returning real rows including the INR→USD presentation trial balance reporting `balanced: true`. **NOT done**: no frontend surface for the two new routes (API-only so far) and no real-browser pass — the three reports do render through the existing generic report screen.
  - **Safety/verification:** additive migration `db/migrations_stage37_1_currency_foundation.sql` was syntax/execution-tested inside `BEGIN`/`ROLLBACK` and was **not applied as of `0f9781f`** (⚠️ no longer self-enforcing — see the migration warning at the top of this section). ## TAX — Tax & Statutory

### TAX › GST rates, HSN & tax calculation

- [x] **13.10 GST/Tax engine** — CGST/SGST/IGST split calculation (calc-only; e-invoice/IRN explicitly out of scope, no GSP credentials).
- [x] **17.5 GST posting enforcement** — HSN/rate gate at checkout and PO creation; tax-inclusive breakdown auto-computed, posted to dedicated GST GL accounts.
- [x] **24.9** GST rounding precision (stdlib `math.Round`, not a new decimal dependency).
- [x] **30.1.2 Make HSN/GST mandatory on Item — closed 2026-07-31.** `db/migrations_stage30_1_2_item_tax_mandatory.sql` flips both `doctype_fields` rows to mandatory (tenant_default + a backfill loop over every existing tenant schema; `db/migration.sql`'s seed updated for fresh installs), so the form shows the required marker and `ValidateDocument` — the choke point every writer already runs through — refuses the save. `validateItemMasterRules` was tightened to match: HSN is now required outright (it previously only fired when a GST rate was also set, which meant "saveable now, unusable later"), and the rate must be positive, which is exactly what `GetItemGSTInfo` has always demanded at transaction time. The two layers now accept the same thing. Covered by `engines/master_data_validation_test.go`. **Live-verified**: an Item with no HSN is rejected with `GLOBAL-0001` naming the field.
  - **Follow-up worth a decision, not guessed at**: this makes a 0% (exempt/nil-rated) item unsaveable — which matches the fact that checkout has always refused to sell one, so nothing regressed. Supporting exempt goods properly needs an explicit tax-exempt flag on Item; flagged rather than slipped in by letting a 0 rate through.
- [x] **30.5.10 Minor — `gst_rate: 0` closed 2026-07-31; the port note was backwards.** `ComputeGSTForLines` built its rolled-up total without ever setting `GSTRate` (a per-line input), so a checkout response said 0% on a sale it had just charged 5% on. It now reports the blended effective rate actually applied (`total_tax / taxable_amount`), which equals the line rate whenever a cart is single-rate. **Live-verified**: a 5% sale now returns `gst_rate: 5`.
  - **Correction to the audit's second half**: `docs/ai_handover.md` saying **5435** is right, not stale — `environments.json`, `manage.ps1`, `promote.ps1`, `routes.go`'s fallback and all 33 test files agree on 5435. The audit's instance was on 5432 because the portable Postgres had been started with a plain `pg_ctl start` (no `-o "-p 5435"`), landing on Postgres's own default. That drift is what made `go test ./...` unrunnable this session — `db.InitDB` `log.Fatalf`s, so one unreachable port aborts a whole package binary. Fixed by restarting Postgres on 5435 as `manage.ps1` does; the doc needed no change. As a durability measure the test connection string is now overridable (`TEST_DATABASE_URL`, default unchanged at 5435) via `engines/testdb_test.go` + `internal/server/testdb_test.go`, so the suite can run against an instance on any port without editing 33 files.
- [x] **26.6.11** Tax-exempt / nil-rated goods cannot be sold at all. **Brought forward 2026-08-06 from archived Stage 30.1.2's deferred follow-up** — it was flagged there but never given a live item, and `engines/master_data_validation.go:87` still points readers at "docs/micro_checklist.md Stage 30", which is now in the archive. The gap is real, not cosmetic: 30.1.2 made `hsn_code` + a **positive** `gst_rate` mandatory on Item, so a 0% item is unsaveable — and checkout has always refused to price one, which is why nothing regressed and why it went unnoticed. But exempt/nil-rated goods are ordinary in Indian retail (unbranded food grain, fresh produce, books, certain apparel below threshold), so any tenant selling them currently cannot create the Item at all. **Built 2026-08-09.** Product decision taken by the user up front: **all four treatments** (Taxable / Exempt / Nil-Rated / Zero-Rated) and **HSN stays mandatory on all four** (it belongs on the invoice whatever the rate is, and GSTR-1's nil/exempt table is itself HSN-wise), so 30.1.2's HSN guarantee is untouched.
  - **`Item.tax_treatment`** — a `Select` doctype field (`db/migrations_stage26_6_11_item_tax_treatment.sql`), **deliberately `mandatory = FALSE`**: blank/absent normalizes to `Taxable`, so every pre-existing Item and every existing CSV import template keeps validating exactly as before. Nothing is relaxed by that default — a bare `0` is still rejected; `0` only becomes valid (and required) once a non-taxable treatment is chosen explicitly, which is the point the item itself insisted on. Slotted at `display_order` 8 between `hsn_code` (7) and `gst_rate` (9, bumped from 8, with the three PIM fields bumped 9-11 → 10-12) so it sits next to the field it governs rather than after "Variant Options"; metadata-only, no document data touched.
  - **`engines/gst.go`** — the four canonical constants, `NormalizeTaxTreatment` (alias-tolerant: `nil rated`/`nil_rated`/`NILRATED` all resolve, but a typo like `Exmept` is **rejected rather than defaulted to Taxable**, which would silently tax exempt goods), and a new `GetItemTaxInfo`/`ItemTaxInfo` as the one place a transaction turns an Item into tax facts. `GetItemGSTInfo` kept as a thin two-value accessor onto it so no call site or test had to change. `GSTBreakdown` gained `ExemptAmount`/`NilRatedAmount`/`ZeroRatedAmount` (`omitempty`, so an all-taxable cart's JSON is byte-identical to before) — deliberately **not** folded into `TaxableAmount`, which is a filed figure on GSTR-3B 3.1(a).
  - **`validateItemMasterRules`** — treatment-aware, and the rate rejection moved from `MASTER-0042` to **`MASTER-0044`** ("Tax category is required for this item"), a catalog row that existed but was never wired precisely because Item had no tax-category field until now. This also fixes a small pre-existing wart: the old code raised an *HSN* headline over a *GST-rate* detail. Both directions are enforced — a Taxable item must have a positive rate, and a non-taxable one may not carry one, which is what makes the treatment trustworthy downstream.
  - **GL/returns bucketing** — the real compliance half. `GetGSTReturnSummary` reads `4100`'s net balance as the period's *taxable* value, correct only because `PostSalesGSTBooking` moves tax out of `4100` and every sale was taxable; an exempt sale moves nothing, so its turnover would have been **reported as taxable** (GSTR-3B 3.1(a) overstated, 3.1(c) understated). New `PostExemptSalesReclass` (`engines/finance.go`, called from `FinalizePOSCheckout` inside the same failure path as the other two postings — misclassified revenue is a filing problem, not a cosmetic one) moves non-taxable turnover into new accounts `4110`/`4111`/`4112`. Three accounts, not one, because the returns will not accept them merged (GSTR-1 gives nil-rated and exempt their own columns; GSTR-3B splits zero-rated 3.1(b) from exempt+nil 3.1(c)). Summary, `ReportDefinition` columns and the Finance report panel all gained the four figures; the panel's extra row hides itself when they are all zero.
  - **Scoping note:** Zero-Rated models the **LUT/bond route only** (supplied without payment of tax). Export-with-payment-then-refund needs a refund-claim workflow that does not exist here and was not invented.
  - Verified: `go build`/`go vet` clean; new `TestExemptGoodsCanBeSold` (8 subtests incl. a mixed cart's per-bucket split, the GL reclass leaving `4100` net −150, the all-taxable no-op, and the **real save path** — `ValidateDocument` then `ValidateMasterDataRules`, the same pair `handlers_core_doc_engine.go` calls — accepting an Exempt item and rejecting a typo'd one) + new `TestNormalizeTaxTreatment` + `TestItemTaxClassificationRequired` extended to 18 subtests; full `go test ./... -p 1` green. Live on a scratch `:8099`: migration applied via `erp-server -migrate`, `/api/v1/doc/Item/meta` confirms the field at order 8 with the right options and `gst_rate` at 9, and `/api/v1/reports/gst-return-summary` returns all four new keys. **Item create could not be exercised over HTTP** — it is HR/Admin-only and `admin` is MFA-mandatory — so that seam is covered by the save-path unit test above rather than by weakening a shared dev account's MFA. `gst_rate` being absent from `Item/meta` for `cashier1` is pre-existing field-permission behaviour (`migrations_stage16_field_permissions.sql`), not a regression.

- [x] **66.1 HSN master list + ranked suggestions.** `engines/hsn_master.json` (embedded via `go:embed`): 290 HSN/SAC codes across all ten industry profiles, each with a description, its GST rate(s) (GST 2.0, in force from 22 Sep 2025; price-banded codes carry both rates with notes, e.g. garments/made-ups/footwear 5% up to Rs 2,500 a piece, 18% above), the industries it belongs to, **keywords** (decide *which* code: the material or the exact product, score 3), **related** words (what *kind* of thing, score 1) and **exclusions** ("german silver", "gold plated" are not precious metal). ## PRT — Printing & Labels

### PRT › Sticker & label printing

- [x] **13.15 Sticker/barcode printing** — text labels (not scannable symbology — unverifiable without a physical scanner), print history log.

- [x] **52.2** Generic document-source resolver (`engines/sticker_document_source.go`, new file) — `ResolveDocumentStickerLines(tenantID, sourceDoctype, sourceDocID)` normalizes a GRN's `received_items` (prints against `accepted_qty` = `qty - rejected_qty - damaged_qty` or an explicit override, the same derivation `wms_receiving.go` posts against; two lines of the same SKU merge only when they share a batch, so a batch-tracked item received across two lots keeps its lots separate on the printed stickers) or a TransferOrder's `items` into a common `{SKU, Qty, BatchNo, ExpiryDate}` shape. Adding a third source (PO/SO) later is one more `case`, not a redesign. `PrintStickersForDocument` resolves lines, optionally filters to a caller-supplied SKU selection (this is what makes "print the whole GRN" and "print one line" the same code path — one-by-one is just a length-1 selection), applies per-SKU copy overrides (defaulting to the line's own accepted/transfer qty), delegates into the same `resolveAndLogSticker` helper the pre-existing manual-scan `PrintStickers` uses (factored out of it, zero behavior change to that function), and returns labels **sorted by resolved category** so a mixed-category GRN prints as separable per-category stacks. `PreviewDocumentStickerLines` is the read-only precursor (no `sticker_print_log` write) backing the frontend's review table. New `GET /api/v1/stickers/preview` route; `POST /api/v1/stickers/print` and the QZ silent-print payload endpoint both extended with optional `source_doctype`/`source_doc_id`/`copies_override` fields rather than a parallel endpoint. `sticker_print_log` gained additive nullable `source_doctype`/`source_doc_id`/`template_id` columns for the audit trail.
- [x] **52.4** Frontend (`public/app.js`, `public/styles.css`) — restructured the single "Sticker Printing" screen into a Print/Templates tab bar (reusing `renderHRView`'s existing tab-bar convention, not inventing a new one). **Print tab**: new "Print from Transaction" panel — a module `<select>` (`BULK_STICKER_SOURCE_DOCTYPES`, currently GRN + Transfer Order) plus `attachLinkTypeahead` (the existing single-door document picker, reused exactly as GRN's own PO-reference field already does) to pick the specific document; loading it calls the new preview endpoint and renders a review table (checkbox per line, editable copy count, resolved category + template name shown per row) with both a per-row **Print** button (one line) and a **Print Selected** button (the whole document, respecting unchecked rows) — both flow through the existing QZ-silent-then-browser-fallback path. `renderPrintSheet` (the browser @media print fallback) now renders a template-driven label as absolutely-positioned mm-sized `<div>`s when a template resolved, falling back to the original fixed markup otherwise, and marks the last copy of each category run with a page-break class so a mixed-category batch tears apart as separate stacks. **Templates tab** (new): a list of `StickerTemplate` documents plus a from-scratch drag-and-drop designer — the first pointer-drag UI in this app (no existing canvas/floor-plan editor to pattern-match against), built as plain `mousedown`/`mousemove`/`mouseup` on positioned `<div>`s, no library. A field palette adds a positioned element bound to a label field (SKU/Name/Barcode/HSN/Category/Batch/Expiry/Qty/Source Doc) or free static text; the canvas renders through the exact same `renderStickerElementHTML` function the live print sheet uses, so there is nothing to keep in sync between "what you designed" and "what prints." - [x] **58.1 Rendering engine** — new `public/sticker-engine.js`, the one renderer for studio canvas, thumbnails, browser print and thermal payloads. Draws every element on a canvas at the printer's DPI, thresholds to 1-bit, and emits a TSPL `BITMAP` (inverted bits, `SIZE`/`GAP`/`DIRECTION`/`DENSITY`/`SPEED`) or ZPL `^GFA` with standard ASCII compression (`^PW`/`^LL`/`^PON|^POI`/`~SD`/`^PR`/`^PQ`). Identical consecutive rows collapse into one image with a copy count; jobs go in 50-row batches (PrintBridge/QZ cap one WebSocket message at 32 MB). Browser path: PNGs at ≥300 dpi laid out as roll pages (CSS named `@page` per template, so one job mixes sizes) or an A4 sheet grid. Hand-written encoders, no library: **Code 128** (auto B/C subset — a 13-digit value is 123 modules vs 178 in pure B), **EAN-13**, **QR** (byte mode, v1-40, L/M/Q/H, mask penalty). Bars/modules are whole printer dots. **Verified**: Code 128 — 20 edge-case values decode exactly with ZXing; EAN-13 — 7 values incl. the ERP's own dated `0200…` codes decode with ZXing; QR — all 160 version × ECC combinations at max capacity + Unicode (₹, Devanagari) decode (159 with jsQR; v23-L, which jsQR alone rejects, decodes with ZXing); ZPL compression — 400 random/structured bitmaps round-trip through an independent spec decompressor.

### PRT › Printers, alignment & PrintBridge

- [x] **31.1.1 The signing contract, verified from QZ's source — closed 2026-08-03.** A wrongly-signed call is rejected *silently* (QZ falls back to prompting per label), so this had to be established as fact, not inferred. `qz-tray.js` hashes the request and passes the **hash** to the backend, which makes both obvious backend implementations wrong. Settled from source: `qz/auth/Certificate.java:363` → `verifier.update(getBytesUtf8(sha256Hex(data)))` with `SHA512withRSA`, over `new JSONObject(message, {"call","params","timestamp"}).toString()` (`PrintSocketClient.java:218`). So: sign the **UTF-8 bytes of the lowercase hex digest**, key order `call,params,timestamp`. Also confirmed there is **no 2.1-vs-2.2 fork** to handle — the tray does its own hashing from the raw JSON, so both client generations agree. Ports `[8181,8282,8383,8484]` secure / `[8182,8283,8384,8485]` insecure; handshake is unsigned `getVersion` → certificate → signed calls.
- [x] **31.1.2 `engines/qz_print.go` — key material and signing — closed 2026-08-03.** RSA-2048 self-signed cert, `QZ_PRIVATE_KEY_PATH`/`QZ_CERTIFICATE_PATH` else auto-generated once into the OS per-user config dir — the same shape `channel_credentials.go` already uses, except it never `log.Fatalf`s: printing is optional and must not take the server down. **The sign endpoint is not a blind oracle** — it accepts exactly one SHA-256 hex digest (`^[0-9a-f]{64}$`) and nothing else, so it cannot be talked into signing an attacker-chosen document, which QZ's own reference backends allow.
- [x] **31.1.3 `Printer` Master extended rather than a new registry — closed 2026-08-03.** Six fields added (`qz_printer_name`, `print_role`, `printer_language`, `label_width_mm`, `label_height_mm`, `dpi`) via `db/migrations_stage31_1_qz_print.sql`, so the whole config screen comes free from the generic Master machinery. `print_role` is what makes it one-click — the server resolves role → printer so no operator picks one per job. Migration also creates `print_job_log` and **catches up existing tenant schemas** with a `DO` block, the failure mode Stage 30.2.2 existed to clean up. Routes share the existing `stickers` module key deliberately; a new key would 403 every existing tenant (the SAAS-0191 trap from 30.7).
- [x] **31.1.4 `public/qz-print.js` — vanilla client, no dependency — closed 2026-08-03.** ~330 lines vs the official ~150KB (which carries a promise shim, its own SHA-256 and remote-relay logic unused here). **A pure-JS SHA-256 fallback is mandatory, not defensive**: `crypto.subtle` is absent outside a secure context, and a packing bench on `http://192.168.x.x` is exactly that. Verified against Node's `crypto` — 8 vectors + 300 random-length fuzz cases, specifically across the 55/56/64-byte padding boundaries.
- [x] **31.1.5 Payloads: raw ZPL/TSPL/ESC-POS or PDF/HTML per printer — closed 2026-08-03.** `engines/qz_payload.go`. **Marketplace PDFs pass through byte-for-byte** — re-rendering a courier's label risks altering a barcode they scan — with 4x6 sizing applied as driver options instead. ERP-native shipping labels *are* generated and gained a real Code 128 AWB symbol on thermal, which `engines/marketplace.go`'s `GenerateShippingLabel` explicitly could not do ("prints text, not a real scannable symbology/PDF"). Stickers route through the existing `engines.PrintStickers`, so SKU validation, the DEVICE-0298 check and `sticker_print_log` are unchanged.
- [x] **31.1.6 UI + graceful degradation — closed 2026-08-03.** Print Setup panel on Sticker Printing: connection status, **Detect Printers** (the OS names must match verbatim — `ZDesigner ZD220-203dpi ZPL`, not "Zebra ZD220"), Test Print, and a file picker that prints any marketplace label/invoice. If QZ isn't running, `qzTryPrint` returns false and every caller falls back to the existing `@media print` sheet; non-thermal sticker printers take the same route via the server's `fallback: "browser"` reply. Nobody is blocked because the bridge is down.
- [x] **31.1.7 Rollout tooling + operator guide — closed 2026-08-03.** `cmd/qzcert` exports `override.crt` (public cert only; the private key never leaves the server) and prints the per-OS install paths. `docs/guides/QZ_PRINTING_SETUP.md` covers Java/QZ install, the certificate, **Chrome's Local Network Access gate** (the step Myntra's own mail spends most of its length on, and the usual cause of "the print button does nothing"), printer-language selection, and a troubleshooting table keyed to the actual error strings.
- [x] **31.1.9 Wire one-click print into the remaining screens — closed 2026-08-05.** All three landed: **Print Label** on the logistics-booking row, **POS receipt via ESC-POS** at checkout, and **Print** on the Sales Invoice row. Two new job types (`Receipt`, `Invoice`) with server-side payload builders, plus the frontend wiring and its fallbacks. `print_role` already offered both names (the Stage 31.1 migration seeded `Shipping Label,Invoice,Sticker,Receipt,General`), so **no migration was needed** — a Printer record just needs `Default For` set.
  - **Both new documents are re-read server-side from their stored document, not taken from the browser.** `BuildReceiptPayload` reads the `POSCart`, `BuildInvoicePayload` the `SalesInvoice`. That is what makes a reprint honest — a receipt printed an hour later shows what was actually rung up — and it means a tampered client cannot print a receipt for a bill that never existed. `fetchPrintableDocument` is a deliberately separate small reader rather than a call into `PostSalesInvoice`/`FinalizePOSCheckout`: those sit inside write paths (`FOR UPDATE`, "only a Draft may be posted") that a print has no business running.
  - **Only a `Paid` cart prints a receipt** (`GLOBAL-0019`, 422). A Pending Approval cart is money not yet collected and a Failed one is a sale that did not happen; a printed receipt is what a customer walks out with, so this refuses rather than printing with a caveat. An **invoice prints at any status** on purpose — a Draft invoice is a legitimate proforma — but is stamped `DRAFT` so it cannot be mistaken for a posted one.
  - **`isESCPOS` is deliberately narrower than the existing `isRawLanguage`.** ZPL and TSPL are label languages with no concept of a continuous feed, so a receipt emitted as raw commands to a ZPL unit comes out blank. Only ESC-POS gets commands; every other language (PDF/HTML/ZPL/unset) gets rasterisable HTML through the OS driver. Do not "simplify" this back to `isRawLanguage`.
  - **`escposColumns` defaults an unset `label_width_mm` to 42 columns (80mm roll).** A 58mm till needs `label_width_mm = 58` on its Printer record or lines are laid out too wide. Every line is clipped to the column count and `escposRow` clips the *description*, never the amount — a receipt is checked on its numbers.
  - **Real bug found and fixed in the existing browser receipt**: `printPOSReceipt` never deducted `offer_discount`. Checkout returns `amount_due = sale_total - loyalty_discount - offer_discount`, so any sale with a Stage 30.7 offer applied printed a total **higher than the cash actually collected**. Now takes a 7th defaulted `offerDiscount` argument and prints Subtotal / Offer discount / Loyalty lines. The stored `applied_offers` are also named on the ESC-POS receipt, which is what the comment on `handlers_pim_pos_finance.go`'s `storedPayload["applied_offers"]` asked for in the first place.
  - **Second real bug fixed in the same area**: `#receipt-print-area` had **no on-screen `display: none`** — only the `@media print` block ever hid it — so after a POS receipt printed, its markup stayed rendered at the bottom of the live page until the next navigation. `styles.css` now hides all three print areas on screen (`#sticker-print-area` always did; the receipt one never has).
  - **`qzTryPrint` gained a `quiet` option, and the three new call sites use it.** "No Printer record is Default For Receipt" is the *normal* state of a tenant that has not set QZ up — without `quiet` a cashier would get a `DEVICE-0298` modal on every single sale before the browser sheet appeared. Quiet suppresses the payload-preparation dialog and the unmapped-printer dialog (both `console.debug`'d instead) and falls through. A failure at the tray itself stays loud in every case: that one means printing was really attempted and really failed.
  - **Print Label falls back to the on-screen label modal, not to `window.print()`** — the plain-text label is not a printable sheet, and someone whose QZ Tray is down still needs to read the AWB off the screen to write the docket. The read-only **Label** button is unchanged and still sits next to it.
  - **Verified.** `go build` / `go vet` / `node --check` clean; **`go test ./... -p 1` fully green** (including the finance-9500 test the notes warn can false-fail). **5 new Go tests** (`engines/qz_receipt_invoice_test.go`) covering column arithmetic, the amount-survives-clipping rule, ESC-POS-vs-label-language selection, the Paid-only guard, coded not-found, offer-discount arithmetic and the DRAFT stamp. Then driven **live over HTTP** on a scratch :8261 as `manager1`: all three job types role-resolved to the right printer and produced correct payloads (receipt 500.00 subtotal → 450.00 due after a 50 offer; shipping label emitted a real `^BCN` Code 128 of the AWB; invoice marked DRAFT), plus every error path (unknown job type, missing `document_ref`, missing document, unpaid cart). Finally **18/18 Playwright checks** against the real `index.html`+`app.js` with QZ absent, so every assertion exercised the fallback.
  - **Traps for whoever touches this next.** (a) The **Stage 31.1 migration was still unapplied on this dev DB** — `-migrate-status` showed it as the 1 pending item; it applied cleanly, so the nested `$f$` dollar-quoting risk 31.1.8 flags is now cleared locally as well as on prod. (b) **`Store Manager` has no read grant on `LogisticsBooking`**, so the Marketplace screen's bookings table is *empty* for `manager1` and a UI test cannot find a row there — assert on `renderLogisticsBookingActions` directly (`admin` can see it but is the MFA-mandatory account). (c) `psql` on this machine needs **flag-style args** (`-h 127.0.0.1 -p 5435 -U postgres -d custom_erp -f file.sql`); passing a `postgres://` URI as the first argument makes it silently ignore `-c`/`-f` and run nothing while still exiting 0. (d) `documents.created_by` is **FK'd to `users`** — seed with `'system'`, not an arbitrary string. (e) Both verification harnesses were scratch tooling and were not kept.
  - **Known parity point, deliberately not closed**: neither receipt rendering prints a GST breakdown, though `gst_breakdown` is stored on the cart. The browser receipt has never shown it and adding it to only the ESC-POS side would make the two disagree. A GST-compliant receipt layout is its own piece of work, not part of wiring the print path. [needs design decision if a compliant tax receipt is wanted]

- [x] **52.8** Found live while walking 52.6's own documented steps (the "fix the app if the doc reveals a real gap" half of this repo's second principle), **not previously reported**: the transaction print's line selection was keyed on **SKU alone**, but `ResolveDocumentStickerLines` deliberately keeps a SKU received on two lots as **two lines** (it merges only within a lot — 52.2). So for a batch-tracked GRN: the two rows shared one checkbox and one copies value (unticking or editing either hit both), and the per-row **Print** button printed *both* lots, directly contradicting "print one line". 52.5's tests covered the resolver's lot-splitting but never selected one of two same-SKU lines, so nothing caught it. **Fixed at the one choke point both print paths already run through** rather than at each call site: new `engines.StickerLineSelection{SKU, BatchNo, Copies}` replaces the old `selectedSKUs []string` + `copyOverrides map[string]int` parameter pair on `PrintStickersForDocument`; `filterStickerLines` matches a line on SKU *and* lot (empty `BatchNo` = every lot of that SKU) and applies each selection's own copy count, so copy resolution now happens in exactly one place instead of two. `engines.SKUSelections` adapts the old shape, and a new shared `stickerSelections` helper in `internal/server` resolves both endpoints' requests identically so the browser-fallback and QZ-silent paths can never disagree. **Backward-compatible**: both endpoints accept a new optional `lines: [{sku, batch_no, copies}]` array *or* the original `skus`/`copies_override` fields, and a SKU-only selection still means "every lot of this SKU" — the manual scan flow and any existing API client are untouched. Frontend (`public/view-printing.js`) now keys row state by line index rather than SKU, sends the per-line shape, and shows a **Batch/Lot** column whenever any line on the document carries a lot (it stays hidden otherwise, so the common non-batch case looks exactly as before); `qzTryPrint` in `public/app.js` forwards the new field. New regression test `TestPrintStickersForDocumentSelectsOneLotOfASKU` pins all four behaviours (both lots by default, one lot addressed alone, a copy override hitting only its own lot, and a SKU-only selection still covering both). `go build ./...`, `go vet`, `gofmt` on the touched files, `node --check` on both JS files, the full Stage 52 engine suite are clean. No new route and no new migration, so `attack_surface.json` needs no regeneration (`TestAttackSurfaceManifestIsCurrent` passed mid-session and later drifted only on a concurrent session's new Stage 53 migration file). **Live-verified over real HTTP** on a scratch instance (port 8097, throwaway two-lot GRN): per-line selection returned exactly the requested lot at the right qty, a per-lot copy override hit only its own lot, and both the legacy `skus` and no-selection forms still returned both lots unchanged; the QZ endpoint emitted 3 ZPL labels for a 3-copy single-lot run and 10 for the whole document. Fixtures and their log rows removed afterwards.
- [x] **53.12 The bill says which store.** New `engines.ReceiptStoreHeader` / `ReceiptStore.Line()` resolving Location → name, and Location → `legal_entity` → LegalEntity → name/GSTIN/state. Wired into **both** server-side branches of `BuildReceiptPayload` (ESC-POS *and* the HTML driver fallback) and into the browser's `printPOSReceipt`. Cashier added: `storedPayload["cashier"]` is now persisted on the POSCart from the resolved identity, so the server can rebuild the full header from the cart alone. Deliberately forgiving — a missing Location, a Location with no entity, or an entity with no GSTIN each drop that line rather than failing the print, because a receipt must always print. `ReceiptStore.Line()` also de-duplicates the Stage 17.9 seed case where `name == code` (no more "HO (HO)").
- [x] **53.12b Pre-existing receipt bug found and fixed (not reported, not in the plan).** The **browser-fallback receipt printed `0.00` on every line**. Stage 47.2 made the checkout payload carry `sale_price: 0` for every server-priced line (only an unpriced assisted-mode line sends a figure), and `printPOSReceipt` was handed that same array — so `qty * sale_price` was 0 for every ordinary line and the line totals summed to nothing. It survived unnoticed because the QZ/ESC-POS path rebuilds the receipt server-side from the stored cart, so the fallback only prints in shops with no receipt printer configured. Fixed via a new `posReceiptItems()` that pairs each payload line back to its cart line and takes the resolved price (and the product name) from there.

### CHN › Public API, webhooks & extensions

- [x] **14.17-14.20 3rd-party extension isolation** — out-of-process HTTP webhook hooks (`document.before_save`/`after_save`) instead of Go's `plugin` package (same-crash-domain risk). Synchronous before-save with goroutine+timeout+recover so a hanging/panicking hook can neither crash nor block the server — live-verified with a real concurrent request during a hung hook call.
- [x] **38.1** Public API v1 — a curated, versioned subset with a compatibility policy, not all 257 routes — **contract written 2026-08-11, first routes opened 2026-08-12 (read-only).**
  - Four endpoints, each naming its required scope explicitly: `GET /items`, `GET /items/{code}` (`items:read`), `GET /inventory?sku=` (`inventory:read`), `GET /orders/{id}/status` (`orders:read`). `publicAPIMiddleware` **panics at registration** for a route that declares no scope, so "public by accident" is not a reachable state.
  - **Every response is a curated projection, not a document dump.** The internal `/api/v1/doc/{doctype}` returns every stored field; publishing that shape would turn every future internal field into an accidental public contract. `engines/public_api_v1.go` defines the four response types — no cost, margin or supplier data on a product; availability without the held-back buckets behind it; order tracking without pricing or PII the caller did not already supply. Availability is computed through the **same `computeATS`** every internal caller uses, so a public read can never disagree with what the order path will accept. Order lookup accepts our order id *or* the caller's own channel order id, since a marketplace connector holds the latter.
  - Paging is clamped at 200 (`NormalizePublicPaging`) — an unbounded public read is the cheapest possible way to take the database down for every other tenant. `updated_since` supports incremental polling instead of re-reading the catalog.
  - Unregistered paths under the prefix answer a **JSON 404** rather than falling through to the static file server and handing an API client an HTML page. Deliberately outside the auth middleware: an unknown path has no scope to check.
  - **Read-only in this slice by choice, not by limitation** — the 38.5 idempotency spine is already in place under the same middleware, so a write endpoint joins by being curated, not by being made safe first.
  - **Verified live over HTTP**: authorised read (200 with budget headers), missing key (401), malformed key (401, generic), a narrower key hitting an endpoint it lacks the scope for (403 naming the scope), missing required parameter (422), unknown resource (404), unknown path (JSON 404).
- [x] **38.3** Rate limiting and quotas per credential — a per-minute burst window (in-process; a minute-scale check does not need durability) plus a **daily quota counted from the traffic log**, so a process restart cannot hand an integration a fresh allowance. Tenant defaults via `platform.public_api_rate_limit_per_minute`/`_daily_quota`, overridable per credential through `PUT /api/v1/admin/api-credentials/{id}/limits` (a null value clears the override, so raising a plan-wide ceiling is one setting rather than a sweep over every key). `X-RateLimit-*`/`X-Quota-*` are published on **every** response, success or rejection — an integration that can only discover its limits by being refused will keep being refused. The two 429s are distinguished in the message and in `Retry-After`, because "wait a second" and "wait until midnight" call for different client behaviour. Revocation and rotation release the in-process window. **Subtlety worth recording**: the DB seed for the daily counter excludes the outcomes that were rejected *before* consuming quota (`PublicAPIUnadmittedOutcomes`), or a credential rate-limited this morning would find its quota mysteriously smaller after a restart.
- [x] **38.4** Webhook subscriptions with HMAC signing, retry/backoff and DLQ — **built 2026-09-01, on top of 38.6 (built first, same session).** Extends `outbox.go` exactly as the backlog item names it: `WebhookSubscription` is a plain generic-doc-API doctype (the `ScheduledReport` precedent — no dedicated create/list/delete handler), and `dispatchWebhooksForEvent` (`engines/webhook.go`) is called from `processOutbox` once an outbox event is already durably committed — fanning out to one `webhook_delivery` async job (Stage 38.6's runner) per Active subscription whose `event_pattern` matches (exact match or a trailing-`*` prefix wildcard). New `engines/document_numbering.go` holds a doctype → `{series key, number fields}` registry and `PrepareDocumentNumber`, attached at the one create choke point (`handlers_core_doc_engine.go`, immediately after `PreparePurchaseRequisition` and *before* `ValidateDocument`, since the fields it fills are mandatory). 12 doctypes: PurchaseOrder (PO), GRN, ASN, RFQ, VendorQuote (QTN), TransferOrder (TO), ExpenseClaim (EXP), Leave (LV), EmployeeLoan (LOAN), Grievance (GRV), ProductionOrder (PRO), Attendance (ATT).

Live-reproduced and now covered by `TestDocumentNumberIssuedByServer`.

Now ANNUAL → `26-27`, MONTHLY → `26-27-07`, NEVER → one continuous series with no period segment. The visible segment and the counter bucket are derived **together** on purpose — a series that resets on a period it doesn't display re-issues last year's numbers, which (the number being the id) is a rejected save, not a cosmetic problem.

Each Default is byte-for-byte the constant it replaced, so an untouched tenant behaves exactly as before, and each is read via `GetSetting*` **at its consuming site on every use** — never captured into a package var at startup, which is precisely what makes "change it and it changes everywhere" true without a restart.   - **Platform (guardrailed):** default/max list page size (500/1000), per-tenant concurrency (15), CSV import batch size (500), max synchronous report rows (5000), blanket field length cap (10000). Each carries a registry `Min`/`Max` that `validateSettingValue` enforces at save time, so the value is admin-editable but a typo can't take the server down.
