### TEN › Branding, logos & hostnames

- [x] **44.1** `public.tenants.host_slug` — `db/migrations_stage44_tenant_host_slug.sql`, additive, applied and verified on the dev DB. Backfilled from `tenant_id` **only where `tenant_id` is already a legal DNS label**: `tenant_id` is free-text `VARCHAR(100)` with no character restrictions and this repo's own fixtures contain `_`, which is illegal in a hostname. Verified: `default` → `default`, `tenant_new` → `NULL` (correctly skipped — a blind backfill would have minted a slug that could never be served, and the failure would only have shown up as an unexplained certificate error much later). Unique index on `LOWER(host_slug)` because hostnames are case-insensitive; partial, so any number of tenants may keep a NULL slug.
- [x] **44.2** Host→tenant resolution attached at the **one** choke point every request already passes (`apiMiddleware`, per CLAUDE.md's shared-choke-point rule) — `internal/server/tenant_host.go`. `<slug>.<TENANT_BASE_DOMAIN>` now precedes `X-Tenant-ID`/`?tenant_id=` in the pre-auth chain, on the reasoning that a hostname had to survive DNS and a certificate to arrive whereas those two are simply whatever the caller typed. Single label only: a two-level name would need a wildcard certificate Let's Encrypt will not issue over HTTP-01, so accepting one would produce a tenant that resolves but can never be served. Reserved labels (`app`, `www`, `api`, `admin`, `sandbox`, `mail`, …) never resolve to a tenant, so provisioning a client called "www" cannot take over that hostname.
- [x] **44.3** **The token stays authoritative, and a mismatch is refused.** A session for tenant A presented on tenant B's hostname returns the same generic 401 as any dead session rather than being silently served as A. This is deliberately *not* "host wins" — letting the host override the claim would have been a real cross-tenant escalation. It is the narrower guarantee: the claim still scopes every query, and the hostname merely has to agree with it.
- [x] **44.4** CORS widened by *shape*, not by list — `originAllowed()`. `CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS` still wins first and is unchanged; the addition is that https origins at the base domain or one label under it are accepted, so provisioning a tenant no longer needs an app restart with a longer allowlist. Scoped tight: https only, no port, no path, same single-label rule. The suffix test is anchored on `"." + base` so a domain someone else registers that merely ends in the same letters (`acme.evilwholeops.in`) is not mistaken for ours — locked by a test.
- [x] **44.5** **On-demand TLS, gated by the app** — `deploy/Caddyfile` + `GET /internal/tls-ask`. Per-tenant hostnames are not listed in the config (the tenant set changes without a config change), so each certificate is obtained on its first TLS handshake. The `ask` gate is what makes that safe: Caddy asks the app before requesting a certificate and proceeds only on a 2xx, so a hostname that is not a live tenant never reaches Let's Encrypt. Without it anyone who pointed a DNS record at this box could drive unbounded issuance. **Deliberately achieved without `xcaddy`** — a wildcard certificate would need a DNS-01 provider plugin and therefore a custom Caddy binary to keep patched, which is exactly the trade 26.1.3a already rejected. Found and fixed during validation: current Caddy **removed** `on_demand_tls`'s `interval`/`burst` throttle, so `ask` is now the only gate — which is why the handler fails closed on every path (unset `TENANT_BASE_DOMAIN`, unknown slug, reserved label, DB-less startup all answer non-2xx). Proxy behaviour moved into an `(erp_app)` snippet imported by both site blocks so the platform host and tenant hosts cannot drift. `/internal/*` is refused on the public listener; Caddy reaches the gate over 127.0.0.1, which never passes through that block.
- [x] **44.10** **Unknown tenant hostnames are refused (`tenantHostGate`, 2026-08-15).** A single-label, non-reserved name under `TENANT_BASE_DOMAIN` that matches no tenant now gets a 404 instead of falling through to `X-Tenant-ID` and then `"default"` — which is what `nosuchclient.wholeops.in` did until now: it served the default tenant's login page. **Opened by 26.1.3b, not by 44.5.** While per-tenant certificates come from the ask gate, an unknown hostname never completes a handshake, so the fall-through was unreachable; behind Cloudflare the origin serves one wildcard certificate for every name under the base domain and the gate stops filtering anything, so the app has to make the judgement itself. Not a security boundary — the token claim scoped every query before this and still does — it is the product guarantee that a per-client address means a client. Attached to the whole-mux wrapper chain in `routes.go` rather than to `apiMiddleware`, because the SPA shell and static files are what a browser asks for first and they never pass through that middleware; inside `securityHeaders` so the 404 still carries them. Inert without `TENANT_BASE_DOMAIN`, locked by a test that asserts localhost/loopback/apex/platform-host/foreign-domain all still pass through.
  - **Found while writing it:** routing this through `writeAPIErrorGeneric` was wrong. A 404 maps to `GLOBAL-0004`, which carries `LogRequired`, so every probe at a random subdomain would have written a Medium row to the system-error log — a log-flood vector, since sweeping subdomains is exactly what scanners do. It now writes through `writeResponse` directly: the same envelope every other error uses (that function is the single place bodies are written), without the catalog's logging hooks.
- [x] **44.6** `clientname.wholeops.in/oms` — the **path**-style module segment. **Resolved 2026-08-31 (asked directly, since the item itself was marked `[needs design decision]`): keep hash routing (`#oms`), do not convert.** The hostname half (44.2) already delivers real per-client addresses; the path form was judged not worth the router rework, every-internal-link update, and `routes.go` static-file-fallback change it would cost. No code change — this closes the decision, not a build.
- [x] **44.8** **Two latent bugs in `deploy/enable_tls.sh`, both found by running it for the first time.** The script was written in Stage 26.1.1 (2026-08-06) and had never been executed, because there was no domain to execute it against — so both would have hit whoever ran it first, not just this session.
  - **It could not be parsed at all.** `${PUBLIC_IP:-this box's public IP}` — the apostrophe in `box's` opens a quote inside a parameter expansion that bash never closes, and the whole script died at parse time with `unexpected EOF` pointing at the *last* line rather than the offending one. Rephrased to drop the apostrophe, with a comment saying why.
  - **It chowned the log directory before validating, which is exactly backwards.** `caddy validate` does not merely parse — it provisions every module, including **opening the access log**. The script runs as root, so validation created `/var/log/caddy/erp-access.log` owned `root:root 0600`, and the subsequent `systemctl reload` (running as the `caddy` user) failed with `permission denied` on a box where the directory, the config and DNS were all correct. Chowning the directory first cannot help: the offending file does not exist yet at that point. Now `chown -R` **after** validation. The script's own auto-rollback worked correctly through both failures, which is the reason this cost nothing.
- [x] **44.9** **The go-live blocker was a DigitalOcean cloud firewall, and it was diagnosed rather than guessed.** First `enable_tls.sh` run installed the config and reloaded Caddy cleanly, then ACME failed at the network layer: `Timeout during connect (likely firewall problem)` for **both** `tls-alpn-01` (443) and `http-01` (80). The obvious readings were all wrong — `ss -tlnp` showed Caddy listening on `*:80`/`*:443` and `ufw` allowed both. What settled it was a `tcpdump` on the droplet while connecting from the dev machine: **zero inbound packets arrived**, and since tcpdump sits below netfilter for inbound traffic, a local iptables DROP would still have shown the SYNs. So they were discarded upstream. The DO console confirmed it exactly: firewall `Test` had a single inbound rule (SSH/22) and "all other incoming traffic is blocked" — it only ever needed SSH while the ERP was tunnel-only. User added inbound HTTP/80 and HTTPS/443. Caddy had been reverted to `Caddyfile.holding` in the meantime so it would stop retrying into Let's Encrypt's failed-validation quota (5/hour/hostname; 2 consumed, window since reset).

Nothing here needed a deploy after all.

Did **not** attempt to log in as the real `minn` tenant (no credentials for a real customer, and none should be guessed at) - host-based tenant *routing* is proven; the account-level isolation guarantee (44.3) was already unit-tested in 44.2/44.3's own tests and is unchanged.

## SEC — Identity, Access & Security

### SEC › Sign-in, sessions & MFA

- [x] **13.3 MFA (TOTP)** — stdlib-only (`crypto/hmac`+`sha1`+`base32`), required for HR/Admin. Login routes an MFA-required role into enrollment or challenge via a short-lived purpose token.
  - **Bug fixed**: the purpose token initially didn't carry `tenantID`, silently blanking tenant scoping for the whole MFA flow.
- [x] **21.4** Account-menu + sign-out redesign.
- [x] **21.5** New self-service User Profile screen.
- [x] **21.6** Personal idle-timeout auto-logout.
- [x] **24.1** Real per-user location code in the JWT (was hardcoded to `"HO"` for everyone).
- [x] **24.4** MFA brute-force rate limiting — audited, already satisfied.
- [x] **24.19** JWT gained `iat`/`jti` claims (stdlib only, not a `golang-jwt` dependency).
- [x] **24.22** `ParseToken` collapsed to one generic error message.
- [x] **24.27** Startup guard refuses to boot in `ENV=production` while the default admin seed credential is still active.
- [x] **24.28** Full password-reset flow via stdlib `net/smtp` — no enumeration oracle, token hash stored not raw.
- [x] **24.38** MFA Physical bypass — **DONE**, honestly scoped: host-shell access is an inherent, unpreventable privilege (raw SQL is always possible with DB access) — this closes the *silent/blanket/untraceable* part, not physical-access-implies-trust itself. `cmd/reset_mfa` rewritten: now requires `-schema`, `-user` (a specific username — `-all-admins` is an explicit opt-in for the old blanket behavior) and `-reason`; defaults to a dry run (`-yes` required to actually execute); writes a real `audit_logs` entry per reset with the same tamper-evident checksum chain (`auditChecksum`, mirroring `engines.LogAuditEvent`'s exact formula) every other MFA action leaves, capturing the OS username/hostname of whoever ran it in `details`.
- [x] **29.8.3 Live user-state re-check (session staleness).** `ParseToken` is pure HMAC and never touched the DB, so a deactivated user kept full access for the rest of `JWT_EXPIRY_HOURS` (24h default) and a demoted user's token kept asserting the old role. `apiMiddleware` now re-reads the user's row per request behind a 30s cache (`AUTH_STATE_CACHE_SECONDS`), with the DB authoritative for role **and** location. Chosen over a jti denylist because a denylist can't fix the role half at all. Invalidation hooked into all three mutation sites (admin set-status, admin set-location, `SyncEmployeeAccessLink`) so a deactivation bites on the next request, not at the end of the cache window. Extension tokens are skipped (no user row exists); MFA tokens are checked. A DB failure returns a retryable 503, explicitly **not** a 401 — a replica hiccup must not log everyone out.
- [x] **29.8.4 JWT signing-key rotation.** `JWT_SECRET_<n>`: highest number signs, every configured key verifies, so a planned rotation is add-key → wait one token TTL → delete-old-key with nobody logged out. Plain `JWT_SECRET` still works unchanged as the legacy key, and with no numbered key set the emitted token is **byte-identical** to before — inert until opted into. Verification deliberately tries all keys instead of selecting by the token's `kid`: `kid` lives inside the payload and is attacker-controlled until the HMAC has already passed, so using it to pick the trust anchor would mean trusting unverified input. `kid` is still emitted for ops visibility, just never load-bearing.
- [x] **32.5 MFA recovery path — BUILT AND CLOSED 2026-08-05.** Design decision (c) approved by the user 2026-08-05; built (c) plus the two adjacent gaps the original entry named, because recovery codes alone still leave a user signed in with a dead authenticator. Three parts, all live-verified against the real dev DB by four handler-level tests (`internal/server/mfa_recovery_test.go`, all passing):
  - **Single-use recovery codes.** 10 codes of 50 bits each (`engines/mfa_recovery.go`), issued at enrollment and shown display-once with copy/download + an acknowledgement gate before the app is entered (`public/index.html` `#mfa-recovery-screen`). Only the SHA-256 hash is stored, never the code — same posture as `engines/password_reset.go`'s reset tokens; SHA-256 rather than bcrypt because these are random high-entropy codes, not user-chosen passwords, which also makes redemption one indexed lookup instead of a bcrypt loop over every outstanding code. `/auth/mfa/verify` accepts one in place of a TOTP code; redemption is a single conditional `UPDATE ... WHERE used_at IS NULL` so two simultaneous logins cannot both spend the same code. New table `mfa_recovery_codes` (`db/migrations_stage32_5_mfa_recovery_codes.sql`, with the standard DO-block catch-up for existing tenant schemas).
  - **Authenticator re-enrollment** (the "move my authenticator to a new phone" flow the entry called out as impossible). New `users.mfa_pending_secret` column parks the new device's secret until a code from it is accepted, so the *existing* device keeps working throughout and an abandoned attempt cannot itself cause a lockout — asserted directly by `TestMFAReenrollMovesAuthenticator`. Re-auth is by password, not TOTP, deliberately: the user who needs this screen is the one whose authenticator is already gone.
  - **Admin reset** (`POST /api/v1/admin/users/reset-mfa`, HR/Admin only, "Reset 2FA" row action on the Users screen) for the colleague who lost both phone and codes. Clears enrollment *and* recovery codes and forces re-enrollment at next login — it does not disable MFA. Replaces the previous only-route of SSH + `cmd/reset_mfa` on a box with no Go toolchain.
  - Profile screen gained a Two-Factor Recovery panel: codes remaining (danger styling at zero, warning at ≤2), regenerate, start/cancel a device change. Signing in with a recovery code now also raises a toast naming the remaining count and pointing at that panel.
  - Note for the record: `handleMFAActivate`'s response gained a `recovery_codes` array, which broke two existing tests that decoded it into `map[string]string` — both updated to `map[string]interface{}` in `server_test.go`. Caught by running the suite, not by inspection.
  - *Original entry, kept for the diagnosis record (found 2026-08-04):* a lost/replaced admin phone locks the tenant out of every HR/Admin screen. Verified by reading the code, not assumed: the only MFA endpoints are `/auth/mfa/enroll`, `/activate`, `/verify` (`routes.go:115-117`), **there are no backup/recovery codes anywhere in the tree** (grep for `recovery_code`/`backup_code` returns nothing), and there is **no endpoint for one admin to reset another's MFA**. `handleMFAEnroll` is gated on `Resolved-Purpose == "mfa_enroll"`, a token `/api/v1/login` only issues to an account that is *not yet* enrolled — so an enrolled user **cannot re-enroll from inside the app**, i.e. there is no "move my authenticator to a new phone" flow. The only recovery is `cmd/reset_mfa` (host-shell + DB access), which on production means SSH to the droplet, and that box has **no Go toolchain**, so it needs a cross-compiled binary or a hand-run `UPDATE users SET mfa_enabled=false, mfa_secret=NULL`. With a single HR/Admin account on prod, that SSH key is the *only* way back in. Mitigations, cheapest first: (a) transfer the authenticator entry with the app's own export feature *before* switching phones — zero code, but only works while the old device still exists; (b) a second HR/Admin account enrolled on a different device, so a lost phone costs one login rather than all admin access; (c) the actual fix — issue single-use recovery codes at enrollment and accept one in place of a TOTP code at `/mfa/verify`. [needs design decision: (c) is the right fix but adds a credential to store and display-once UI — confirm before building]
  - Related dev-loop trap worth remembering: **`admin` is the one MFA-mandatory role, so it cannot be used for quick local verification** — use `manager1`/`cashier1` (see `DEV_CREDENTIALS.local.txt`). And the login/MFA rate budget is **5 requests per minute per IP** (`rateLimitCategory`, `middleware.go:168`), which covers `/login`, `/mfa/verify` *and* `/mfa/activate` — four wrong codes in half a minute puts the next attempts into 429 regardless of correctness. IPv4 `127.0.0.1` and IPv6 `::1` are **separate buckets**, so a curl test can pass while the browser is still throttled.

Listeners now capture (passive) and include `wheel`/`touchstart`, so scrolling inside a table or panel (scroll does not bubble) counts.

Built `internal/server/login_abuse.go`: backoff per typed name + address after 3 failures (2^(n-3) s, max 15 min, 429 + Retry-After, password unchecked inside the wait), dummy bcrypt for unknown names, a locked account passed by the right password from the owner's remembered MFA device (clears the lock), spray / distributed-guessing audit events (`LOGIN_ABUSE`) once per 15-minute window; in-memory, bounded. ### SEC › Security hardening & findings

- [x] **1.3 API security & gateway foundation**
  - Rate limiting (5/min login, 60/min standard CRUD)
  - Strict tenant resolution from a verified JWT (no IDOR leaks)
  - Parameterized SQL everywhere; allowlisted query-filter keys
  - 2MB body cap + file size/MIME validation
  - CORS allowlist (no wildcard); note: CSRF-token/cookie controls don't apply here — auth is a Bearer token, never a cookie, so classic CSRF has no attack surface
  - Secrets via env vars, no hardcoded keys
  - Object-level authorization (role/location/ownership checks on every read/write)
- [x] **12.2 IP & binary safety** — frontend minified/obfuscated, no sourcemap leak; release binaries stripped (9,446 KB → 6,602 KB).
  - Automated backups + encryption + monthly restore drills — **done** (Stage 17.3 backup/restore baseline + AES-256 encryption-at-rest, commit `99d63de`). This line stayed marked "re-opened" long after both gaps had actually closed.
- [x] **13.1 Security response headers** — HSTS/CSP/X-Frame-Options/X-Content-Type-Options via one `securityHeaders` middleware wrapping the whole mux.
- [x] **13.14 Per-category rate limiting** — keyed `ip:category` (login/bulk-upload/report/webhook/search/default) instead of just `ip`, fixing cross-endpoint interference.
- [x] **14.21-14.24 Security hardening** — CI wired to apply all Stage 14 migrations (was silently testing pre-Stage-14 schema); `govulncheck` baseline (30 reachable CVEs, all in the Go stdlib, none in this project's own 2 dependencies); account-level brute-force lockout (10 attempts / 15 min).
  - **Bug fixed**: lockout expiry compared a Postgres UTC timestamp against Go's local (IST) clock — a genuinely-expired lock looked ~5.5 hours in the future. Fixed by doing the whole comparison in SQL against Postgres's own clock.
  - Inbound Shopify webhook HMAC signature verification added.
- [x] **17.2 CSV formula-injection protection** — shared `sanitizeCSVCell`, applied to every import/export/error-file path.
- [x] **24.16** Debug panic endpoint gated to non-production.
- [x] **24.17** Schema-name allowlist before SQL interpolation.
- [x] **24.18** Stop silently swallowing JSON unmarshal errors — down from 27 occurrences to 1 safe one (left alone, file was mid-edit by a concurrent session).
- [x] **24.25-24.26** Upload content-type validation + CSRF — audited, already satisfied/not applicable.
- [x] **24.33** `_ = json.Unmarshal(...)` (ignored error) has crept back into production code since 24.18 — 5 current occurrences, two with real fail-open risk: `engines/transactional_validation.go:85` (malformed `PurchaseOrder.items` silently computes zero ordered-qty, which could let an over-receipt check pass incorrectly) and `internal/server/handlers_core_doc_engine.go:449` (malformed prior document data silently feeds `ValidateTransactionalRules` an empty prior-state, which could let an invalid status transition through). **DONE.** `fetchPOItemQuantities` now returns the real unmarshal error instead of a silently-empty map; its two callers (`validateGRNRules`'s PURCHA-0082/84/87/88 checks, `validateASNRules`'s ASN-0271 check) now distinguish `sql.ErrNoRows` (PO genuinely not found/no lines — still a legitimate skip) from any other error (now fails closed, rejecting the write) instead of collapsing both into the same silent skip. `handlers_core_doc_engine.go`'s prior-document-data unmarshal now returns a 500 instead of silently continuing with `priorData == nil`, which every edit-gate check downstream (`validatePurchaseOrderEditRules` etc.) would otherwise treat as "this is a create, nothing to gate." `engines/transactional_validation.go:212` and `engines/pim_content_versions.go:67` (lower-risk) and `internal/server/handlers_pim_pos_finance.go:130` (not a real risk) left as-is, per the original scoping. `go build`/`go vet`/`go test ./... -p 1` clean.
- [x] **24.35** Inbound webhook fail-open risk — **DONE.** `verifyShopifyWebhookSignature` (`internal/server/middleware.go`) now fails **closed**: an unset `SHOPIFY_WEBHOOK_SECRET` rejects the request (still logs a one-time warning) instead of skipping verification, matching `engines.VerifyWebhookHMAC`'s (BigCommerce) existing fail-closed posture. No test/script relied on the old fail-open behavior (grepped first).
- [x] **30.5.9 Soften the report rate limit for interactive browsing — closed 2026-07-31.** Budget raised 20 → 60/min, and the bucket is now keyed by `ip:category:session` instead of `ip:category`. The per-session half is the more important one: every user behind one NAT address — an office, a store router — used to draw down a single shared budget, so one person browsing the catalog could rate-limit their colleagues. The session key is a truncated SHA-256 of the bearer token (`sessionFingerprint`), not the resolved user id, because the limiter deliberately runs *before* authentication so an unauthenticated flood is still limited; a request with no token falls back to the original IP-only bucket. The 429 now carries a `detail` (via 30.2.4) naming the category, the limit, and the wait, instead of a bare "Too many requests".
- [x] **43.1** **Token claim delimiter smuggling — a live security defect, fixed.** The session-token payload was a flat `k=v&k=v` string built from columns (username, role, tenant, location_code) with no character restrictions; a crafted value containing `&`/`=` could forge `purpose`/`role`/`tenant` claims that still carried a valid HMAC signature — a working privilege-escalation and cross-tenant path (`requireHRAdmin`-gated, so insider-persistence rather than anonymous remote). Fixed with `url.QueryEscape`/`SplitN` at the one choke point every token kind already passes through (`ParseToken`).
- [x] **43.3** **`X-Forwarded-For` now parsed right-to-left against a trusted-proxy set.** The old left-most-entry parse was correct only for as long as Caddy's `trusted_proxies` config line stayed right, with a silent, total bypass of the login rate limiter as the failure mode. Walking right-to-left past known proxy hops means a forged header can't bypass the limiter even if that config ever drifts, and makes Cloudflare activation an env-var change rather than a code change.
- [x] **26.1.3a** Origin/proxy hardening and rate-limiting design — **engineering scope closed 2026-08-06**. Everything achievable without a public hostname is done:
  - `deploy/Caddyfile` rewritten as the real production proxy config: strips `Server`/`X-Powered-By`, caps request bodies at 12MB *before* they reach Go (the app's own limits are 2MB global / 10MB on the PIM upload route, so this is the outer bound), health-checks the upstream, sets proxy read/write timeouts to 90s — deliberately **above** the app's own 60s `WriteTimeout` so the proxy never truncates a long report export the server would have finished — and rolls access logs at 50MB × 10.
  - `trusted_proxies static private_ranges` in the global block. This is load-bearing rather than decorative: `TRUST_PROXY=1` is set on the box, so without it a client could forge `X-Forwarded-For` and defeat the app's per-IP rate limiting entirely. With it, Caddy replaces rather than appends the header.
  - **Two genuinely missing security headers added — in the app, not the proxy.** `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer` and a `Permissions-Policy` denying geolocation/microphone/camera/payment/usb were absent everywhere (`internal/server/middleware.go` already set HSTS/CSP/X-Frame-Options/nosniff). Attached at the existing `securityHeaders` choke point per CLAUDE.md's shared-choke-point principle, so they hold on the SSH-tunnel path too — which never touches Caddy, and is currently the *only* access path.
  - **Deliberately NOT done: rate limiting at the Caddy layer.** Caddy has no built-in rate limiter; the community `caddy-ratelimit` module requires rebuilding Caddy with `xcaddy` and maintaining a custom binary to keep patched — a new build toolchain on the box for something the app already does (Stage 13.14: 5/min/IP on the auth category, general per-IP budget elsewhere). Rejected as a poor trade under the lightweight-first principle, and the reasoning is written into `deploy/Caddyfile` so it isn't silently revisited.
  - This closes the repository-owned work. The production activation is tracked separately below so an external prerequisite is not misreported as unfinished engineering.

### SEC › Audit trail & retention

- [x] **1.2 Core engine logic**
  - Audit engine — DB triggers log every change (old/new value, user, time), append-only.
  - Panic handler middleware — captures crashes, writes stack traces to the log DB.
- [x] **24.20** Pagination on the audit logs endpoint.
- [x] **24.24** Audit log tamper-evidence (hash chain).
- [x] **47.7 Audit evidence, queryability and bounded legal retention** — closes A-07/A-30. **All of 47.7.1–47.7.8 built and green 2026-09-12.** Model chosen by the user 2026-09-09: **independently signed events + checkpoints**, not a serialized tenant chain.
  **Why that model, concretely.** What existed was the worst of both: `engines/logs.go` hashed each row's checksum from the *previous* row's — chain semantics — while deliberately not locking, and said so: *"Worst case under real concurrency is two rows briefly chaining from the same parent, not a broken tamper-evidence guarantee."* The second half of that sentence was wrong, and it is exactly the failure 47.7.2 names: sibling rows are what made the verifier report a break on perfectly clean data. **A verifier that cries wolf under normal load is worse than no verifier**, because it trains an operator to ignore it. Taking the lock instead would have serialized every audit write per tenant — on a table that takes a row on nearly every request — and Stage 47.3 had just finished making checkout deliberately concurrent. A per-tenant chain would have put a global serialization point back on every sale.
  - [x] **47.7.1** Evidence shape extended to what the item names: `entity_type`, `entity_id`, `correlation_id` (tying a row to the request *and* to 47.3's command-idempotency record), plus `signature` and `sig_version`. Trusted time is the row's own `created_at`, signed.
  - [x] **47.7.2** `engines/audit_evidence.go`. Each row signed over its **own** content with a length-prefixed canonical encoding (so `a|bc` and `ab|c` cannot collide), with **no dependency on any other row** — concurrency stops being a correctness question. The one thing per-row signatures cannot catch is **deletion**: remove a row and every survivor still verifies. Checkpoints close that — a digest over the ordered signatures in a definite `seq` range, so a missing row changes both the count and the digest. Checkpoints chain to each other (there are few, written by one job, so it costs nothing and gives the series a single verifiable head). Same shape as AWS QLDB digests and Certificate Transparency signed tree heads.
  - [x] **47.7.3** `WriteAuditEvidenceTx` writes evidence **inside the caller's transaction**, so evidence and mutation commit together or neither does — proven by a test that rolls back and asserts no row survives. This is the half the chain model could not do: reading "the last row" inside a business transaction is precisely what would deadlock or serialize against other in-flight sales.
  - [x] **47.7.4** **345,808 of 383,810 rows (90.1%, matching the audit's own ≈90% estimate) carry no checksum.** The tempting move — backfill them so the verifier reports 100% — is refused explicitly: a signature computed today proves only that the row exists today, and asserting otherwise converts a known gap into a false assurance an auditor would rely on. Instead: one boundary checkpoint seals the legacy range (their content is fixed **from the seal forward**), and every verification returns a `coverage_statement` saying in words that those rows predate the scheme and are **deliberately not counted as verified**. A test asserts that negative.
  - [x] **47.7.5** Four indexes, for the four access patterns the API actually issues: newest-first, by actor, by entity, by correlation. **No speculative index** — the item says so, and every index is a write cost on a table that takes a row on nearly every request.
  - [x] **47.7.6** Retention/legal-hold schema (`audit_retention_policy` versioned, `audit_legal_hold` scoped by entity/actor and outranking retention, shipped default 365 days hot with auto-deletion OFF) plus the archive itself, built 2026-09-12: `engines/audit_archive.go` — AES-256-GCM-encrypted, gzip-compressed archive files (`AUDIT_ARCHIVE_KEY`/`AUDIT_ARCHIVE_DIR` env vars, same key-management pattern as `channel_credentials.go`); one archive == exactly one checkpoint window, never partial; a held row (legal hold) blocks the *whole* window rather than fragmenting it. **Manifest-then-delete is literal**: the file is written and self-verified (re-decrypt, re-decompress, re-check the digest) *before* the archive row is recorded and the source rows deleted, all inside one transaction. Checkpoint verification (`verifyCheckpoints` in `audit_evidence.go`) is archive-aware: an archived window is verified against its archive file instead of the (now-empty) live table, so a legitimate archive is never mistaken for a deletion attack — the archive redirect still catches the archive file itself being deleted, corrupted or swapped. `GET/POST /api/v1/admin/audit-logs/archive(s)` + `/{id}`, `/{id}/export`, `/{id}/restore`; `StartAuditArchiveScheduler` runs daily on Stage 38.6's runner.
    **Incident during build (2026-09-11), fixed same-day, recorded so it isn't re-derived**: an early test version sealed a "boundary checkpoint" over all pre-existing history to isolate its own rows, then called the (correctly tenant-wide) `RunAuditArchive` with retention disabled — which archived that boundary checkpoint too, into `AUDIT_ARCHIVE_DIR=t.TempDir()`, deleted by Go at test exit. `tenant_default.audit_logs` dropped from ~389,000 rows to 334, unrecoverably (no usable backup — nearest was 2 months stale, and restoring it would have rolled back every other session's dev data). Root-caused and closed with four independent fixes, each verified by its own test: (1) tests now run against a freshly provisioned, single-use scratch tenant schema, never `tenant_default`; (2) `RunAuditArchive` refuses `archive_after_days` below a 30-day floor (`minArchiveAfterDays`) as a coded error, so a misconfigured policy can't reproduce this in production either; (3) `maxRowsPerArchiveWindow` (50,000, overridable only via an explicit `allow_large_windows` flag on the manual trigger) caps how large a window the *scheduled* pass will process unattended; (4) `ensureArchiveDirReady` refuses a non-absolute, non-existent or unwritable `AUDIT_ARCHIVE_DIR` before anything is read, rather than discovering it mid-pass. **Two related security gaps found in peer review, also fixed**: a checkpoint's `archive_id` isn't covered by its own `signCheckpoint` signature, so a DB-write attacker could repoint it at an unrelated archive (closed by an explicit checkpoint-id match check) or — the sharper version — at its *own* previously-restored archive after deleting the live rows again (closed by having `RestoreAuditArchive` **delete** the archive manifest row, inside the same transaction as restoring the rows and logging the restore itself as a signed audit event, rather than flagging it with a mutable, unsigned `restored_at` column — so the repoint is refused by `audit_checkpoints.archive_id`'s own foreign key, not merely by an app-level check that a second UPDATE could bypass). 21 orphaned `audit_archives` rows (dead references to the deleted temp files) remain in `tenant_default`, left for a deliberate operator cleanup rather than an agent-run `DELETE` against the shared dev DB.
    13 tests in `engines/audit_archive_test.go`, all green in isolation: the full write→verify→query→export→restore drill; legal hold blocking a whole window (and respecting scope — a non-matching hold does not block); archive-file tamper detected via the checkpoint redirect; the repoint-after-restore attack failing on the foreign key; the oversized-window ceiling (and its override); the archive-dir safety check (relative path refused; unwritable directory skipped where the OS/filesystem cannot make that genuine).
  - [x] **47.7.7** Checkpoint and verification run as jobs on **Stage 38.6's durable runner** (retries, DLQ, visibility screen already there) rather than a bespoke ticker — 47.11.4 names every bespoke ticker as something to migrate *onto* that runner, so adding one here would move the wrong way. `StartAuditEvidenceScheduler` only *enqueues*, hourly, idempotent per tenant-hour. **47.7.7's subtle half is implemented**: `AuditVerificationOverdue` alerts on verification that did not *happen*, not only on verification that *failed* — absence of a failure is not evidence of success, and a stopped verifier is exactly the state an administrator-level attacker would engineer.
  - [x] **47.7.8** `engines/audit_evidence_test.go` — 24 concurrent writers all verify (the false-positive case that drove the model choice); direct SQL tamper detected; a row deleted from inside a sealed window detected *by the checkpoint*; legacy rows sealed-not-fabricated; key rotation **not** mistaken for tampering; overdue-verification silence detected; evidence rolled back with its transaction. **A real bug was found by these tests and fixed**: Postgres `TIMESTAMP` stores microseconds while `time.Now()` carries nanoseconds, so the value signed differed from the value stored and *every freshly written row failed its own signature*. Caught because the tamper test reported a row as tampered before anything had touched it.
  - **Acceptance: met.** Coverage and limitations are explicit and machine-readable; concurrent clean data verifies; tamper and deletion are both detected (live table or archive, whichever is authoritative for that window); the measured query patterns are indexed; the archive/restore drill is built and tested. The conditional-claim register (`engines/environment.go`) is updated rather than cleared — the legacy coverage boundary is a permanent factual limitation of this data set and an auditor must be told, not left to discover it. **Not yet done:** the 47.7.6 migration (`db/migrations_stage47_7_6_audit_archive.sql`) and the three new Go files are uncommitted, deliberately kept separate from `7f5fadf`'s Stage 47.5/47.7-core/48/49 commit while the incident above was being fixed; the 21 orphaned `audit_archives` rows in `tenant_default` (dev only) are unreviewed cleanup, not yet done.

Store before, after, actor and reason for every allowed post-sale edit, with a report. The reprint log is 71.7(h). [rows: Bill edit/change history P1, Void/cancel/reprint P1]

- [x] **38.5** Idempotency keys on every mutating public endpoint — **required, not optional**: a retry after a timeout is the normal case for any network integration, and without a key the server cannot tell a retry from a second genuine request. The unique index on `(credential_id, idempotency_key)` *is* the lock, so two concurrent retries cannot both proceed however they are scheduled. A `request_fingerprint` (SHA-256 of method+path+body) means the same key with a **different** body is a 409, never a replay — answering a question the caller did not ask would be worse than no idempotency at all. A `5xx` is deliberately **not** stored: the claim is released so a retry after a server error is a genuine second attempt. Keys expire on `platform.public_api_idempotency_retention_hours` (default 24) and are then reclaimable. A panic releases the claim rather than wedging the caller out for the whole retention window. Exercised through direct engine tests rather than a route, since the first public slice is read-only — the guarantee has to be proven **before** the first mutating endpoint relies on it, not after.

- [x] **29.7.1 O1 — gl_postings reporting index.** `db/migrations_stage29_gl_postings_reporting_index.sql` adds `idx_gl_postings_account_created` on `(account_code, created_at) INCLUDE (debit, credit, cost_center)`, backfilled into every existing `tenant_%` schema (new tenants inherit it via `ProvisionTenantSchema`'s `LIKE ... INCLUDING ALL`). **The QC report's literal recommendation — a bare `(account_code, created_at)` — was measured and does not work**: on a seeded 1M-row `gl_postings` the planner produced a byte-identical Seq Scan plan with the bare index present and absent, because the reports need `debit`/`credit` per row and a non-covering index means a heap visit per row, which costs more than the seq scan it would replace. The `INCLUDE` payload is what makes the plans flip to index-only scans (`Heap Fetches: 0`). Backfill guard matches on index *definition*, not name, because `LIKE ... INCLUDING ALL` does not preserve index names — a name-only `IF NOT EXISTS` would have built a second redundant copy on any tenant provisioned after the migration.
- [x] **29.7.2 O1 (part 2) — sargable date predicates, without which the index is inert.** Nine gl_postings report queries spelled their range as `created_at::date BETWEEN $1 AND $2`; the cast wraps the indexed column in a function call so it can never be a range seek. Rewritten to the equivalent half-open `created_at >= $1::date AND created_at < ($2::date + 1)` in `finance_reports_stage26.go` (P&L, balance sheet, cash flow, tax ledger, statutory export), `gl_cost_center.go` (cost-centre P&L), `reports.go` (`glAccountNetBalance`, GST txn count) and `report_definitions.go` (`gstReturnDrillDown`). The convention is documented once at the top of `finance_reports_stage26.go` so new queries follow it. **The index and this rewrite only pay off together** — neither is worth shipping alone.

### UI › Navigation, menus & shortcuts

- [x] **21.3** Icon-minimal sidebar (26 per-item icons removed, user's explicit choice).
- [x] **21.7** Sidebar scroll-position bug (found live) — fixed to center the active item instead of snapping to an edge.
- [x] **21.11 Standard-ERP module renaming** — **DONE (2026-07-22).** Odoo/ERPNext-style naming for the ~12 top-level sidebar labels (POS→Point of Sale, Finance→Accounting, etc.), individual screen names left alone.
- [x] **27.6** Server-side SPA path fallback (`internal/server/routes.go`) — a small loop over `engines.ProductPackages` registers `GET /<prefix>` and `GET /<prefix>/{rest...}` serving `public/index.html`, so a direct/bookmarked hit on `/wms`, `/pims`, etc. works against the plain `http.FileServer` that would otherwise 404 it. Adding a future product to the map gets a working URL automatically.
- [x] **27.7** Frontend entitlement-aware nav (`public/app.js`/`public/styles.css`) — `MENU_MODULE_MAP` + `applyModuleEntitlements()` mirror the existing role-based `MENU_PERMISSION_MAP`/`applySidebarPermissions()` exactly (own `module-hidden` CSS class so the two filters can't clobber each other), hiding sidebar items whose module is disabled and collapsing an emptied flyout. `applyProductPathRouting()` silently rewrites bare `/` to a single-product tenant's own URL via `history.replaceState` (never a reload, never an access-control decision - `moduleGate` is still the only real enforcement). A minimal `renderProductSwitcher()` (plain `<select>`, `history.pushState`) appears only for a tenant with 2+ products but not the full suite. **Real bug found and fixed during live-browser verification**: `owned_packages` initially listed every package for a full-suite tenant too (such a tenant technically satisfies every individual package's requirements), incorrectly showing the switcher - fixed with `engines.IsFullSuite`, which suppresses `owned_packages` when a tenant has the complete module set.
- [x] **29.5 Flyout hover navigation** — sidebar and Schema Designer module flyouts now open as soon as the pointer reaches the module row/arrow, with the same behavior on keyboard focus; click remains available for touch devices. The sidebar stacking layer is above sticky table headers, so the full menu stays visible and clickable over table UI.
- [x] **28.5.2 Sidebar submenu closing before it could be used / clicks doing nothing.** Reported as "in POS nothing is working, if I click anything it is not opening anything". Not a routing bug — every menu handler was correctly bound (verified by clicking all 38 sidebar entries programmatically: 37/38 navigated, the 1 being Dashboard already being the current view). The flyout was disappearing out from under the pointer, so the click landed on the page behind it. **Four distinct causes**, each confirmed by a scripted pointer-path repro before and after: (a) the hide timer was per-container but called the *global* `closeSubmenus()`, so sliding from module A to B left A's timer running and it shut B 200ms later — replaced with one shared timer that any open cancels; (b) the 8px gap between the sidebar row and the flyout panel is outside the container's box, so crossing it (or pausing in it, which reaching for a submenu item requires) fired `mouseleave` and started the close — added an invisible `.menu-flyout-bridge` hit area, a child of the container, spanning exactly that gap; (c) `mouseleave` was bound alongside `pointerenter`, and pointer events fire *ahead* of their compatibility mouse events, so the leave handler ran **after** the next row's enter handler had already cancelled the pending close and scheduled a fresh one nothing cancelled — both sides are now `pointer*`; (d) sibling entries with no flyout of their own (Dashboard/Reports/Manufacturing/PIM) had no listeners at all, so they were dead zones where a close scheduled on the way past went through unopposed. Added on top: hovering a *different* module now requires a 140ms dwell before it takes the open menu (500ms if the pointer is measurably travelling *towards* the open panel), so a diagonal reach across intervening rows no longer steals it; sidebar scroll repositions the open flyout instead of closing it; Escape closes; a click on the module row can no longer close a menu the user just hovered open (only a second, deliberate click on an already-pinned row does).
- [x] **28.5.3 Long flyouts running off the bottom of the screen.** Found while verifying 28.5.2, same interaction. `openFlyout` capped a flyout's height to the space *below* its trigger, so Stock's 12 screens (and Setup's ~25 master doctypes) anchored low in the sidebar put their last items off-screen — reachable only by scrolling inside the panel, and in practice not reachable at all because the pointer had to leave the panel to get there. It now takes its natural height and slides up to keep its bottom on screen, scrolling internally only when taller than the whole viewport. Verified: all 12 Stock items on screen at a 900px viewport (last item bottom 751 of 900).
- [x] **28.5.4 Global search did nothing.** The top-bar box promised "Search menu, category, type or HSN" but only filtered the table you already had open — on the dashboard, or any non-table screen, typing had no effect at all. Added `setupGlobalSearchSuggest()`: an index built from the live sidebar DOM (every destination, including the ones only reachable by hovering the right module) plus every registered record type, matched with label-hits ranked above module-hits, rendered in a dropdown reusing the existing `.typeahead-menu`/`.typeahead-item` vocabulary. Picking one dispatches a click on the real sidebar element wherever one exists, so routing/permission-filtering/active-item highlighting stay in one place instead of being duplicated. Keyboard (↑/↓/Enter/Escape), mouse, an explicit empty state, and a dedupe so a record type the sidebar already lists as a screen doesn't appear twice. The pre-existing table filtering is untouched and still runs alongside. Permission- and entitlement-hidden entries are excluded because the index reads the same `perm-hidden`/`module-hidden` classes the sidebar itself uses.
- [x] **28.5.5 Follow-up: click-to-open needed two or three clicks, and a parked cursor didn't bring the menu back.** Reported straight after 28.5.2 shipped, and both were caused by that same change. (a) The click handler 28.5.2 added was a *toggle* — a row you had already hovered open closed on the click, so it read as "click it two or three times before it sticks". A module row now only ever **opens**; closing is moving away, clicking outside the nav, or Escape. The `flyoutPinned` bookkeeping that toggle needed is gone. (b) While the pointer rests on a row, `pointerenter` never fires again, so anything that closed the menu in the meantime — navigating away from it, an outside click, Escape, or the sidebar re-rendering and replacing the DOM node under a stationary cursor — left it shut with the cursor still sitting right there. `pointermove` on the container now re-opens when nothing is open, so the smallest movement brings it straight back. Verified 8/8 on a dedicated repro (one click opens while another module is showing; second and third clicks keep it open; outside-click closes; cursor-still-on-row reopens; parked 3s without moving stays open; one click reopens after navigating away), with the 34/34 navigation pass and the three original flyout scenarios re-run green.
- [x] **29.9.1 Module-level renames applied.** `public/index.html` sidebar labels + `public/app.js` matching hardcoded page titles/tooltip text + `docs/guides/USER_SOP.md`/`USER_GUIDE.md`/`UAT_CHECKLIST.md`/`ADMIN_SOP.md` breadcrumbs, all updated together so code and docs don't drift: Accounting→**Financial Accounting**, Buying→**Procurement**, Point of Sale→**POS**, HR & Assets→**HRM**, Purchase Orders→**Purchase Order**, Sales Invoices→**Sales Invoice**, Vendor Invoices→**Vendor Invoice**, Customers→**Customer** (Fulfillment flyout), Goods Receipt (GRN)→**Goods Receipt**, Transfers→**Stock Transfer**, Bin Master→**Bin**. Internal ids/module_keys left unchanged (same convention as the 21.11 renames) — display text only, no schema/route change, zero risk to existing data or bookmarked state.
- [x] **29.9.2 "Settings" (module-admin) vs. "Setup" (menu-master-definition) collision — user decided: keep admin module as "Settings".** No rename applied; `menu-master-definition` keeps its existing "Setup" label unchanged. No code change needed — both labels were already correct as-is.
- [x] **29.9.4 "Order Management" → "Sales Order" — user decided: keep "Order Management".** No rename applied — it accurately describes the broader channel-order-through-invoice workbench (`renderOMSWorkbenchView`).
- [x] **32.1.1 The sidebar's hover "aim test" was structurally always-true — closed 2026-08-04.** Root cause of the whole hover complaint. `pointerAimingAtOpenFlyout()` decided whether a module row must be dwelt on for 140ms or 500ms before it may take the open menu, and it asked `flyoutPointerTrail.dx > 0 && r.left >= flyoutPointerTrail.x`. The flyout panel **always** sits to the right of the sidebar, so `r.left >= x` is true for essentially every pointer position in the nav; the whole decision therefore collapsed to `dx > 0`, measured **frame-to-frame**, which at 120Hz is a sub-pixel sample dominated by hand jitter. Result: hovering a module while another menu was open waited **500ms on roughly half of all approaches, at random**. Replaced with a real trajectory test — velocity sampled over a 90ms window, a 12px minimum travel to count as a deliberate reach, and the pointer's projected crossing point required to land inside the panel's **vertical** span (±24px) before the grace applies.
- [x] **32.1.2 The pending open re-evaluates instead of locking in — closed 2026-08-04.** The delay was chosen once at `pointerenter` and then ran to term: `container`'s `pointermove` handler was guarded by `!flyoutOpenTimer`, so while a timer was pending every subsequent move was a no-op. A pointer that had stopped aiming still served the full aim grace. Dwell is now measured from a `hoverStart` stamp and recomputed on every move, so the required wait only ever counts **down** — stop aiming and the menu opens on the next move.
- [x] **32.1.3 Open-timer ownership — closed 2026-08-04.** `cancelFlyoutOpen()` was global, so row B's `pointerleave` could cancel an open row C had already scheduled. It now takes an optional owner (`flyoutOpenTarget`) and leaves another row's pending open alone.
- [x] **32.1.4 Delays cut to what the gesture actually needs — closed 2026-08-04.** Switch 140 → **60ms** (below the ~100ms that reads as instant; it exists only to stop a fast sweep down the sidebar strobing every menu), aim grace 500 → **220ms**, hide 260 → **200ms**. The blanket dwell was doing the job the aim test was supposed to do, which is why it had to be so long.
- [x] **32.1.9 The "AllocationRule needs two clicks" report, root-caused and reproduced — closed 2026-08-04.** From the user's screen recording: the frame at 15.25s shows **Stock's flyout open under the pointer while the page and the highlighted row are HR** — a menu belonging to one module while the app sits on another. That is the pre-28.5 defect exactly: `hideTimer` was **per-container** but `closeSubmenus()` is **global**, so module A's already-armed 200ms timer fires after B's menu has opened and closes it; the menu vanishes from under the pointer and the click lands on the page behind it. The Setup flyout is the worst case (longest list, anchored lowest, so `maxHeight = availableBelow` forces internal scrolling and a long pointer journey). Reproduced mechanically by replaying the gesture — hover module A, move to module B, travel into B's flyout, click: **deployed build 0/6 first clicks registered, local tree 6/6.**
- [x] **45.1** **Duplicate panels on Vendor Invoice / Payment Proposals / Bank Reconciliation.** Root cause was a re-entrancy gap in the shared router, not anything view-specific: `renderView()` (app.js) cleared `#view-root` and showed a placeholder synchronously, then `await`ed the view's own fetch before appending its header/panel — so a second call fired before the first one's fetch resolved (double-click, or any duplicate trigger) would clear the first call's placeholder but not stop the first call from still appending its content afterwards, landing both calls' output side by side, permanently. Fixed with a `viewRenderToken` counter: each call renders into a **detached scratch container**, and only swaps it into the live `#view-root` if its token is still current when its fetch resolves — a stale call's content is discarded outright instead of ever touching the visible DOM. The existing Chromium sticky-header-caching workaround (`requestAnimationFrame(() => root.offsetHeight)`) and the `translateDOM` sweep moved from `renderViewContent` into `renderView`'s token-gated `finally`, since both need to run against the real root post-swap, not the scratch container. Affects every one of the ~45 views dispatched through this router, not just the three that happened to get screenshotted.
- [x] **45.2** **Module tab bars (PIM/Finance/Reports/HR/Manufacturing) silently clipped instead of scrolling.** `.page-container` is `overflow-x: hidden`, and each module's tab-bar row (`tabBar.style.display = 'flex'`, no wrap, no scroll of its own) is a bare unwrapped flex row — so at a narrow enough width/zoom (reported: 90%), trailing tabs (e.g. PIM's "Supplier Submissions") weren't just hard to find, they were **unreachable through the UI**, with no scrollbar, no wrap, and no recovery path short of resizing the window or knowing the direct URL. Fixed by giving each of the 5 tab-bar rows its own `overflow-x: auto`, scoped to the row rather than widening `.page-container`'s own overflow behaviour (which risked introducing a page-wide horizontal scrollbar for unrelated wide content elsewhere).
  - **The first version of this fix was verified live and found to make it worse: the tab bar collapsed to `height: 0`, fully invisible.** `.page-container` is a `flex-direction: column` container; `overflow-x: auto` alone suppresses a flex item's automatic min-height (content-based sizing only applies when overflow is `visible`, and per the CSS Overflow spec the *used* value of the other axis becomes `auto` regardless of what's declared) — so whenever the page's other content was tall enough to overflow vertically, the tab bar had nothing stopping it shrinking to nothing. **Fixed with `flex-shrink: 0`**, which exempts the item from shrinking at all rather than trying to win the automatic-minimum-size calculation. `overflow-y: visible` was added alongside it on the theory that it would stop the axis-pairing rule from firing — **live measurement disproved that theory** (`getComputedStyle` still reports `overflow-y: auto` even with `visible` explicitly declared); it's harmless and documents intent but `flex-shrink: 0` is what's actually doing the work. Re-verified live after the correction: normal width unchanged, narrow width shows a real non-zero-height scrollable bar (measured 46px, vs 0px before) with "Supplier Submissions" reachable by scroll.
- [x] **45.4** **Setup flyout submenu, two visual fixes.** (a) Group headers (CRM/CORE/FINANCE/HR/…) had no background, just bold muted text sitting directly on the flyout's own background — gave `.submenu-group-label` a solid chip (`var(--bg-color)`, rounded) so groups read as distinct bands. (b) The sticky "Filter setup lists…" search box leaked scrolling list text through its bottom border at fractional zoom/DPR — the exact class of bug Stage 41.2 already diagnosed and fixed for the table `<th>` (`border-bottom` alone leaves a hairline gap; needs `box-shadow: inset` to seal it), just not applied here. Same fix, same file, reused rather than reinvented.

Reset clears, in order: every `erp_swr_*` entry in sessionStorage (the stale-while-revalidate cache behind every list/metadata read — collected into an array *before* deleting, since removing while iterating by index reindexes and silently skips every other key), `erp_nav_state`, the in-memory `state` caches, the POS till via the new silent `clearPOSTillState()` (split out of `resetPOSTerminal` so the two resets cannot drift), then re-fetches labels/doctypes/permissions and re-renders.
- [x] **53.17b Three deliberate non-actions, each a data-safety call rather than an omission.** (1) **Reset refuses to run at all while offline POS sales are queued**, with a message naming the count — `erp_pos_offline_queue` holds *completed sales that have not reached the server*, the customer has walked out with the goods, and that is not cache. Same posture `closePOSSessionFlow` already takes for the same reason. The guard runs *before* the confirm dialog, since there is no point confirming an action that must not proceed. (2) **It does not sign the user out** — resetting a screen must not eject a cashier mid-shift. (3) **It does not reset the theme** — a personal preference is not stale data. Every storage read/write is wrapped in try/catch (private browsing, quota, disabled storage): a cache that cannot be read cannot be stale either, so none of those is a failure worth stopping for.

### UI › Screen layout & window fit

- [x] **33.1.1 Every dialog in the app could be taller than the screen with no way to scroll — closed 2026-08-04.** The real defect behind "nothing is visible". `.modal-container` had **no `max-height` and no scroll region**, and `body` is `overflow: hidden`. So a form taller than the viewport got centred by `.modal-overlay`'s flexbox and then clipped off **both** ends — the first fields *and* the Save/Cancel footer were unreachable, with nothing anywhere to scroll. The container is now a flex column bounded by `calc(100dvh - 40px)` (with a `vh` fallback line), the header and footer are `flex: 0 0 auto`, and `.modal-body` takes the overflow (`flex: 1 1 auto; min-height: 0; overflow-y: auto`). `min-height: 0` is the load-bearing part — without it a flex child refuses to shrink below its content and the container overflows again. Also added `padding: 20px 16px` to the overlay so the dialog can never touch the viewport edge.
- [x] **33.1.2 The `<form>` wrapper was swallowing the flex chain — closed 2026-08-04.** Found by the harness, not by reading: 33.1.1 alone still failed at ≤1280x720. In `index.html` most dialogs wrap body+footer in `<form>`, so the **form** is the container's flex child, not `.modal-body` — the form stayed a content-sized block, the body never received leftover height to scroll in, and the footer was clipped exactly as before. Fixed with `.modal-container > form { display: flex; flex-direction: column; flex: 1 1 auto; min-height: 0 }`, written as `> form` so the handful of JS-built modals that put `.modal-body` directly in the container are unaffected.
- [x] **33.1.3 The generic document form is a 1/2/3-column intrinsic grid — closed 2026-08-04.** `openDynamicModal()` (every master and document create/edit screen) is the one dialog with an unbounded field count — Item renders ~20, and one column made it taller than any screen. `#dynamic-modal-body` is now `grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(min(240px, 100%), 1fr))`: **no breakpoints and no media queries** — the column count follows the width actually available, which is exactly what makes it zoom-proof (zoom only changes the CSS-pixel viewport, and both the grid and the `dvh` bound are recomputed from it). Scoped to `#dynamic-modal-body`, so the table/summary modals that share `.modal-body` are untouched.
- [x] **33.1.4 Wide dialog is opt-in above 4 fields; composite editors span the row — closed 2026-08-04.** A 3-field master in a 920px box would be two-thirds empty row, so `openDynamicModal` sets `.modal-container-wide` only above 4 fields; below that the dialog stays 520px and the 240px grid minimum yields one column on its own, i.e. **small masters look exactly as they did**. The JSONTable/JSONMap line editors (30.5.3) get `.form-group-wide` → `grid-column: 1 / -1`, since squeezing a multi-column table into a 240px track defeats the point. Column count itself stays the stylesheet's job; the field count is the only thing JS needed to know.
- [x] **33.1.5 Same fix applied to the second dialog system — closed 2026-08-04.** `.custom-dialog-box` (`showCustomAlert`/`showCustomConfirm`/`showApiError`/`showCustomPrompt`) had the identical structure and the identical bug: a long `showApiError` detail list clipped off-screen with its OK button unreachable. Given the same flex column, `dvh` bound, pinned header/footer and scrolling body. Verified with a 40-row error list.
- [x] **33.1.6 Cache-buster versions bumped — closed 2026-08-04.** `index.html` referenced `styles.css?v=14` / `app.js?v=20`; both files changed, so a browser holding the old query string would have served the **cached pre-fix files and shown no change at all** — including on production behind the tunnel. Now `?v=15` / `?v=20`. Note this also covers Stage 32.1's `app.js` edits, which never bumped it. **Any future change to either file must bump its `?v=`** or the fix ships invisibly.
- [x] **45.5** **Help icon button (top-right "?") reused text-button padding.** `.btn`'s base `padding: 8px 14px` / `gap: 8px` is sized for an icon+label pair like "Sync" next to it; on a single icon with no label it read as a stretched rectangle. New `.btn-icon` modifier (`padding: 8px`, `gap: 0`) applied to `#help-btn` — square footprint, same border/hover treatment as every other `.btn-outline`.

  - **Bug fixed**: `openMenu()` called `closeMenu()` to clear stale results, which also wiped the just-fetched results — the menu could never render.
  - **Bug fixed (pre-existing, Stage 17.9)**: Location/LegalEntity/Department/CostCenter were gated to a `'core'` module never registered anywhere — every role got 403 on every read/write since Stage 17.9 shipped.
  - **Gap flagged, not fixed**: Store Manager/Cashier lack read access to Vendor/Item/Customer, so the pickers are code-correct but not usable by those roles.
  - Verified live via Playwright against the real dev DB.
- [x] **30.5.1 Empty pickers now name the record type and link to where one is created — closed 2026-08-01.** Attached at the two shared choke points rather than per screen: the generic form's **Link** field (one site, covering every Link on every one of the 53 Setup doctypes) and **`attachTypeahead`** (a zero-match search used to close the menu silently, which is indistinguishable from "the search has not run"; it now shows a non-selectable row naming the doctype with a **create one** link). Employee's five HR `<select>`s get it via `employeePickerHint()`, since they build options as an HTML string and cannot use the Link path. New shared vocabulary — `openSetupDoctype()`, `setupLink()`, `emptyPickerHint()` — plus `.empty-state-hint`/`.empty-state-link` in the token-based CSS, so it themes for free. **Live-verified**: opening New Leave with zero Employees renders *"— No Employee records yet —"* in the select and *"No Employee records exist yet — create one first."* under it, with a working link.
- [x] **30.5.3 Two new fieldtypes, one generic line editor, six fields converted — closed 2026-08-01.** `JSONTable` (array of row objects) and `JSONMap` (key/value object) join the six existing fieldtypes. **The column spec lives in `doctype_fields.options`, not in JavaScript** — same reasoning as 30.6.4's `auto_generated`: a doctype/field list kept in `app.js` is a second source of truth that drifts the first time anyone adds a field. Adding a line editor to a new field is now one migration row and no code. The editor is a UI layer over a **hidden input carrying the field's own name**, so `handleDynamicFormSubmit` needed no change at all and the stored value is byte-identical to what a user used to hand-type — every Go consumer (`explodeBOMComponents`, `fetchRoutingOperations`, `byProducts`, `applyReportCatalogSavedFilter`) reads exactly what it read before. Link columns render a live typeahead, which also gives them 30.5.1's affordance for free. **These fields previously had no validation of any kind**: `validateJSONTableValue` now rejects malformed JSON and names the offending line and column for a missing required value (a malformed *spec* deliberately fails open — a configuration typo must not lock a tenant out of a doctype). Every key was read off the Go struct that consumes it, not off the old label text. **Live-verified over HTTP**: a malformed `components` is refused with GLOBAL-0002, a line missing `qty` with *"Field \"Components\" line 2 is missing \"Qty per Unit\""*; in the browser the editor serialises `[{"sku":"SKU-A","qty":2},{"sku":"SKU-B","qty":3,"scrap_percent":5}]` from four typed cells. A pre-existing value the editor cannot parse is shown in a raw-JSON escape hatch rather than silently emptied.
- [x] **30.5.8 Consistency sweep — closed 2026-08-02.** Add the missing typeahead on `pos-return-location`, `mkt-manifest-location`, `user-location` (siblings all have one); group the 103-entry Location typeahead by `type`; settle employee pickers on one control (`<select>` in HR vs typeahead in `asset-custodian`); ~~auto-generate the hand-typed `Attendance Code` / `Transfer Number` / `Claim Number`~~ **(done in 30.6, 2026-08-01 — along with 9 more the audit hadn't listed; `cart_number` is POS-session state, not a document number, so it stays out)**; give the icon-only row Edit/Delete buttons visible labels or aria-labels.
  - **Partly closed by 30.5.7 (2026-08-01)**: the icon-only row Edit/Delete buttons now carry `aria-label`s naming the record they act on, so that half of the sweep is done. The typeahead, Location grouping and employee-picker-consistency halves are still open.
  - **The root cause was that there was no one place to be consistent in.** All 42 picker call sites configured `attachTypeahead` themselves, so "how a Location is chosen" was decided 15 separate times — which is how the three missing ones went unnoticed. Rather than patch the three, every bespoke call site now goes through one door, **`attachLinkTypeahead(el, doctype, opts)`**, which merges in per-doctype defaults from a single `TYPEAHEAD_DOCTYPE_OPTS` table before delegating to the unchanged engine. The generic record form's Link field and a JSONTable's link column route through the same door, so they inherit every picker improvement for free — a Location Link on a Setup doctype is now grouped without anyone having edited that screen. The table is presentation only; it declares no schema, and a doctype missing from it simply takes the unadorned default.
  - **Two new opt-in options on `attachTypeahead`**, both off by default so the other ~35 pickers are untouched. `groupBy` renders a heading per distinct value — Location gets `groupBy: 'type'`. Group order is **first-appearance, not a hardcoded `Store,Warehouse,HO` list**, so a tenant that adds a fourth Location type gets it grouped with no code change; a record whose group field is missing/null/empty forms one unheaded bucket that sorts last rather than rendering a heading reading `undefined`. `showAllOnFocus` opens the menu on focus with an empty query, so a picker can be *browsed* and not only searched.
  - **The subtle part is index alignment.** `highlight()` and `pick()` address rows by index into `items`, so grouping reorders the `items` array itself rather than only the DOM, and headings/notes are deliberately **not** `.typeahead-item` — otherwise arrow-keying past a heading would select the wrong record. Verified explicitly: ArrowDown ×3 across two heading boundaries picks the 3rd *record*.
  - **Employee settled on the typeahead**, being the control ~35 other pickers already use. The five HR `<select>`s (Attendance, Leave, Payroll, Loans, Expenses) are now one shared `employeePickerField()`; `employeeOptions()`/`employeePickerHint()` are gone. Nothing is lost: `showAllOnFocus` keeps the "show me everyone without typing" affordance a dropdown had, 30.5.1's empty-state guidance actually *improves* (a static hint underneath becomes a focus-triggered dead-end row that links to where an Employee is created), the stored value is byte-identical (`code` is mandatory on Employee, so `valueFields` resolves to exactly what `e.code || e.id` sent), and validation is unaffected — `employee_id` is a Link, so a non-existent id is refused with META-0198 whichever control typed it. **Side benefit**: the whole Employee list used to be fetched on every HR tab render purely to build `<option>`s, *including for the eight tabs with no employee picker at all*, plus a parallel fetch on the Expenses screen. Both are gone.
  - **A browse that fills its page now says so** — "Showing the first 50 — type to search the rest." Without it, replacing a `<select>` that listed everyone with a menu showing 50 would let a user conclude the tenant has 50 employees.
  - **The aria-label half went wider than the item's wording.** 30.5.7 had done the row Edit/Delete pair; this pass found the other icon-only buttons had only a `title`, which is the weakest accessible-name fallback and is skipped by several screen readers. Labelled: the seven row actions in `renderDocTable` (Submit for Approval ×3, Send/Receive Subcontractor, Merge Customer, History), the Approval Rules edit/delete pair, and the five `modal-close` buttons in `index.html`. The biggest one was **`copyableCell()`** — one shared helper rendering ~30 copy chips per record list, every one of them announcing "Copy, button" with no indication of which row; it now names the value (`Copy LOC-0001`), fixed once at the helper.
  - **Verified**: 6 unit tests over the grouping helpers (run against the shipped source, not a copy) and **26 live browser checks** against a real Store Manager session — the three new pickers open grouped menus, multi-type grouping clusters correctly with the untyped row last, keyboard nav survives heading boundaries, typing-to-search is unregressed, all five employee pickers browse on focus and store the code, and every icon-only button on a record list carries a label.
  - **Incidental bug found and fixed while verifying**: `renderExecDashboard` did `document.getElementById('exec-dashboard-cards').appendChild(...)` with no null check. Reports is `DEFAULT_VIEW`, so it runs on every login, and navigating away before its fetches land detaches that container — an uncaught `TypeError` every time. Guarded the same way its own sibling `renderExecDashboardTrendChart` already guarded its container. Unrelated to this item; caught because the browser run asserts on uncaught page errors.
  - **Swept the rest of that defect class (2026-08-04)** rather than leaving it at the one instance the browser run happened to trip over. `app.js` has 352 chained `document.getElementById('x').y` dereferences, which is far too many to guard blindly and mostly harmless — the common pattern is *set `container.innerHTML`, then wire the elements you just created*, where the element provably exists. The dangerous shape is narrower: a deref **after an `await`**, of an element **this function did not create**. Scripted that filter over every one of the 216 async functions; it returned **14 sites in 8 functions**, and reading each one classified them:
    - **3 genuinely reachable, now guarded** — `submitWaveAssign`, `submitRequestRecount`, `saveReportCatalogFilter`. Each refills a form field after its request lands, so navigating away mid-request threw. The request itself had already succeeded in every case; only the convenience refill is now skipped.
    - **4 false positives** in `createASN`: the `getElementById` calls are *arguments* to the `apiFetch` call, so they evaluate before the await ever suspends. Never post-await despite matching the pattern.
    - **5 false positives** in `handleLoginSubmit`/`startMFAEnrollment`: `login-form`, `mfa-challenge-screen`, `mfa-enroll-screen` and `mfa-enroll-secret` exist only in `index.html` (0 occurrences in `app.js`), so the router cannot swap them.
    - **2 unreachable** in `submitPutaway`/`submitBinConditionTransition`: the deref sits immediately after `await showCustomAlert(...)`, and the dialog backdrop is `position: fixed` at 100vw × 100vh — the user physically cannot reach the sidebar to navigate while it is open. Left unguarded deliberately; a guard on unreachable code is noise.
    - Net: **one** genuinely severe instance (the exec dashboard, which fired on *every* login with no user action) and three minor ones. Nothing else of that shape remains.

- [x] Page-level scroll + frozen table header — replaced every table's own cramped inner scrollbox (`table-wrapper`/`table-panel` `overflow:auto`) with genuine whole-page scroll (`.page-container` is now the one scroll container); the table header (`thead`) freezes at the correct position as the page scrolls (`position:sticky`, confirmed via exact pixel math). **Historical limitation, fixed in Stage 41:** the original `thead` implementation did not fully occlude rows scrolling underneath it; Stage 41 moved stickiness to each `<th>` cell so it paints above the body rows.
- [x] **41.2** Sticky table headers — root-caused to CSS2.1 §17.5.1 table paint-layer ordering (a row group stays in the table layer regardless of its own `position`, so `position: sticky` on `thead` was fighting paint order, not fixing it); moved sticky onto the `<th>` cells themselves, which paints in the positioned-descendants layer above every `<td>`.
- [x] **116.1 Rows scroll through a band above the frozen header** (user, 2026-10-19: *"ui is breaking fix this every scroll of page"*). Cause, measured on a scratch server: `.page-container` (the page scroller) had 24px top padding, and a sticky header sticks at the padding edge, so after scrolling the header sat 24px below the scroller's top with table cells painted in that band. Fix: the top gap is a `::before` spacer inside the scroll (`--view-pad-top` / `--view-gap`; the RF shell and transaction-screen overrides set them), so the page looks the same at rest and headers freeze flush at the top. *Verified 2026-10-19:* scratch server, Prefix Configurations scrolled 600px - before: header 24px below the scroller top, a TD painted in the band; after: header flush (gap 0), the band is the TH; at rest the page still starts 24px down; transaction screen keeps its 10px top at 1400 and 390px wide. *Status: Done*

- [x] **28.2** **Theme: light / dark / system.** Dark palette layered on the existing `:root` CSS tokens (`:root[data-theme="dark"]` + `prefers-color-scheme` scoped `:not([data-theme="light"])` so System follows the OS, explicit choices win); all structural literal-color backgrounds (`#f8fafc`/`#f1f5f9`/`#f3f4f6`/`#e2e8f0`/toggle track) tokenized so dark mode is complete (semantic status colors kept literal). Persisted per-user (`users.theme_preference`, `migrations_stage28_user_theme.sql`, surfaced/set via `/api/v1/me`, validated) + localStorage for a no-flash pre-paint apply (inline `<head>` script), reconciled with the server value on load. 3-segment toggle in the account popover. Live-verified: Playwright both themes render clean (zero console errors), `/me` round-trips, invalid rejected.
- [x] **28.5.1 Popup text invisible in dark mode.** `.custom-dialog-body` carried a literal `color: #334155` — dark slate on the dark `--panel-bg` (#1a2436), ~1.3:1 contrast, i.e. the message in every `showCustomAlert`/`showCustomConfirm`/`showCustomPrompt` was unreadable. Fixed at the source rather than one rule at a time: **every** literal colour below the token blocks is now a `var()` token. Added semantic tokens (`--on-primary`, `--text-placeholder`, `--danger-color/-hover/-strong/-soft-bg/-soft-border`, `--warning-*`, `--success-*`) to all three token blocks (`:root`, `[data-theme="dark"]`, the `prefers-color-scheme` block) and routed 25 literal-colour rules + 9 inline `style="color:#..."` strings in `app.js` through them. Light-theme values are the exact previous hexes, so light mode is byte-identical in appearance. Also gave `.custom-dialog-body` explicit `color: inherit` rules for the elements callers inject (p/li/td/th/h*/label/strong/code) plus `a`/`small`/`.text-muted` — deliberately *not* a `*` selector, which would have flattened an intentional `.badge-danger` dropped into a dialog. A rule comment above the dark token block now states that no rule below may use a literal colour, with the two sanctioned exceptions (print-only `.receipt`/`.sticker-label`, which are always ink-on-paper, and translucent rgba scrims/glows). Measured after the fix, dark mode: dialog body 12.99:1, badges 7.87–11.54:1, banners 7.87–9.40:1, `pre` 11.54:1.
- [x] **32.1.5 Interaction feedback decoupled from the layout duration — closed 2026-08-04.** Every hover state in the sheet ran on `transition: all var(--transition-speed)` = **250ms**, the duration meant for sidebar-width and panel slides. Hover feedback at 250ms reads as the UI lagging a beat behind the cursor. Added `--transition-fast: 0.11s` / `--transition-med: 0.16s` / `--ease-out`, and pointed `.menu-item`, `.submenu-item`, `.btn` and `.action-btn` at them with **named properties instead of `all`** (`all` was also animating the geometry — padding, border-width — on `.menu-item.active`).
- [x] **32.1.6 Press feedback added — closed 2026-08-04.** There was no `:active` state anywhere. A button that looks identical the instant it is pressed reads as "didn't register", which is precisely what makes a user click again — and on a submit a second click is a duplicate request, not a cosmetic issue. Added `:active` to `.btn` (1px depress), `.action-btn` (0.9 scale), `.menu-item`/`.submenu-item` (background), plus `user-select: none` and `-webkit-tap-highlight-color: transparent` on the nav rows and buttons so a double-click never selects the label text.
