Closing stays instant. Added the sheet's first `prefers-reduced-motion` block.
- [x] **32.2 Smoothness pass beyond the nav — audited and closed 2026-08-05.** Done as the per-screen interaction audit the entry offered as the alternative to the user naming screens.
  - **Transition sweep, deliberate not blind.** The "~20 remaining sites" estimate was stale — 32.1 had already swept most; **11** were left, and each was read against the `:hover`/`:focus` rule it actually pairs with before being changed. Every one turned out to animate only `background-color`/`border-color`/`box-shadow`/`color`/`opacity`, i.e. pure feedback, so all 11 moved from `--transition-speed` (0.25s, the *layout* duration) to explicit property lists at `--transition-fast` (0.11s) — the convention the token block's own comment sets and 32.1's sidebar fix already follows. Sites: `.header-search`, `.search-box`, `.modal-close`, `.form-input/.form-select/.form-textarea`, `.pagination-btn`, `.account-trigger`, `.account-popover-item`, `.theme-seg-btn`, `.copy-chip`, `.custom-dialog-close-x`, and `.account-trigger-chevron` (→ `--transition-med`, since it is tied to the popover opening rather than a bare hover). The form-control one is the widest-reaching: `transition: all` there was also animating `width`, which interacts badly with Stage 33's responsive form grid. The **only** remaining `--transition-speed` use is `.sidebar { transition: width }` — correct, it is genuinely layout.
  - **The likely second cause of "I have to click many times", found.** `renderView()` cleared `#view-root` and *then* awaited the view's fetches, so on anything slower than localhost a click produced a blank white panel with no sign it had registered — and the natural response is to click again. No amount of transition tuning could have fixed this, because there was nothing rendered to transition. Split into `renderView` (a thin wrapper owning feedback: clear → show an indeterminate loading bar → hand off) and `renderViewContent` (the untouched dispatch), with the placeholder removed in a `finally` so a throwing renderer cannot leave a permanent "Loading…" on screen. New `.view-loading` styles honour `prefers-reduced-motion` by holding the bar static rather than dropping the feedback entirely.
  - Since this closes the last open Stage 32 item, **Stage 32 is complete**. Frontend-only, so it ships with 33.2's deploy.

  - `deploy/install_backup_cron.sh` — idempotent (a marker comment identifies our line, so re-running replaces it rather than appending, and never touches other jobs), preflights every failure mode the droplet actually hit (missing env file, missing `DATABASE_URL`/`BACKUP_ENCRYPTION_KEY`, missing `pg_dump`/`openssl`, missing user), creates+chowns `/opt/erp/backups` and the log, then **runs one backup immediately** — because a cron line existing is not evidence that the backup works, which is precisely how the box ended up with zero backups.
  - `deploy/restore_drill.sh` — the Linux counterpart of `manage.ps1`'s `Invoke-RestoreDrill`, which only ever existed on the Windows dev machine, so production had no way to test its own backups. Verifies the sha256 sidecar, restores into a throwaway database, compares row counts against live, drops the scratch database. Never writes to the live database.

Both are `bash -n` clean; their behaviour on the real box is unproven until someone runs `sudo bash /opt/erp/deploy/install_backup_cron.sh` there. Until that happens **production still has no backups**.

  - **Found 2 real bugs in `install_backup_cron.sh`, both of which would have failed silently at 02:00 every night.** (1) **The cron line could never have worked as written** — the line documented in `backup.sh`'s header comment since day one used `source /etc/erp/erp.env && ... backup.sh`, but that file holds bare `KEY=value` lines with **no `export`**, and must (systemd loads the same file via `EnvironmentFile=`, which rejects an `export ` prefix). So `source` set `DATABASE_URL` as a *shell* variable, `backup.sh` ran as a **child process** and never inherited it, dying on `set DATABASE_URL (source /etc/erp/erp.env)`. Fixed by loading the env with `set -a; . file; set +a` — exports everything sourced without touching the file systemd depends on. This is the whole justification for the script's step-5 immediate run: had the header comment been pasted into a crontab by hand, as the documented procedure said, the job would have failed every night into a log nobody reads. (2) **The installer failed under its own documented `sudo` invocation** — run as root from `/root` (0700), the step-5 verification drops to `erp`, which cannot traverse that cwd, so `pg_dump` warned `could not change directory to "/root"` and the retention `find` exited non-zero, failing the run under `set -e` **even though the dump succeeded**. Cron is unaffected (jobs start in the user's home), so this was purely an install-path artifact — fixed with `cd /` at the top.
  - **Verified that cron itself can run it, not just that the line exists** — a distinct claim, since `erp`'s shell is `/usr/sbin/nologin` and cron's `PATH` is only `/usr/bin:/bin` versus the wider `sudo` environment the manual run inherits.   Original item text: The real code work
  in this Stage, and an improvement independent of hosting. `engines/alerting.go:297` resolves
  `BACKUP_DIR` (default `/opt/erp/backups`) and `CheckBackupFreshness` stats the newest
  `custom_erp_*.dump.enc` in it — and at `engines/alerting.go:310` treats a **missing directory as
  "not a machine that takes backups" and returns silently**. Correct on a dev laptop; on a PaaS it
  means backup monitoring switches itself off and reports nothing, which is the worst available
  failure mode. It also cannot be fixed by pointing `BACKUP_DIR` at a volume, because Railway does
  not share a volume between services: the app checking the folder and the job writing to it are
  different services and cannot see each other's disk. Fix: additive `backup_runs` table (new
  incremental migration), the backup job writes a row on success with size/duration/outcome, and
  `CheckBackupFreshness` reads the latest row instead of stat-ing a directory. Keep the
  `tenant_*`-exports-do-not-count rule (26.1.6). Separately, make "no backup mechanism configured"
  a **loud** finding when `ENV=production` rather than silence, on both providers.

### DOC › Knowledge base & in-app help

- [x] **45.6** **Knowledge Center had no path in beyond the per-screen drawer or knowing the `/help` URL.** Not in the sidebar, not in `buildGlobalSearchIndex()` (which only reads sidebar entries + registered doctypes). Added a standalone sidebar item ("Knowledge Center", right after Reports) wired to `renderView('help')`; it's automatically searchable now too since the search index reads the sidebar at build time — no second registration needed.
- [x] **39.1** Minimal Markdown renderer in Go — **built 2026-08-11**, stdlib only: headings with stable duplicate-safe anchors, paragraphs, ordered/unordered lists, tables, fenced code, links, emphasis, images and GitHub-style admonitions. Raw HTML is escaped and URL schemes are allowlisted (`http`, `https`, `mailto`, relative) so article text cannot inject script/data URLs. Tests cover the full vocabulary, unsafe links/raw HTML, malformed emphasis, invalid UTF-8 and unclosed code fences.
- [x] **39.2** `cmd/genkb` — renders `docs/kb/**/*.md` → HTML fragments + `index.json` + `search.json`, nav built from frontmatter. **Output goes to `internal/kb/content/`, not `public/help/`, and that is the access model.** The app serves `public/` straight off disk with `http.FileServer`, so anything written there is readable by anyone who can reach the host — which directly contradicts 39.6. The generated tree is embedded with `go:embed` instead and only reachable through a handler that decided to let you. It also means the Knowledge Center ships wherever the binary ships: no deploy-script change, no second artifact to forget. Frontmatter is a deliberately tiny YAML subset (scalars, booleans, ints, one-line lists) parsed in ~40 lines rather than taking a YAML dependency for a header that holds eight keys. The build **fails** on an article with no `section` — that article could not appear in the sidebar, and shipping a page nobody can navigate to is worse than not shipping it — and on duplicate slugs across the tree, because a slug is a permanent link people bookmark and must not change when a file moves between folders.
- [x] **39.3** Client-side search over a prebuilt inverted index — ~35 lines of vanilla JS over a `search.json` built at generation time. Terms from the title are indexed twice so a title match outranks a body match; stopwords are dropped (they match everything and rank nothing); queries match by **prefix**, so typing "reserv" finds "reservation" rather than a search box that feels broken mid-word. No Lunr, no Algolia, no scan over article bodies per keystroke.
- [x] **39.4** `/help` route + shell — sidebar grouped by section in a fixed reading order, live search, breadcrumbs, an on-page table of contents from the renderer's own heading anchors (no second slug implementation), prev/next following the sidebar order, and `/help/<slug>` as a real bookmarkable URL that resolves ahead of any saved view. All styling uses existing CSS tokens, so the Knowledge Center follows the app's light/dark theme with no palette of its own.
  - **Found and fixed a latent bug this was the first URL to hit**: `index.html` referenced its assets **relatively** (`styles.css`, `app.js`), so any two-segment SPA URL resolved them against the wrong directory and got the SPA shell back — the browser then refused every stylesheet and script on MIME grounds and the app never booted. Single-segment product prefixes like `/wms` never exposed it; `/help/<article>` does. Fixed at the source by making the five asset references absolute, which also hardens `/wms/<anything>` and every future deep link.
- [x] **39.5** In-app contextual help — a `?` in the header opens a drawer over the current screen (built on the existing `.modal-overlay` primitives, so no second dialog system) showing the article(s) mapped to that screen. The mapping comes from each article's own `screens:` frontmatter via the index's `screen_map`, so there is no second mapping file to drift. A screen with no article says so plainly rather than showing an arbitrary one — a wrong article is worse than an honest gap.
- [x] **39.6** Access model: authenticated by default, per-article `public: true` for the API/integration subset. **Structural, not a check that can be forgotten**: there is no copy under `public/` for a file server to hand out. Three authenticated endpoints serve the whole centre; three `publicRoutes`-listed endpoints serve **only** articles whose frontmatter opts in. The public index and public search index are **rebuilt narrowed**, not filtered in the browser — an index that lists an internal article's title has already leaked it, whatever the client is told to render. Requesting an internal article through the public door returns the same 404 an unknown slug gets, because "that exists but is internal" is itself information.
- [x] **39.7** `docs/kb/update-kb.ps1` with `-Check` — regenerates in memory, compares against the committed output, and exits non-zero naming every stale, missing or **orphaned** file (an article deleted from source whose HTML is still being served). Uses the mandatory `%TEMP%`-then-copy write path for the same Controlled Folder Access reason as `update-brain.ps1`. `WriteTo` deletes orphans rather than merging, so a deleted article stops being served.

Plus a **real-browser pass**: deep link opens the right article, sidebar renders 4 sections, breadcrumb, prev/next, 4-entry TOC, admonition styling, prefix search finds and opens an article, the drawer opens on a mapped screen and closes clean, no horizontal overflow, **zero console errors**. - [x] **30.8.1 Region model over the whole tree — closed 2026-08-01.** `docs/brain/brain.map.json` is the only hand-edited file: **35 regions in 8 lobes** (Cortex/Interface, Brainstem/Kernel, Functional Lobes/Business, Peripheral Nerves/Integrations, Autonomic/Background, Hippocampus/Docs, Motor Cortex/Build, Cerebellum/Tests). Membership is by glob pattern, and **the more specific pattern wins** rather than declaration order, so appending a region can never quietly steal files from an existing one; an explicit `priority` overrides that where it must (the test suite claims `engines/pim_bulk_test.go` off PIM's `engines/pim*.go`).
- [x] **30.8.2 Coverage measured against the working tree, not the graph — closed 2026-08-01.** The generator walks the repo (with an ignore list) rather than trusting graphify's file list, because **only 246 of 345 files are parsed** — graphify has no extractor for `.sql`, JSON, PowerShell or Markdown, and `tree_sitter_sql` is not installed, so all 71 migrations contribute zero nodes. Measuring coverage against the graph would have reported 100% while silently omitting a third of the repo. Currently **100% of 345 files claimed**; an unclaimed file is named in the run output, listed in BRAIN.md §6, and fails `update-brain.ps1 -Check`. That is the mechanism that makes "we will append if new is added" self-policing rather than a promise.
- [x] **30.8.3 Declared links for boundaries no call graph can cross — closed 2026-08-01.** The first draft left the whole Cortex floating unconnected, which was *technically* accurate (the SPA is JavaScript, the server is Go, no extractor links them) and completely useless. 8 `declared_links` now state those edges by hand — HTTP/JSON, the error envelope, offline replay, runtime profile loading, outbox dispatch-by-event-name, PowerShell driving migrations and the binary — each drawn as a thick `==>` arrow and carrying a `note` saying *why* it cannot be extracted, so an asserted edge is never mistaken for a measured one.
- [x] **30.8.4 Honest confidence encoding — closed 2026-08-01.** **99% of cross-region relationships are graphify `INFERRED`**, because it resolves calls within a file exactly and calls across files by name — and a cross-region call is cross-file by definition. The first encoding (dot the edge when >50% inferred) therefore dotted literally every edge and carried no information. Now: dotted = *entirely* inferred, solid = contains at least one relationship parsed straight from source, and the legend states the global figure outright. The map's *shape* is reliable; any *single* edge is a lead to confirm with grep, exactly as `CLAUDE.md` requires.
- [x] **30.8.5 Two outputs, one generator — closed 2026-08-01.** `BRAIN.md` (7 Mermaid diagrams — lobe level, region map, the same map with the three universal hubs removed so module-to-module wiring is visible at all, and the four signal pathways — plus a region index and a detail card per region with file:line links) and `brain.html` (interactive: click a region, hover to light its wiring, filter by lobe or connection strength, search by file or symbol, table view). Self-contained, vanilla JS, no CDN, light+dark, per the repo's first principle. Stdlib-only Go, no new dependency.
- [x] **30.8.6 `update-brain.ps1`, and the Windows failure it exists for — closed 2026-08-01.** **Controlled Folder Access** (Defender ransomware protection, on by default) refuses any write under `Documents\` from a binary it does not recognise — and a freshly compiled Go binary never is. It reports that refusal as `ERROR_FILE_NOT_FOUND`, so Go says *"the system cannot find the file specified"* about a directory that plainly exists. Confirmed by isolation (writes succeed outside `Documents\`, PowerShell writes succeed inside). The wrapper generates into `%TEMP%` and copies in with PowerShell; `writeOut` in the generator detects the same case and names the cause instead of leaving the next person to debug a phantom missing directory.

#### Stage 34 — Market intelligence / competitor pricing ⏳ (opened 2026-08-06; 34.1-34.3 built 2026-08-07, 34.4-34.6 still gated)

**Source:** [docs/product/research/market-intelligence.md](../product/research/market-intelligence.md), the knowledge kept from the retired OmniCore/"Buying Catalog" Python project (see `project_ledger.md` §81). **Nothing in this Stage is approved work** — it is the buildable shape of the one genuinely net-new concept that project held, written down so the analysis isn't repeated. `engines/marketplace.go` covers courier serviceability, labels/manifests, delivery/RTO and settlement reconciliation; it does **not** do competitor-price or catalog harvesting.

**The constraint that shapes the whole Stage.** `go.mod` carries exactly two dependencies (`lib/pq`, `x/crypto`) and there is no vendor directory, so **there is no HTML parser available**. Anything needing DOM traversal means a new dependency, and a headless browser (the retired project used Playwright) means a new *runtime*, not just a library — both against `CLAUDE.md`'s first principle. That single fact is what splits 34.1-34.3 (buildable now, stdlib only) from 34.4-34.5 (gated).

**Sequencing:** 34.6 is the real gate. Do not start 34.4 before it is answered, and 34.1-34.3 are worth doing regardless of how it lands, because they are how the data gets *used* no matter where it comes from.

#### Stage 60 — Number series per transaction and store, item types with barcode rules and behaviour, names not codes, platform data console (opened 2026-10-14 from the user's "Build") ✅ (archived 2026-10-19)

**Why it was opened.** The user asked whether PO/GRN/barcode were ready and found: numbers carry the store *code* and a year (`GRN/HQ/26-27/000001`), there is no suffix and no per-store prefix, the barcode rule is one switch per client, `Item.item_type` is only Stock/Fixed Asset, codes still show in some screens, and there is no way for a platform super user to fix data inside a client.

**Decisions (user, 2026-10-14):**
- Lengths: purchase series (PR, RFQ, QTN, PO, ASN, GRN, PRT, DN) **5 digits**; stock/sales/production/asset (TO, TI, SI, PRO, AST) **6**; HR (LV, ATT, EXP, LOAN, GRV, Payslip) **5**. Each transaction keeps its own row - formats differ per transaction.
- The store segment inside a number is the store's **Short Code** (falls back to Store Code when blank). A store carries Store Name, Short Code, Store Code and **Facility Code**; Facility Code is the one OMS uses.
- Item types: **barcode rule + behaviour** (Gift / Free-with-item sell at zero price, Backflush is consumed at production completion).
- Platform console: **edit every table, raw**, in any client, customer personal fields masked, every change audited.
- "No code in UI" means internal record codes. Shown as codes on purpose: document numbers (PO/GRN...), Design ID, Combination ID, barcode. Everything else shows its name (vendor, store, product...).

- **Verification (2026-10-14):** `go build`/`go vet` clean; full `go test -p 1 ./...` green (engines, internal/server, db, cmd/*, securityscan, docgen, kb, supplychain); release budget cold core 184,099 / 184,320 after moving the series form and `prefixConfigSample` out of the startup files and condensing two comments. Found by the suite and fixed: the item-type normalisation made every import row miss the batch Link prefetch (64 s for 20,000 rows) - `validateDocumentWith` now remembers Link hits for the rest of the file (2.2 s). **Not deployed; not committed.** Deploy needs the new binary and all four 60.x migrations together (an old binary against the migrated schema rejects "Stock" item types), and `ERP_PLATFORM_OPERATORS` set on the server.

#### Stage 89 — Item master: org defaults, one pick fills the item, every field asked once, attributes from masters, where each field is asked (Item / PO / GRN), attributes mapped to the type (opened 2026-10-18 from the user's Edit Item screenshots)

User, 2026-10-18, on the deployed **Edit Item** (antique necklace; Product Family *Anitque*; More details: Sub Category, Type, Device Master Record, Device Type / Category, Polish / Plating, Metal Type, Purity, Gross / Net Weight, Stone Type / Weight, Making Charge Type / Value, Size): *"What ever is there in item master, It will be some deafult config for org. if chang required in item user will change it. While creating item it self it should ask all this. User will never revisit this. & It need to smart filled/ Auto filled with a single selction. Tax treatment will deafut taxable. Ask family mandatory in top it self. Code auto generate. Tracabity, GRN batch one company level define and Item will inherit and offcourse user can chnage required. But ask in org level. All Shelf life default take std value. Weight and ask in GRN to fill. Catrgory/Type make mandtory. Type and Famiy will create Item name it can be a+b or b+a. Allow to change once in config. It will be reversible. Purity Ask in GRN, It will hidable in GRN as well. Give in config. What ever attribute to ask in PO and GRN, Need config. Polish, Color, all will be drop down. It should ask to add in Master if not present. There will be another logic. COlor, Polish, Size etc will have one master data individually. next Categorywise there will be another mapping for color,polish and size and other attribute. This applies to all industry. Make that flexible. While Creating PO, I order for Antique Necklace- Antique will be Catgory and necklace will be type. Now red color will be attached to necklace. Once I order necklace it will show necklace related color. So, This will be a config to turn on and off. If Off all attribute will show to al. Else I ahve to map attribute to type. By dafeaut it will be all. Bring this. This should be flexible and dynamic with new master created. If on, It should where to map. Smart As well."*

Then, on the form's **Barcode and label** and **Selling and accounting** sections (every dropdown showing *— Select Option —*): *"Same goes for barcode as well. Config at org level. Account as well. Make the default for normal prod. Make it easy for user, Ask What type of product. Very easy Std option you ask and as per that change it will define the accounting drop down. Make that field mandatory to Item creation as well. The drop down should be dead easy and changeable if user do mistake."*

**Found while planning (what exists).** Code is already numbered by the server (`Item/HQ/2026/000001`). **GRN batch number** is already org-level (`inventory.grn_batch_number`, 61.6) with Item Type and Item overrides (*Item type default*). **Traceability** (`tracking_mode`) and **shelf life** have no org default - blank on every new item. **Tax Treatment** is blank on a new item. Item **Category** is free text; there is **no Type** on Item. The **Category / Product Type / Item Name** masters exist (65.3: Item Name = *Category + Product Type*, holding HSN + GST) but only the PO uses them; the Item form does not. **Product Family** on the Item is the PO's *design* (65.4: design number, vendor, design attributes, item name) - not a category; the client's family *Anitque* is being used as one. The ERP's own **Item Attribute** master exists (86.3) and feeds the Item form's Variant Options and the PO; the jewellery industry profile separately adds **free-text** Color / Polish / Size / Stone Type and fixed-list Metal Type / Purity fields to Item (`public/profiles/jewelry.json`; the 81.6 overlap). The client's Item also carries **Device Master Record / Device Type** - fields a Medical profile added before the industry changed (82: a change adds, never deletes). The GRN line has no place for weight, purity or any attribute. Nothing maps attributes to a type. **Barcode** is already org-level (`inventory.barcode_generate_at`, `inventory.barcode_per_receipt_date`, 57.7) and the eight accounting dimensions already come from the **Item Type** profile (72.1: Item > Item Type > company default = ordinary merchandise); the 13 shipped profiles are the "type of product" (Product = normal product, Packaging, Gift, Free With Item, Service, Gift Card, Consumable - Periodic, Non-Stock Expense, Non-Asset, Accessory, Backflush, Fixed Asset, Virtual Kit). But Item Type is optional on the Item, and every inheriting dropdown shows a blank *— Select Option —*, so the form reads as nine unanswered questions when a normal product needs none. **Changeable after a mistake** meets 72.12: once an item has stock history, MASTER-0407 refuses a change to its stock tracking, valuation or accounting treatment (D5).

**Decisions (user, 2026-10-18, asked).** **D1** the pick at the top of New Item is the **Item name** (*Antique Necklace*): it fills Category, Type, HSN, GST and the type's attributes; a new one is made right there from Category + Type; Product Family stays the PO's design and is not asked - *"Option1 but I may change in config saying Item name can be Type+Category or Category+Type"*. **D2** switching the name order **renames existing item names too** (and back when reversed); bills already printed keep the name they printed. **D3** values asked at the GRN (weights, purity, …) are kept on the **GRN line and its batch** - stickers and the POS read them from the batch. **D5** **free until stock moves; after that an admin-approved correction** - first answered *free until stock moves*, then (same day): *"Admin change + correction ... this is also required. Tell the impact in detail and show preview of impact and Admin approve and it will change. Warn and Change after multiple Confirmation. Are you sure one. Multiple mean no 100 times. In the std way how many time it should ask. We should give all flexibility to user. We will not build again this. May case come admin identify later after GRN."* So: until the first stock movement the kind of item and its accounting change freely; after it, a change to stock tracking / valuation / accounting treatment goes through **89.8** (impact preview → reason + one typed confirmation → admin approval → applied with its correcting journal) instead of being refused. Two confirmations, the standard: the reviewed preview with a reason, then typing the item code. **D4 taken without asking** (user: *"make that flexible"*): attributes map to a **Type** (the user's necklace example), a **Category** may be mapped too, and the more specific mapping wins (Type over Category), as Backflush rules resolve (72.3). Also taken without asking (reversible, say if wrong): org defaults live in **Configuration → Inventory** beside the existing GRN batch setting; an item inherits a default by holding *Company default*, the pattern `grn_batch_number` already uses, so changing the org default moves every inheriting item; attribute-to-type mapping works at both levels (which attributes a type has, and optionally which values); with mapping on, a type with nothing mapped still shows everything, so turning it on never empties a form.

#### Stage 62 — Fast-fashion buying: designs and combinations inside the PO, multi-PO GRN at invoice price, automatic debit/credit notes, standard prints (opened 2026-10-15 from the user's "Build everything not built yet … don't ask, start building") ✅ (archived 2026-10-19)

**Why it was opened.** The user's buying flow: *"In PO it will ask vendor first, then item will be created and SKU can be created in PO itself, or type design and load all combinations and we can remove a few"*; *"while creating PO it should ask all matrix of product defined in the org; once all filled it will create design and variant"*; a **design number** that is either *always new* or *reused when every attribute matches*, per config, and a pasted existing design number that *always takes the same design* while allowing new combinations; *"GRN from multiple PO of the same vendor"*; *"GRN we will have credit note and debit note but never be hold"*; *"PO price and received invoice price — two columns; vendor's invoice amount at the top to type; it will generate the diff and the credit note and debit note; a section to see"*; *"std print profile for PO, GRN, credit note, debit note"*. IRN later (not in this stage).

**Decisions taken without asking (user: "everything recommended approved, don't ask") — reversible, flag if wrong:**
- **Design = `ProductFamily`** (already numbered `Design/...` since 51.5); **combination = `Item`** with `family`/`parent_product_code` = the design and `variant_option_values` = its attribute values. No new design master.
- **"All matrix defined in the org" = every Active `ProductAttributeDef` of Value Type Select** (its `value_options`). Pick one value → a design-level attribute; pick several → an axis; the combinations are the cross product of the axes, any of which can be removed before creating.
- Items are created **through the ordinary record API** (`POST /api/v1/doc/ProductFamily`, `/doc/Item`), so numbering, variant code, barcode policy, duplicate-combination checks and audit all apply unchanged.
- **GRN prices are ex-GST per unit.** PO Rate is read from the PO by the server (never trusted from the screen); Invoice Rate defaults to it and is editable.
- **Stock and GRN Suspense (2100) are booked at the Invoice Rate** — the vendor's bill then matches its GRN exactly, which is what removes the hold.
- **The PO price is the agreed price.** Invoice Rate above PO Rate → a **Debit Note** to the vendor for the excess; below → a **Vendor Credit Note** for the shortfall; both incl. GST at the line's rate, **posted immediately** (never Draft, never held). GL: Debit Note Dr 2100 / Cr 5150 (taxable) / Cr 1500 (GST); Vendor Credit Note the mirror. Net payable and net cost both land on the PO value.
- The **vendor invoice amount typed at the top** is a control total: the screen shows lines total vs typed total and the difference, and the GRN records it, but it does not block or hold.
- **Multi-PO GRN:** every line carries its own `po_id`; the header keeps `po_id` (first PO, unchanged for every existing reader) plus `po_ids`. All POs must be the same vendor. Every PO check (approval, over-receipt, unexpected item, fully received) runs per PO on that PO's lines.

#### Stage 42 — WMS Parity Plan (SAP EWM + Infor WMS) ✅ (2026-08-16 → 24; all 6 open decisions resolved 2026-08-31) — 58 items, 6 phases

Consolidated from [SAP Extended Warehouse Management](https://help.sap.com/docs/SAP_EXTENDED_WAREHOUSE_MANAGEMENT/) and [Infor WMS 11.5.x](https://docs.infor.com/wms/11.5.x/en-us/sceolh/default.html), reconciled against real code. Full per-item detail, the 33-row gap table and the explicit out-of-scope list lived in `docs/specs/wms_parity_plan.md` before this move. **Infor was the benchmark actually aimed at** (right size, ~70% of its TOC achievable here); **SAP feature-list parity was explicitly not attempted** — read only as a concept checklist. MFS/PLC equipment control, Infor's 3D yard view, and a separate Warehouse Order object are explicit non-goals, on the record.

- **42.1 Traceability foundation** (11 items, closed 2026-08-19) — `Batch`/`SerialNumber` masters; a new `bin_stock_batch` breakdown table, not a column (avoids rewriting `bin_stock`'s primary key); FEFO/FIFO allocation through one `AllocateFromStock` choke point; expiry gates; outbound lottable constraints; UOM conversion; a hand-rolled Code128 barcode encoder/renderer (`engines/code128.go`, no new dependency, checksum pinned against a third-party worked example). **Real bug found and fixed**: the generic doc-save path only ever ran master-data validation for Item/Vendor/Customer/ProductContent, so Batch/SerialNumber/LottableConstraint/UOMConversion's own duplicate-row rejections were unreachable through the live UI the entire time — collapsed into one unconditional call.
- **42.2 The warehouse task spine** (10 items, closed 2026-08-19) — `WarehouseTask` doctype, retrofitted onto the 5 existing floor actions with no signature change; `GetNextTask` dispatch (`FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`); configurable `TaskDispatchStrategy`; `Zone` master (kept `Bin.zone` as Data, not Link, the same "don't rewrite live tenant data for a cosmetic type change" call made throughout this Stage); bin capacity enforcement; directed putaway; configurable `AllocationStrategy` (FEFO always wins for a batch-tracked item, never overridable); exception-code follow-on actions; the Warehouse Cockpit. **Real bug found and fixed, unrelated to this Stage**: a Stage 45 change to `renderView`'s render-buffering left a scratch container fully detached from the DOM until render finished, silently breaking `getElementById` for the overwhelming majority of screens, not just this Stage's two new ones.
- **42.3 Inbound depth** (10 items, closed 2026-08-20) — dock/appointment scheduling with capacity-overlap enforcement; yard check-in/check-out; hold/release riding the existing maker-checker engine unchanged; configurable receipt-tolerance rules; catch-weight/dimension capture; planned cross-dock/transship; hazmat compliance gating on putaway; an RF receiving screen (keyboard-wedge scan input, the same convention POS already uses).
- **42.4 Outbound depth** (11 items, closed 2026-08-21) — `WaveTemplate` auto-wave creation (hourly worker reusing the existing scheduled-report ticker shape, not a second timer mechanism); a real Wave lifecycle that gates pick-list generation; sortation/put-wall; cartonization v2; packing validation; deconsolidation; loading + Bill of Lading; a pre-ship gate; VAS/kitting off the existing Manufacturing BOM.
- **42.5 Inventory control depth** (8 items, closed 2026-08-24) — physical inventory freeze/count/reconcile; `CycleClass` ABC-tier plans; demand-driven + wave-triggered + dynamic-pick-face replenishment; slotting v2 (unslotting, dimension-aware re-slot, consolidation); facility hierarchy + copy + cross-facility inquiry; multi-owner stock segregation (42.5.5, gated on decision 42.D2 — resolved 2026-08-24: yes, 3PL is real scope — via a new `bin_stock_owner` breakdown table, the same non-destructive pattern as `bin_stock_batch`, rewiring both billing paths onto it).
- **42.6 Labour and billing depth** (9 items, closed 2026-08-22) — engineered labour standards computed at run time, never a stale flat-seconds override; shift/schedule masters; labour planning + a 6-report family; charge codes/rate groups/contracts; an event monitor that auto-captures owner-attributed billable charges with no duplicate-capture risk on retry; invoice generation from captured charges (closing Stage 26.5.15's report-only carve-out); storage billing v2 off daily balance snapshots.
- **6 open decisions, all resolved**: 42.D1 (regulated-category traceability worth building regardless — acted on early rather than waiting), 42.D2 (3PL/multi-owner is real scope — yes), 42.D3 (batch AND serial, not batch-only — asked directly), 42.D4 (moot — the RF screen's keyboard-wedge input works identically with or without real scanner hardware), 42.D5 (wave auto-creation confirmed and built), 42.D6 (Zone-master auto-create migration confirmed non-destructive — resolved 2026-08-31 as a docs-only close; the migration itself was already written non-destructively and applied to dev when 42.2 closed 2026-08-19).

#### Stage 59 — Mixed-owner (3PL) WMS isolation, built on bin stock that tracks reality (opened 2026-10-08 from the user's "build this") ✅ (59.1-59.6 closed 2026-10-17; archived 2026-10-18 at the Stage 73 release)

**Why it was opened.** The page-wide "Conditionally supported" banner carries three caveats (`engines/environment.go` `supportedConfigurationCaveats`). Only one can be closed in code: **47.5**, mixed-owner isolation, which 47.5.1 (archived) had de-scoped on 2026-09-09 to "one owner per warehouse, enforced" because nobody used mixed ownership. The user chose on 2026-10-08 to build the real thing: **47.5.2–47.5.6, plus owner per order**. The other two can't be closed in code. **47.6** needs real device/scanner/printer certification (47.6.6). **47.7** is permanent: audit rows written before signing existed can't be proven after the fact. So the banner keeps two lines even when this stage closes.

**What reading the code turned up first (it changed the plan).** `bin_stock` only ever went up. Putaway, cross-dock, VAS and moves wrote it; no pick or dispatch path ever took anything out (dispatch only reduced `inventory_availability`). The pick list was recalculated on every call and never saved, so two open tasks could be sent to the same last unit. `bin_stock_owner` was only touched by its own HTTP endpoints. An owner filter on allocation alone would have been isolation on paper only. So 59.1 makes bins tell the truth first, and owner isolation is built on top of it.

**Decisions (user, 2026-10-08):** full Stage 59 (not 59.1 only); **one owner per order** (`owner_id` on the SalesOrder header), not one per line.

#### Stage 35 — OMS parity (Unicommerce/Uniware level) ✅ (≈16-20 sessions; release train R1 built 2026-08-11, rest through 2026-08-25, archived 2026-09-27)

**Release train R1 (35.1 + 35.2 + 35.3) built 2026-08-11.** Full detail below; the three structural debts R1 existed to clear are now cleared.

**Two bugs found and fixed while building R1, both outside its nominal scope:**

**Verified**: `go build`/`go vet`/`node --check` clean, `go test ./... -p 1` fully green, every new endpoint exercised over HTTP on a throwaway server (port 8097, stopped and released), **and a real-browser pass via Playwright** — 4 tiles, 7 facet controls, working pager, detail modal with 7 actions and all 9 sections, **zero console errors**, no horizontal overflow.

**Known limitation, stated rather than hidden:** `inventory_reservation` has **no `order_id` or line reference** (`db/migration.sql` §301), so reservations cannot be attributed to the order that made them. The detail screen matches them by the (sku, location) pairs the order's lines allocated to, and `releaseLineReservation` releases the oldest match — correct in aggregate (the same quantity returns to the same pool, which is all `computeATS` consumes) but not provably "this line's" under concurrency. **Related: nothing anywhere ever expires or sweeps `inventory_reservation`** — `expires_at` is written and indexed but never read, so every reservation is effectively permanent. Attributing reservations per line and adding a sweeper is one schema change plus one worker; it is not in Stage 35's scope but should be picked up before 35.4.

Make it std pos, research and make it best / it should work with name search / Bill should which loction and store / location of store sellable non saleable / it should freeze untill i reset there should reset button"*.

**What is actually wrong today** (read from `public/view-pos.js`, `engines/qz_payload.go`, `engines/inventory.go` before planning, not assumed):
- The customer field is literally labelled **"Customer Code (optional)"** placeholdered *"For loyalty points"*. A `Customer` typeahead *is* already attached (`attachLinkTypeahead`), and the server's `?q=` search already scans **every** field (so name and phone already match) — but the box shows and stores the raw code, so it reads to a cashier as "type a code you don't know". The two loyalty buttons then re-read that box and say *"Enter a customer code first."* The capability is there; the UX denies it.
- The SKU box is `Scan or Enter SKU` with an `Item` typeahead, but `addSKUToPOSCart` sends **whatever string is in the box** straight to `/api/v1/availability?sku=`. A typed product *name* produces a zero-availability phantom line, not an error — there is no barcode→SKU resolution and no result list.
- `GetAvailableToSell` already returns `qc_hold`, `damaged`, `blocked` and `hold_qty` alongside `ats`; the cart throws all of it away and prints one "Available" number, so nothing on screen distinguishes sellable from non-sellable stock.
- `Location` (`db/migrations_stage17h_location_masters.sql`) has `type` (Store/Warehouse/HO) but **no sellable concept**. Nothing stops a POS session being opened, or a sale rung up, against a warehouse or HO. The screenshot the user sent is exactly this: a till sitting on **HO**.
- Receipts print the location **code** and nothing else — no store name, no legal entity, no GSTIN, no cashier. True on both paths: the browser fallback (`printPOSReceipt`, `${location}`) and the server-built ESC-POS payload (`BuildReceiptPayload`, `b.WriteString(location + "\n")`).
- Nothing freezes. The location picker is editable mid-shift, and after `Complete Sale` the cart is silently emptied behind a confirm dialog — the next customer's scan lands on a live, indistinguishable cart with no record of the bill just closed on screen.

**Two readings were ambiguous and were put to the user before planning (answered 2026-10-04): "freeze" = BOTH (lock the store for the shift AND freeze the till on the completed bill), "sellable/non-sellable" = BOTH (a flag on the `Location` master AND splitting the cart's availability figure).**

Scope discipline per this repo's first principle: no new framework, no new dependency, no new picker pattern. Customer/product search reuses `attachCodeNamePicker`/`attachLinkTypeahead` and the existing `/api/v1/doc/{doctype}?q=` endpoint; the sellable/non-sellable split needs **no backend change at all** (the fields are already in the availability response); the `Location.sellable` flag is one additive migration in the Stage 17.9 style.

#### Stage 77 — POS billing for a real store: customer capture, high-value rules by country, tenders, salesmen, hold/resume, store returns, scan without Enter, stock locations (opened 2026-10-17 from the user's POS screenshots, during Stage 76)

**Why it was opened.** Four messages from the user while Stage 76 was being built, on the POS screen. The inventory (2026-10-17) found:
- **Customer.** The quick-add asks for name + phone only. Customer has no address, anniversary, gender or PAN, and there is no default customer. The receipt prints the raw customer *code* (`qz_payload.go:542`).
- **Missing.** No high-value rules, no tender master (Cash/Card/UPI hard-coded, `view-pos.js:122`; one `payment_mode` per bill), no salesman, no hold/resume.
- **Returns.** Bill lookup is tenant-wide by exact number. A return at store B of a store-A bill just lands at B.
- **Stock.** Buckets are fixed columns plus a fixed `bin_stock.condition` CHECK. There is no stock-location master, no per-store enablement and no per-transaction from/to defaults.
- **Session close** adds item price × qty for cash bills - discounts and cash refunds are not subtracted.

**User's words (2026-10-17), the scope:**
- Customer name + number (number optional), address, DOB, DOA, gender, PAN. No number → a default customer with a default number, never printed on the customer copy; a real number is printed.
- Bill ≥ ₹50k → ask address; > ₹2 lakh → PAN mandatory - India's rule, and the equivalent for other countries.
- A tender module: which tenders each store bills with, under the user's control; reports pick them up.
- Salesman name/ID before saving - optional per configuration; different per store; always a default salesman; prompt to create one for a store; disable one who left.
- Hold bill / resume bill.
- Sales return: search the store's bills. Centralised return: SR on the original store, TO from the original store, TI at the store where the customer is, into the inward location.
- Stock locations inside a store: Main (sellable), Sold (physically gone), In-Transit (TO done), Inward (after GRN / TI), Purchase Return (warehouse only), Damage. Logic settable; a location master; enable per store; defaults applied to every new store; per transaction a default from/to; a new transaction (e.g. Damage) appears there automatically.
- Scanning without Enter, everywhere (POS, TO, TI, advance, return), typing still possible.
- POS screen: the customer messages take too much room; give the space to the products.

**Rules found (research 2026-10-17, to be held as settings with country defaults, not hard-coded):**
- India, address ≥ ₹50,000 to an unregistered buyer: CGST Rule 46(e) - name, address, delivery address, state + code.
- India, PAN for a sale of goods/services > ₹2,00,000 per transaction: Income-tax Rules 2026 Rule 159 (was 114B). A buyer with no PAN signs Form 97 (was Form 60).
- India, cash of ₹2,00,000 or more from one person per transaction/day is prohibited (s.269ST) - the cash part must be refused, the balance taken by card/UPI.
- Elsewhere, full invoice details above a simplified-invoice limit: UK £250, Germany €250, UAE AED 10,000. No rule found for the others - setting left blank.

- *Coordination:* `pos_checkout.go`, `pos_payment.go`, `qz_payload.go`, `returns*.go`, `transfer_*.go`, `settings_definitions.go`, `handlers_pim_pos_finance.go` have another session's uncommitted Stage 73 changes - check `git status` before each.

User, 2026-10-19: *"Store app"* (one of four asks; see Stage 99's opening). Earlier, 2026-10-18 (55.5a): *"we will build a PWA for the approval"*.

User, 2026-10-22: *"Stage 101 CRM: about 35. Stage 102 store app: about 10 left. Build all"* - every open item below built in one run. D4 is decided, so the shared-phone sign-in it describes is now its own item, 102.1.4. 102.2.1 is built on its own read call because Stage 100's datasets do not exist yet; Stage 100 can take that call over as a dataset.

**What exists (found while recording, 2026-10-19).**
- The ERP is a web app laid out for a desktop or till screen: no app manifest, no service worker, nothing to install on a phone.
- The POS keeps selling offline: sales queue in the browser and sync when the line returns, with a heartbeat and a gap check (20.13; POS Offline Gaps).
- Pieces a store app would reuse: store access per user and the working store (85), the approval engine and the task inbox (73.3.3), scan-to-age lookup (61), the RF traceability screens (`public/view-rf-traceability.js`), sticker printing through QZ Tray (desktop only), and the second approval for returns, built and switched off (55.5a).

**Decisions (asked 2026-10-19; D1, D2 and D5 answered the same day - user, replying to "for store staff rather than shoppers? an installable web app with no app store and no new framework? phone billing stays out of the first version": *"We can build a pwa"* - all three as recommended. D3 and D4 not yet answered):**
- **D1 Who it is for.** **Decided: store staff** - manager, cashier, salesman, stock staff. A shopping app for the brand's customers is a different product (Shopify's own mobile store, with Stage 99, covers online buying).
- **D2 How it is built.** **Decided: an installable web app (PWA)** served by the same server at `/store/`, plain JavaScript like `public/` - installed from the browser, no app store, updated on next open; a Play Store listing later by wrapping the same app (TWA) if wanted. Rejected: a native, Flutter or React Native app (a new framework and build step; first principle).
- **D3 Offline.** Recommended: item, price and stock lookups work from the last download; counts and scans queue offline and sync later; approvals need a connection. *Until answered:* the app itself opens offline and says it is offline; lookups and approvals need a connection.
- **D4 Signing in on a shared phone.** Recommended: the manager registers the phone to the store once; each person then signs in with their own PIN, locked after a few idle minutes (49.14.3). *Until answered:* the app uses the ERP's own sign-in (password, then the two-factor code where the role needs it; the Stage 67 shift session) - right for a personal phone; the PIN is added on top once decided, with no rework.
- **D5 Billing on the phone.** **Decided: not in the first cut** - a salesman builds the basket on the phone and the till recalls it (77's hold / resume); full billing on a tablet later if asked.

**Order:** 102.1 the app shell → 102.2 manager → 102.3 stock → 102.4 selling floor → 102.5 guides and real-phone checks. **First slice (started 2026-10-19):** the parts that need no other stage - 102.1.1 the installable app, 102.1.2 camera scanning, 102.2.2 approvals and 102.3.1 scan an item. 102.2.1 waits for Stage 100's datasets, 102.3.4 for 98.4, 102.4.1 for 101.1.

#### Stage 74 — Transaction modules master BRD: the eleven 71.7 modules specified (external PDF; opened + planned 2026-10-17, nothing built yet)

User, 2026-10-17: *"Read this and prepare the checklist for this as well"*, sharing `Enterprise_Transaction_Modules_Master_BRD.pdf` (BRD-TXN-001 v1.0, 17 Oct 2026, 46 pages, same folder as the Stage 73 PDF). Contents: §1 decision brief and the eleven gaps with P0 / P1, §2 system ownership, shared lifecycle and invariants, §3 configuration masters, §4.1-4.11 one mini-BRD per module (journey, fields, numbered FR with acceptance proof, stock / GL / tax outcome, UI brief, negative scenarios, reports, test fixture), §5 posting blueprints and refund-vs-credit-note separation, §6 print outputs, §7 roles and segregation of duties, §8 command pattern, data model and illustrative APIs, §9 screen map, §10 UAT matrix (68 module cases + E2E-01..16), §11 sixteen registers R-TX-01..16 and the reconciliation identities, §12 NFR-01..15, §13 decisions DEC-01..22, §14 waves 0-5 and pilot gates, §15 statutory sources, §16 sign-off.

**How this stage is built (read before adding to it):**
- **It is 71.7, specified.** The BRD's eleven gaps are 71.7(a)-(k) item for item (its §15.1 baseline is this file and the handover). 71.7 asked which to build and in what order; the BRD gives the order (P0 money and statutory movement first, P1 after; waves in §14) but leaves its 22 decisions open. 71.7 now points here and nothing is listed twice.
- **An index, not a copy.** Each item names the BRD section and the FR / UAT ids it must pass; the full acceptance wording stays in the PDF. Build order = its waves: the Wave 1 shared spine before any new economic command.
- **Overlaps point elsewhere.** Stage 73 owns the per-line refund allocation (73.1.1), split tender and refund to the original tender (73.1.6), transfer batch / discrepancy (73.1.7), RFQ / quote / award → PO (73.2.1-73.2.3), the GRN rejected-quantity policy (73.2.4, D05), period reopen (73.1.10), GL actor (73.1.9), report control totals (73.2.19), till cash movements (73.2.7) and the one task inbox (73.3.3). Stage 72 owns item classification (72.1), Consumption Entry (72.6) and the stored-value ledger (72.8) that store credit reuses. E-invoice / e-way credentials stay 20.30 / 20.31 / 26.2.3 / 26.2.4.
- **Every gap was re-checked against source on 2026-10-17**: two read-only sweeps, with file:line evidence in each item. The two claims that change the shared spine were read directly (`inventory.go:353-397`, `numbering.go:118-133`). The BRD itself says its gaps are "not an independently executed code audit"; 74.0.2 lists what it does not know.
- **The first principle applies to the BRD's §8 model.** Its tables and routes are "illustrative; reuse existing routes where possible". Reuse map:
  - number series → Stage 60 `GenerateSequence`
  - approvals → `approval_rules` value slabs + the existing self-approval block
  - reasons → the `ReasonCode` master
  - idempotency → `command_idempotency` / `ClaimCommand`
  - store credit → 72.8's stored-value ledger
  - registers → `ReportDefinition`
  - provider calls → `async_jobs` + `channel_credentials` + the courier adapter pattern
  - prints → Stage 63's print endpoint and templates
  - errors → `writeAPIError` (the BRD's 400 / 403 / 409 / 422)
  
  No second stock ledger, invoice ledger, approval engine or report framework.
- **Tax sign-off sits outside code.** Per the BRD, tax positions need Account Head / qualified tax professional sign-off before production (DEC-02, 03, 10, 14-16, 20). A module can be built and verified on a test client. It is not switched on for a real client until that sign-off exists. Each module ships behind a client setting, default off (NFR-15: old clients unchanged).
- **Acceptance bar = the BRD's §1.2 and its §10 execution rule.** A permissioned user can configure, create, approve, post, partly fulfil, reverse, search, print / reprint and report the transaction, and stock, custody, money, GL and compliance reconcile from the same saved ids. The evidence for each case:
  - the UI action and a readback
  - stock / GL reconciliation
  - the print
  - a denied-role test
  - a replay test

  Each module also gets its guide sections and a `docs/guides/UAT_CHECKLIST.md` section when it ships.

##### 74.0 Wave 0 — verify and decide

- **74.0.2 Re-verification against source (2026-10-17): what the BRD does not know.** Use this alongside each item.
  - **Already there, to reuse:**
    - Legal Entity carries GSTIN and state, Locations link to it, and the GL carries `entity` (`migrations_stage17h_location_masters.sql:18-23`, `finance.go:144`).
    - Department and Cost Centre masters exist (`:10-11, 25-30`). A GL posting accepts `PostingOptions{CostCenter, Department, Entity, Project}` (`finance.go:46, 138-149`), but only journal vouchers and expenses pass it.
    - Approval rules use value slabs per doctype, and self-approval is refused under a row lock (`approval.go:26-27, 138-147, 324-339`).
    - Editing an approved PO resets it to pending and needs an `amendment_reason` (`approval.go:523`, `transactional_validation.go:645-669`).
    - `command_idempotency` gives payload-digest and lease semantics (`command_idempotency.go:98, 197`).
    - The GRN posts Dr 1200 / Cr 2100 GRN Suspense, which is the BRD's GRNI (`costing.go:237-252`). The vendor invoice three-way match holds a mismatch (`vendor_invoice.go:103, 212, 295`).
    - Multi-PO GRN keeps the PO on each line (62.1).
    - Vendor invoices are unique per vendor + number + FY (`migrations_stage17g_vendor_invoice.sql:21-27`).
    - `print_job_log` is written by QZ printing (`migrations_stage31_1_qz_print.sql:41-53`).
    - `async_jobs` has backoff, dead letter and replay (`jobrunner.go:73-397`).
    - `channel_credentials` are AES-GCM encrypted with a key ring, and the courier adapter interface can serve as the model (`courier.go:22, 86`).
    - The stored-value profile already offers instrument type "Store credit" with its own liability account (72.8, uncommitted).
  - **Worse than the BRD assumes:**
    - (a) **The stock ledger row is written after the commit, best effort.** `WriteStockLedgerLines` (`inventory.go:353-397`) runs in its own transaction once availability has committed, and a failure is only a WARN in the system log (`:394-395`). This is deliberate, because a replay rewrites it. But it breaks the BRD's one-transaction invariant (§2.2, §8.1 step 4) → 74.1.5.
    - (b) **Cycle count posts no GL.** An approved variance moves quantity only, clamped with `GREATEST(0, …)`. There is no inventory gain or shrinkage account → 74.2.3. *2026-10-18:* 73.1.8 made the post one transaction under the line's row lock, and Approved-only. It still posts no GL, and it still writes its ledger row after the commit (`PostCycleCountAdjustment`, `wms.go:697`).
    - (c) **Stock postings never check a closed period.** `rejectIfCurrentPeriodClosed` runs only inside `PostDoubleEntryTx` and payroll (`accounting_periods.go:256`, `finance.go:182`) → 74.1.5.
    - (d) **Three stock writers bypass the choke point:** transfers, the cycle-count post and WMS bin writes (`transfer_orders.go:168, 298`, `wms.go:697`). A transfer shortfall used to be received nowhere. *2026-10-18:* 73.1.7's lifecycle (`transfer_lifecycle.go`) now tracks damaged / lost / excess / returned per line, lot and serial, each with a *Transfer Discrepancy* reason code. Lost and damaged units still post no GL, and the old single-call receive keeps its free-text reason (TRN-0259) → 74.1.1, 74.2.3.
    - (e) **There are no attachments.** "Attachment" is not a supported field type (`doctype.go:94`); only PIM product media can be uploaded (`pim_media.go:275`) → 74.1.6.
    - (f) **GL accounts are hard-coded** (`finance.go:424-581`, `returns.go:867`, `notes.go:78-114`):
      - POS: 1100 / 1101 / 1102 / 4100 / 5100
      - GRN: 1200 / 2100
      - refund: 4100 / 1100. *2026-10-18:* since 73.1.6 a refund goes back to each tender's clearing account, but a "Store Credit" choice falls through to cash 1100 (`paymentModeClearingAccount` default, `finance.go:444`).
      - credit note: 4150 / 1100

      Only 72.1's item expense account and 72.8's liability account are configurable → 74.1.3. Stage 73 has since added more fixed accounts: 5290 till petty cash (73.2.7) and 2630 loyalty liability (73.2.12).
    - (g) **A POS sales return creates no GST credit note.** It prints as "Sales Return", numbered with the `RR…` document id rather than a series (`print_documents.go:641-643`, `returns_atomic.go:199`). The separate `CreditNote` posts Dr 4150 / Cr 1100 with no tax split (`notes.go:78-114`) → 74.2.2.
    - (h) **Reports have no store / location scope.** They are limited only by module gating, a row cap and sensitive-column masking; `scope_policy.go` is not applied. They export CSV only, and XLSX exists for the vendor PO alone (`report_export.go:38`, `xlsx_writer.go:198`). The BRD wants permission-scoped registers with CSV / XLSX → 74.5.1. *2026-10-18:* the scope half is now 75.3.3, to be done before any new report.
    - (i) **Transaction prints record nothing on the server.** The print data endpoint only returns data, and "printed by / at" is filled in by the browser from its own clock (`trade-docs.js:409-421`). Store, party and GSTIN are read live from today's masters (`print_documents.go:132-177`) and PO lines are re-priced at print time (`:411`), so a reprint after a master change shows different particulars → 74.1.4.
    - (j) **POS session close counts only cash.** Expected cash = opening + gross Cash / blank-mode paid carts, not net of refunds, gift cards or loyalty, with no per-tender totals (`pos_session.go:104-141, 265-324`). An advance or a store-credit movement has no line to land on → 74.2.1, 73.2.7. *2026-10-18: fixed by 73.2.7* (`SessionCashPosition`: float + cash tendered − cash refunds ± paid in / paid out / safe drops). A per-tender close is 77.5. Advances and store credit still need their own lines in it.

The number is not duplicated, but the save fails → 74.1.2. *2026-10-18:* the length cap is now 76.7 (a length count against the country cap). The race is unchanged.

#### Stage 100 — Custom data dashboards: build your own charts and number tiles from the ERP's data, filtered by date and store (opened 2026-10-19 from the user's message) ✅ (archived 2026-11-10)

User, 2026-10-19: *"Data Custom Dasboard"* (one of four asks; see Stage 99's opening).

**What exists (found while recording, 2026-10-19).**
- The home dashboard is a saved **DashboardLayout** (`engines/dashboard.go`, 37.11): a list of tiles, each tile one registered report shown as its table; private, or the default for a role. **DashboardDigest** emails all its tiles as one CSV on a schedule. The default is four exception reports.
- Reports come from the `ReportDefinition` / `RegisterReport` framework, already cut by the viewer's store scope and money permission.
- Fixed per-module screens: warehouse cockpit, PIM dashboard, OMS console tiles, CRM analytics (lifetime value, cohort retention). The Inventory dashboard (88.5.1) is not started.
- No charts anywhere: the front end draws none, and a tile cannot be a number, a line or a bar.

**Decisions (asked 2026-10-19; not yet answered):**
- **D1 What a widget can read.** Recommended: (a) any registered report, and (b) a **dataset** builder over a fixed list of datasets - sales lines, POS bills, stock on hand, stock movements, purchase orders, goods receipts, transfers, customers, loyalty, online orders, expenses, ledger - pick fields, filters, group by, sum / count / average. The server builds the query from that list only, with the viewer's store scope and money permission applied. Rejected: a SQL box, even for admins (another client's data, the database's safety).
- **D2 Widget types.** Recommended: number with change against the previous period, line, bar (stacked too), donut, table and pivot (rows × columns), drawn as SVG by a small hand-written helper - no chart library (first principle).
- **D3 Filters.** Recommended: dashboard-wide date (today, this week, month to date, custom), store, brand, category and channel; a widget may fix its own.
- **D4 Who builds, who sees.** Recommended: a **Build dashboards** permission; share with users, roles or stores; every viewer sees only their own stores' data, and money only if their role may, so one dashboard serves every store manager.
- **D5 How fresh.** Recommended: loaded on open and refreshed every 5 minutes while open (a setting); each widget's result kept for 60 seconds on the server so 100 stores opening the same dashboard do not each hit the database.

**Order:** 100.1 data layer → 100.2 charts and the widget editor → 100.3 dashboards, sharing, ready-made set → 100.4 guides and walk-through.

#### Stage 63 — Print Template Studio for transactions (opened 2026-10-15 from the user's message during Stage 62) ✅ (archived 2026-10-19)

**Why it was opened.** The user, mid-Stage 62: *"Print template should be customisable by the user. Drag and drop from master table. Placement for each template. Similar to barcode print, drag and drop from product attribute. I can map product-wise different templates. Each transaction should have its template: PO one page, Transfer Out one page, Transfer In, GRN, Vendor PO template — Vendor PO may have images, in Excel, or exact product detail. My brand name will always be there. There should be a selection of which store I am generating from, and a place in the template for it. Store address, state, product detail, tax bifurcation, total and everything should be there."*

**Decisions taken without asking (user: "don't ask, start building") — reversible, flag if wrong:**
- **One document designer, not a second sticker studio.** A transaction print is a page with flowing line tables and a tax summary, so it renders to HTML pages (exact on any printer, PDF via the browser); the Sticker Studio stays the thermal-label designer. Same way of working: drag fields from a searchable field list, inspector, mm positions, snap.
- **Print data comes from one server endpoint per document** (header fields, brand, generating store, vendor / other store, every line with its Item master fields and image, GST split per rate, totals, amount in words), so a template can place *any* field and every transaction prints the same way.
- **Templates are `PrintTemplate` records** per transaction (PO, Vendor PO, GRN, Transfer Out, Transfer In, Debit Note, Vendor Credit Note), with a default per transaction and optional **mapping by vendor and by product family/category** — the most specific match wins, and the user can still pick another at print time.
- **Brand always prints:** setting `print.brand_name` (blank = the legal entity's name); a template without a brand element gets it in the page header automatically.
- **"Which store I am generating from"** is chosen at print time (defaults to the document's own store); its name, address, state, GSTIN fill the store block.
- **Vendor PO to Excel** is a hand-written .xlsx (standard library zip/XML, no new dependency) with the item image in a column when the item has one.

#### Stage 98 — Print, PDF, send and export for every transaction: PDF download, the vendor's copy sent by the ERP, the right printer at each store chosen once, CSV / Excel line exports with the item matrix, attribute names you can rename (opened 2026-10-19 from the user's Send to Vendor screenshot and two messages)

User, 2026-10-19 (screenshot: the *Sent to Vendor* pop-up on a PO): *"I want to download in vendor template and Sent it to Vendor. Same for PO, GRN, TO and Sales Bill. I want a pdf download and print as well. As we have print set up. It will call diff printer for barcode and other a4 or a5 or pos bill style other style prin t automatically if all connected. ERP will be installed in 100 stores. All printer will be different. Need auto call to those printer. once erp connected. It should ask one time which printer for what txn once then nver ask. But user can change it. & I am ok if it happen automatically with out asking user in erp."* Then: *"i can download csv & excel also each txn where ever product invovled as design combination barcode qty and all other item matrixes and mrp (& add cost price in po and grn only.) & other detail as per txn po number, or grn number, vendor name & I need brand in item matrix. (Optional) User can rename atribute name like color to colour or anything."*

**What exists (found while planning, 2026-10-19).**
- The Print dialog (`printTransactionDocument`, `public/trade-docs.js`) on PO (PO / Vendor PO), GRN (GRN / Vendor Copy), Transfer (Out / In), Sales Invoice, the POS tax invoice, returns and notes: template, generating store, live preview. **Print** is the browser's print dialog (`window.print()`). **Excel** exists only for a PO (`/purchase-order/{id}/excel`, the hand-written `engines/xlsx_writer.go`, no library). No PDF download anywhere.
- **Send to Vendor** stamps `sent_to_vendor_at` and fires `PurchaseOrderIssued` at a `NotificationChannelConfig` webhook: nothing is attached and the ERP emails nobody itself. The server can already send mail (`net/smtp` with `SMTP_HOST` ..., used for account notices). The blocking pop-up in the screenshot is already a toast in the tree (92.4).
- **Silent printing** exists through QZ Tray (`public/qz-print.js`) for stickers, shipping labels and receipts. `resolveQZPrinter` (`internal/server/handlers_qz_print.go`) takes the first Active Printer whose *Default For* matches the job **across the whole company**: the Printer's Location is ignored, so 100 stores would all get the same printer. *Default For* knows Shipping Label, Invoice, Sticker, Receipt, General - not PO, GRN or Transfer. A4 / A5 documents never go through QZ.
- Every print is built by one function, `BuildPrintDocument` (`engines/print_documents.go`): each line already carries SKU, barcode, design, variant, qty, rate, MRP, tax, amount and every attribute under its Item Attribute **Label** (87). An export built on it covers every transaction at once.
- Item Attribute has a code and a **Label**; the label is what the PO add row, the prints and the 87 columns show. Industry-profile fields (the jewellery Color, Polish ...) are relabelled through Settings ▸ Customize ▸ Dynamic Labels.

**Decisions (asked 2026-10-19; answered the same day: D1 picture of the print, D2 both - the ERP emails the PDF and a PDF download is always there to send yourself, D3 per computer on the server, D5 as recommended; D4 automatic, as the user allowed; D6 and D7 as recommended):**
- **D1 How the PDF is made.** Recommended: from the pages the print preview already shows - each page drawn to an image in the browser and put into a PDF by a small hand-written writer (no library). Print, PDF, email and silent print then look the same; the PDF is a picture of the page (text not selectable, about 0.3-0.5 MB a page). Alternative: a PDF writer in Go on the server - selectable text, but a second layout engine to keep identical to the template studio, and a font to ship for the ₹ sign. A JavaScript PDF library is ruled out by the no-dependency rule.
- **D2 How Send reaches the vendor.** Recommended: the ERP emails it itself - to the vendor's email, the PDF attached, sent from the server's mail account with the store's email as Reply-To; the webhook keeps firing for anyone who uses one. With no vendor email it downloads the PDF and records the send, as now.
- **D3 Where "which printer for what" is kept.** Recommended: per computer, saved on the server - computer + store + kind of print → printer, so it survives a browser reset and can be seen centrally; a store-wide Printer record (Location + Default For) is the fallback for a new computer. Alternative: per store only - simpler, but two billing counters in one store could not use different printers.
- **D4 Ask or choose automatically.** The user allowed automatic. Planned: choose by itself when the choice is clear (A4 / A5 documents → the computer's default printer; bills → the one receipt printer; stickers → the one label printer), ask once only when two printers fit; a toast names the printer used, with **Change**.
- **D5 Prices in exports.** Recommended: PO and GRN carry cost (rate, taxable, tax, amount); a sales bill carries its own selling price (it is printed on the bill); transfers, returns and every other export carry **MRP only**.
- **D6 Brand.** Recommended: a **Brand** column in exports and in the print's item table, filled from the item; shown when any line has a brand, and a template or export can leave it out.
- **D7 Renaming attribute names.** Recommended: the **Label** on Setup ▸ Inventory ▸ Item Attribute is the one name shown everywhere (PO, GRN, prints, exports, filters); renaming never changes stored values, because the code stays.

**Order:** 98.1 exports (no device work) → 98.2 PDF → 98.3 send → 98.4 printer routing → 98.5 docs and walk-through.

#### Stage 99 — Shopify: products, prices and stock out; orders, payments and refunds in; shipping sent back (opened 2026-10-19 from the user's message)

User, 2026-10-19: *"Shopify Integration. Data Custom Dasboard. CRM Moule better/best one. Store app. Add in checklist to build all this"* - recorded as one Stage each: **99** Shopify, **100** custom data dashboards, **101** CRM, **102** store app. Nothing built yet. Suggested order across the four: 100 first (no outside dependency, and 101 and 102 read its datasets) → 101 → 102; 99.1-99.7 can be built at any time against a fake Shopify in tests, only the live run (99.8) waits for credentials.

**What exists (found while recording, 2026-10-19).**
- `engines/connector_shopify.go` publishes one product with its images (GraphQL Admin API, staged uploads) and reads it back; its rate limit self-corrects from Shopify's query cost. The publish payload (`ChannelProductPayload`, `engines/connector.go`) is product-level - title, description, mapped attributes, images - with no variants, prices or stock.
- `POST /api/v1/integration/shopify/product/map` links an ERP SKU to Shopify; `POST /api/v1/integration/shopify/order` takes the orders webhook (HMAC-checked) into a Sales Order with customer name, shipping address and SKU / qty / price only - no Shopify order number, discounts, shipping charge, tax lines, payment, phone or email.
- The token and shop address are stored encrypted (`engines/channel_credentials.go`).
- Under the Stage 35.6 connector SDK, Shopify is a **legacy** connector (`engines/connector_zz_legacy_sdk.go`): pull orders, push stock and push order status are not implemented. WooCommerce has all three and is the pattern. So stock, prices, shipping / tracking, cancellations, refunds and payouts do not flow today.
- It has never run against a real Shopify store: 20.3 / 26.2.1 have waited for non-production credentials since 2026-07.

**Decisions (asked 2026-10-19; not yet answered):**
- **D1 Which side owns what.** Recommended: the ERP owns products, prices and stock; Shopify owns online orders and their payments. A price or stock edit made in Shopify admin is overwritten at the next sync, and the sync log says so.
- **D2 How the ERP connects.** Recommended: a Shopify **custom app** in each client's store, its admin token pasted once into the ERP. Alternative: a public Shopify app (one-click install for every client) - needs a Shopify Partner account, Shopify's app review and an install (OAuth) flow.
- **D3 Stock per location.** Recommended: each Shopify location mapped to one ERP store or warehouse; the quantity sent is available minus reserved minus a safety buffer (a setting), never below 0.
- **D4 How orders arrive.** Recommended: webhooks (order created / updated / cancelled, refund created) plus a pull every 15 minutes that catches any webhook Shopify failed to deliver; the Shopify order ID stops an order being imported twice.
- **D5 Which store ships.** Recommended: the store mapped to the Shopify location Shopify chose; the OMS allocation rules move it when that store has no stock.
- **D6 Shopify POS.** Recommended: out of scope - the ERP's own POS bills the stores.

**Needed from the user:** a Shopify development store (or the client's store), a custom app on it with access to products, inventory, locations, orders, fulfilments and customers, and its webhook secret.

**Order:** 99.1 connector (built against Shopify's API shape in tests, no store needed) → 99.2 setup page → 99.3 products and prices → 99.4 stock → 99.5 orders → 99.6 shipping, cancellations, refunds → 99.7 payouts → 99.8 live run on a development store → 99.9 guides.

#### Stage 76 — Short codes, store-wise transaction numbering, state dropdowns, address lines, country-correct tax IDs (opened 2026-10-17 from the user's New Vendor screenshot)

**Why it was opened.** On the New Vendor dialog: the code comes out as `Vendor/HQ/2026/000006` (no series confirmed → fallback shape with store and year), State is free text and optional, the address is one line, and GSTIN is checked against India's shape only, with no check digit and no regard to the home country. The inventory behind 76.7-76.11 found worse on the transaction side: the POS bill number is made by the browser (`POS-<store>-<epoch>`, `view-pos.js:951`), sales invoices / credit notes / JVs are 32-character `NewDocID`s, and series numbers use the maker's session store rather than the document's own store. None of those meet India's 16-character rule.

**Decisions (user, 2026-10-17):**
- **D1** Existing long master codes are re-coded to the short style, with every reference updated (user chose "Re-code everything" over keep-old).
- **D2** Transaction numbers are user-controlled **per store, per transaction** (PO, GRN, ST/TO, TI, POS bill, advance, return, MI, MR, damage, ...). A store with no series cannot transact. A new store appears in the module automatically. The final length is capped at the country's legal maximum - India **16** (CGST Rule 46(b); the IRP portal also refuses longer). No published cap was found for the other home countries, so they get a product cap of 20, shown on the screen.
- **D3** State starts blank and must be picked. It fills itself from the GSTIN when there is one, and a State that contradicts the GSTIN is refused.
- **D4** (user: "better practices are ok, but short") A master code is a prefix plus a zero-padded number, with no separator, store or year, never resetting: `V00001`. The prefix and length are asked for **in the master's own New form** the first time.
- **D5** State short code = ISO 3166-2 (`KA`; 2023 codes CG/OD/TS/UK, older ones accepted). It is filled into `state_code` on setups (Legal Entity, Location) and not shown on Vendor.
- **D6** Every address = Address Line 1 (the existing field, relabelled - no data moves) + Address Line 2 + City + State + PIN code.
- **D7** The tax ID follows the home country: India GSTIN with its check digit; 22 other countries with a certain rule; the rest get 5-20 letters/digits.

##### 76.A Masters and addresses

- [/] **76.3** Address lines: `address` relabelled Address Line 1, plus `address_line2` (+ City, PIN code where missing) on Vendor, Location and Legal Entity; SalesOrder shipping address the same; OMS manual order form split; prints join the lines. *Partly done 2026-10-17:* migration `76_2` (Line 1 relabelled, Line 2 / City / PIN / State / State Code added; SalesOrder line 2 / city / PIN) and `addressLines` in the PO and party print blocks (`print_documents.go`, `purchase_order.go`). **Left:** the OMS manual-order form split (`view-oms.js`) and the POS receipt (`qz_payload.go`) - both have another session's uncommitted edits.
  **Rest done 2026-10-18 ("Build 2 to 9 all").** OMS manual order: Address line 1 · line 2 · City · State (the home country's list) · PIN code (6 digits, required) in one row; `POST /api/v1/orders` takes `shipping_address_line2` / `shipping_city` / `shipping_state` / `shipping_pincode`; the order stores the parts beside `shipping_address` (line 1). `engines.ShippingAddressText` reads them back whole - validation (the PIN check), sourcing, re-allocation, order changes and a replacement order use it, so a split address still carries its PIN; a channel order's one-string address reads back unchanged. Order detail *Ship to* joins them; the courier PIN lookup takes `shipping_pincode` first. POS receipt: the store's address (lines, city, PIN from its Location) under its name, in the printer and HTML forms (`ReceiptStoreHeader.Address`) - a GST tax invoice must show the supplier's address. Test `TestStage763ShippingAddressText` + order / receipt / QZ tests; browser on scratch :8151 - fields in one row, 38 states, "Enter the 6-digit PIN code" when it is missing, no page errors. USER_GUIDE 9A.1 and the receipt paragraph updated. *Status: Done*
