#### Stage 44 — Per-tenant hostnames (`<client>.wholeops.in`) ✅ (opened + built 2026-08-14, **live-verified in production 2026-09-13**)

Opened because the user registered **wholeops.in** (Hostinger, 2026-08-14) and asked for a URL scheme of `clientbrandname.wholeops.in` with the module after the hostname. Checking that against the code first found **the scheme did not exist on either axis**, and that is recorded here rather than quietly building something adjacent:

- `apiMiddleware` never consulted the `Host` header at all. Tenant came from `X-Tenant-ID`, then `?tenant_id=`, then `"default"`, and after login from the bearer token's own claim. One hostname served every tenant.
- The SPA routes on `location.hash` (`public/app.js`), so the module segment is `#oms`, not `/oms`.

**Scope decision (2026-08-14):** the host→tenant half is built now because it is what makes per-client addresses real. The `/module` path half is **not** built — see 44.6.

**Backward compatibility is the load-bearing property**: the entire feature is inert unless `TENANT_BASE_DOMAIN` is set. Unset, `tenantForHost` returns "no match", `originAllowed` falls back to the old exact-match allowlist, and the ask gate refuses everything — so the localhost and SSH-tunnel paths behave exactly as before. Locked by its own tests rather than assumed.

#### Stage 54 — Version identity in the UI (opened + built 2026-10-04 from the user's request) ✅ (archived 2026-10-19)

User asked for "a version system in erp. Std one. It will show near profile. Each deploy should update automatically and user friendly one and release/build date as well." Scoped on inspection: the **backend already existed** (Stage 14.6) — `internal/server/VERSION` is `go:embed`ed, `gitCommit`/`buildTime` are `-ldflags`-stamped by `manage.ps1`, `deploy/deploy.ps1`, `promote.ps1` and CI, and `GET /api/v1/version` has been public since 14.6. Nothing surfaced any of it in the app. So this Stage is the UI plus the one derived field it needed, not a new version system.

Three product calls came from the user mid-build: **keep the version at `0.1.0`** (bumping it would desync ~47 governance docs carrying `applies_to: source release 0.1.0`, and nothing about the UI requires a different number); **version and date only** — the git commit and build timestamp were explicitly rejected as "not user friendly", so an About dialog, a copy-for-support action and the commit/build-time rows that were built first were all removed again before this landed; and after seeing it live, **the date came off the screen entirely** (see 54.3a).

**Note for whoever bumps the release number**: `internal/server/VERSION` is the single source. Nothing else needs touching for the UI — the date follows the build automatically. ~47 docs under `docs/` carry `applies_to: source release 0.1.0` in their frontmatter and would want a sweep at the same time; `cmd/doclint` only checks that the key exists, not its value, so they will not fail the build if left behind.

#### Stage 47 — Deep persona audit remediation: trustworthy, lightweight, self-operable ERP ⏳ (planned 2026-09-01; ≈30-45 sessions, release-gated)

Source of record: [`audits/ERP_DEEP_PERSONA_AUDIT_2026-09-01.md`](audits/erp-deep-persona-audit-2026-09-01.md) (live HTTP + browser + code + database evidence) and [`audits/LIGHTWEIGHT_SMOOTHNESS_PLAN_2026-09-01.md`](audits/lightweight-smoothness-plan-2026-09-01.md) (first-principles architecture, resource budgets and sequencing). The documentation reorganization needed to keep the resulting product supportable is separately planned in [`audits/DOCUMENTATION_ARCHITECTURE_PLAN_2026-09-01.md`](audits/documentation-architecture-plan-2026-09-01.md).

**Why this Stage exists:** the audit found that breadth is ahead of control integrity. A fast screen is not smooth when a Cashier can read payroll/trial balance/system logs, a tampered POS client can choose price/cost, a failed checkout can leave stock posted and deduct it again on retry, a partial return can be replayed, a 3PL allocation can cross owners, or a phone-sized WMS task cannot accept an alphanumeric Wave ID. Stage 47 is therefore a trust-and-operability program, not another module expansion.

**Release rule:** 47.R0 (47.0-47.7) is the critical path. Do not call payroll/privacy, high-value POS, mixed-owner 3PL, mobile/RF WMS, or regulated audit-trail use Production-ready until its applicable R0 gates pass. Existing Stage 37-39 work may continue in parallel only where it does not change the same authorization, POS/return, inventory-owner, audit, or mobile foundations.

**Lightweight constitution for every 47.x item:** preserve the Go modular monolith + PostgreSQL + vanilla-JS topology. No mandatory Redis/Kafka/Elasticsearch/Kubernetes/frontend framework/Node runtime or new production service unless a measured SLO and an ADR prove PostgreSQL/stdlib cannot meet it. Every item records executable/RSS/browser-byte/database-growth/background-work/retention delta. Budgets: stripped binary ≤25 MiB (audit baseline 16.59), idle small-tenant RSS ≤80 MiB (baseline ≈65), cold core transfer ≤180 KiB compressed (baseline ≈287), core JS before interaction ≤120 KiB gzip (baseline ≈237), no unbounded list/report endpoint, no generic failure at the specified normal-screen burst, audit/security hot data ≤20% of hot DB after the legally reviewed retention design (baseline ≈71%), zero mandatory external runtime downloads (no `npm`/`npx`/CDN/remote-font dependency to build or start), p75 LCP ≤1.5s and p75 INP ≤200ms on the reference journeys, cached view-switch p95 ≤250ms, and server p95 ≤150ms/p99 ≤500ms per endpoint under representative load.

##### Release train 47.R3 — legal readiness, assurance and product maturity gates

**Stage 47 completion definition:** all applicable R0 conditional stop-ships closed or unsupported configurations technically blocked; R1 budgets and replica/restart behavior proven at representative scale; target owner/floor roles complete reference journeys without developer help; R2 documentation and supported claims match runtime; R3 qualified/external evidence is attached where required; no new infrastructure added speculatively. Only then may the product claim the applicable configuration is Production rather than an exceptionally broad prototype.

#### Stage 49 — Evidence-driven maximum-security program ⏳ (planned 2026-09-03; ≈40-60 sessions, continuous release gate)

**North-star, not a marketing claim:** “most secure in the world” is not an objectively provable permanent state. The product goal is the strongest practical, independently evidenced security posture for each supported deployment and industry configuration. Never claim “unhackable,” universally secure, certified or compliant. Publish the exact scope, release, configuration, controls tested, residual risks, exceptions, assessor and expiry behind every assurance statement.

**Security constitution:** secure by default; deny and fail closed; least privilege; explicit tenant/entity/location/owner scope; server-authoritative business decisions; one durable outcome per command; no shared or hidden support access; no hard-coded/default credential; no secret or sensitive payload in source, URL, client storage, ordinary log or documentation; no control silently disabled to improve speed; no security-through-obscurity; no production claim without prevention, detection, response and recovery evidence. A security control that operators cannot understand, users route around, or the team cannot patch is not complete.

**Dependency and ownership rule:** Stage 49 does not reopen or duplicate work. **47.0-47.7** remain the P0 stop-ship remediation; **47.8** owns browser/session containment; **47.11** owns bounded request/worker/side-effect safety; **47.16** owns India-first control implementation; **47.17** owns reference-journey release evidence; **48.6** owns the normative security/privacy/legal documents; existing **20.5/26.11.1** own the external penetration-test engagement; **38.2d** owns OAuth2 client credentials. Stage 49 turns those controls into one threat-led security system and adds the missing platform, SDLC, detection, recovery and continuous-assurance gates. Security, privacy, infrastructure, product, finance/control, data, SRE and qualified legal/audit owners approve their domains; an AI/developer may draft and test but cannot self-certify them.

**Lightweight security rule:** retain one Go application plus PostgreSQL and the vanilla-JS client. No mandatory WAF appliance, service mesh, SIEM cluster, secrets platform, message broker, policy engine, antivirus daemon, Node toolchain or security sidecar merely to obtain a checkbox. Prefer compile-time route contracts, shared middleware, PostgreSQL constraints/transactions, OS/reverse-proxy controls, bounded structured events and optional export adapters. A new dependency/service requires 47.18.4 evidence and an ADR. Every 49.x item records binary/static-byte, cold-start, request CPU/latency, idle/peak RSS, DB/index/WAL/log/backup growth and operator burden. Security evidence obeys approved retention/legal holds and may not recreate the audit-log space failure Stage 47 found.

**Priority rule:** 49.S0 and the applicable Stage 47 P0 items are release-blocking. 49.S1-S3 must close before an internet-facing multi-tenant Production claim. 49.S4 must close before the corresponding enterprise, regulated or contractual assurance claim. Existing module work may continue only when it does not alter the same security boundary without updating its threat model and tests.

##### Phase 49.S4 — People, vulnerability operations, legal assurance and continuous proof

**Stage 49 completion definition:** all supported surfaces, crown jewels and trust boundaries are owned and threat-modeled; Stage 47 stop-ships are closed or unsupported configurations are technically impossible; identity/session/authorization/tenant/business invariants withstand the adversarial matrix; data, keys, host, database, integrations, build and artifacts have verified lifecycle controls; priority attacks are detectable and rehearsed through containment/recovery; independent testing has no unresolved critical/high finding in scope; every customer/legal claim is configuration-specific and approved; continuous gates prevent silent regression; and the fully secured reference deployment remains within the lightweight performance, memory, storage and dependency budgets.

**Bugs this pass found in its own work, by testing against a clone of the dev DB before touching it:**
- The first matrices were written from `db/migration.sql`'s original option strings, but later migrations had extended four doctypes (`PurchaseOrder` gained `Pending Approval`/`Rejected`, `ProductionOrder` gained `In Process`, `TransferOrder` gained `Packed`, `CycleCountLine` gained `Recount Requested`). A real PurchaseOrder was sitting in `Pending Approval` that strict mode would have **frozen permanently**. - A real `SalesInvoice` was sitting in status `Active`, which isn't in its own option set (legacy debris). No rule can name a `from_status` the schema doesn't declare, so strict mode would have trapped that row forever. Added an escape: a write leaving an **undeclared** status is always allowed — the destination is still constrained by `ValidateDocument`, so this can only move debris back into a legal state.

Four defects reported by the user in one session, all in `public/app.js`/`public/styles.css` only (no Go, no schema, no dependency). See `project_ledger.md` §65.

**Testing gotcha found here (worth knowing next time):** sidebar module labels are **tenant-configurable**, not fixed strings — mid-session the shared dev DB's active profile changed and the same modules rendered as `POS`/`Financial Accounting`/`Procurement`/`HRM` instead of `Point of Sale`/`Accounting`/`Buying`/`HR & Assets`, which broke a Playwright check that matched on the English name. UI tests against this app must key off element IDs or DOM order, never the visible label. A test that "suddenly fails" on a nav label is very likely this, not a regression.

**Verification (2026-07-28):** `node --check public/app.js` clean. Live Playwright against the running dev server as `manager1`: all 38 sidebar entries click-navigate; hover→click via a realistic pointer path 34/34 (a continuous diagonal corner-cut, the worst realistic case, went from 6/34 before the fix to 32/34 after); the three original flyout repro scenarios all pass; search suggestions correct for `buy`/`invoice`/`bin`/`pos` with a proper empty state for a non-match, and both Enter-to-navigate and click-to-navigate confirmed; zero console/page errors throughout. Dark and light both screenshot-checked, with computed contrast ratios recorded above. **Not changed:** the `category`/`HSN` half of the search placeholder — suggesting menus and record types is navigation over data the client already holds; searching product records across entities would need a new server-side endpoint and is a separate piece of work, not a bug fix.

Note 32.3's scripts are built but not yet run on the droplet, so production still has no backups until the user installs the cron.)

User report, after using the deployed app: *"The interface is not at all smooth. I have to click many times. Then it is working. Hover is also not working. I have to click on arrow then it is showing permanently else it is going away."*

- **Verified 2026-08-04, live in Chromium against the real `index.html`/`styles.css`/`app.js`** (harness serves `public/` statically and seeds an `erp_token`; `setupModuleFlyouts()` runs synchronously at the top of `init()`, before the first `await`, so the nav binds fully even with every API call 404ing). 12 assertions, 5 consecutive clean runs. The decisive pair, run against `HEAD` and against the fix:
  - *jittery approach, 6 runs* — **before: `[2, 81, 3, 445, 70, 477]`ms** (the randomness the user was feeling); **after: `[4, 1, 4, 2, 7, 4]`ms.**
  - *hover a module, wait a beat, then reach right for the menu* — **before: no menu at all** (leaving the row cancelled the pending open *and* scheduled the hide, so clicking the arrow was genuinely the only thing that worked — exactly the reported behaviour); **after: the menu is there.**
  - Also asserted: cold hover opens < 150ms; a fast sweep across 10 rows still opens ≤ 2 menus en route; crossing the 8px gap into the panel keeps it open; the diagonal reach to the item at the bottom of an 11-item flyout survives the trip and that item ends up `:hover`ed; leaving the nav closes within 400ms. A straight synthetic path down the sidebar has `dx == 0` and so **never trips the old bug** — reproducing it needed a jittering pointer, which is why this is worth keeping as a harness rather than a one-off check.

#### Stage 56 — Railway Pro migration (opened 2026-10-04 from the user's decision)

The user purchased a **Railway annual plan (₹3,000/year)** and decided to proceed; the DigitalOcean
droplet is ₹500/month. Assessment on opening found the app is already largely PaaS-ready and the
work is smaller than a provider migration usually is: migrations are `go:embed`ed into the binary
(`db/migrate.go:19`) so Railway's pre-deploy command can apply them with no `db/` folder on the
host; an unset `HOST` binds every interface (`internal/server/routes.go:1190`), which is what
Railway needs; every secret already has an env override (`JWT_SECRET`, `CHANNEL_CREDENTIAL_KEY`,
`AUDIT_ARCHIVE_KEY` — the config-dir file fallbacks in `engines/auth.go:61` /
`engines/secret_keyring.go:123` are dev-only paths production already bypasses); job claiming uses
`FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` (`engines/jobrunner.go:261`), so Railway's overlapping rolling deploys
cannot double-run a job; and the `Dockerfile` — dormant since 2026-07-27, built by CI's
`docker-build-check` on every push so it cannot rot — already produces a distroless static image
stamped with build identity (54.6).

**Architecture decision, recorded because the alternative was the user's first instinct:** this is
**one** Railway app + **one** Railway Postgres serving **many** tenant schemas, via
`TENANT_BASE_DOMAIN` (`internal/server/tenant_host.go`, Stage 44) and `tenantctl provision`.
It is **not** one Railway app per client. One-app-per-client multiplies the metered bill, the
deploys, the migration runs, the backup checks and the version-drift risk by the client count, and
bypasses the multi-tenancy engine already built. Hosting many clients is the goal; separate
instances are not the mechanism. A contractual physical-isolation requirement from a single large
client is the one legitimate exception, and is a priced premium tier, not the default.

**Production stays on the droplet for all of 56.1-56.10.** Nothing in those items touches the live
box, so there is no window where a client is at risk. 56.7/56.8 exist because the two things that
actually decide this migration — metered cost and India latency — are measurements, not
assumptions, and both are now cheap to take since the plan is already paid for.

**2026-10-07 — pre-emptive fix landed for 56.1's expected first failure (`Dockerfile`, uncommitted).**
At the user's request, rather than waiting for the deploy to fail: the runtime stage's base image is
now `ARG RUNTIME_BASE=gcr.io/distroless/static-debian12:debug`, used as `FROM ${RUNTIME_BASE}`. The
`:debug` variant is the same distroless image plus a busybox `/bin/sh` and nothing else — same
`nonroot` user, same static-only contents. Reason: a PaaS pre-deploy/release hook runs its command
*through a shell*, so `./erp-server -migrate` on the shell-free image fails with
`exec: "sh": executable file not found`, which reads like a missing binary and is not one. Made an
overridable ARG rather than a hardcoded swap so the shell-free image can be pinned back with
`--build-arg RUNTIME_BASE=gcr.io/distroless/static-debian12` without editing the file.
**The ARG is declared global (before the first `FROM`) deliberately** — declared inside the builder
stage it is out of scope at the runtime `FROM`, expands to empty, and the build dies on a bare
`FROM`; that mistake was made and corrected while writing this.
Two caveats, both load-bearing:
- **Unverified by build.** Docker is not installed on this machine (`docker: command not found`), so
  this has never been built. CI's `docker-build-check` is the first thing that will exercise it, and
  Railway the first thing that will boot it. Do not record it as working until one of those passes.
- **It cannot reach Railway until it is pushed.** Railway builds from GitHub, which is at `c90e5ca`
  (2026-10-06); this change is uncommitted in the working tree. Until a commit of `Dockerfile`
  reaches `origin/main`, 56.1 will still hit the original shell failure. `Dockerfile`'s only
  uncommitted hunk is this change (54.6's build-identity ARGs are already committed in `c90e5ca`),
  so it is cleanly committable on its own — but committing/pushing is the user's call, not a routine
  dev step, per the Git Safety Protocol.
- **Retire this before 56.12** if a container path ever becomes production: a shell in the runtime
  image widens the Stage 49.S2 attack surface and is justified only while the migrate hook needs it.
  Either run migrations as a one-off job that bypasses a shell, or confirm the platform can invoke
  the hook in exec form. Today's droplet production runs the plain binary under systemd and is
  unaffected by this line.

**Carried from the opening assessment, so it is not rediscovered:** the four items that read as
alarming (56.2, 56.3, 56.4, 56.9) are ~1 to 1.5 days of work in total, not the bulk of this Stage.
Three are config-sized once the empirical value in 56.3 is known. The weight is in 56.9/56.10
(backups, done properly) and 56.12 (verification and a safe cutover) — the same shape as any
provider move: the container was never the hard part.

#### Stage 96 — No Windows Firewall dialog when a dev erp-server starts (opened 2026-10-18 from the user's Windows Security screenshot) ✅ (archived 2026-10-19)

User, 2026-10-18: *"Still asking. See to avoid this. I turned off setting"* - screenshot of Windows Security: "Do you want to allow public and private networks to access this app? Windows Firewall has blocked some features of erp-server", with UAC already lowered.

Why it asks: with `HOST` unset, `internal/server/routes.go` binds all interfaces (`":"+port`), and Windows Firewall asks about every newly built `erp-server.exe` that listens on the network. UAC has nothing to do with it. Production (`HOST=127.0.0.1` in `erp.env`) and the Docker image are Linux, so Windows is only ever a dev or test box.

**Decisions (made here, from the user's "tell the suitable way"):** D1 the release and deploy are PowerShell scripts in the repo started by double-click `.cmd` files at the root, like `Open-ERP.cmd` - no new tools or dependencies. D2 the cleanup runs on the server as a root cron job, not inside the ERP: it needs root, must work when the ERP is down, and keeps the ERP light. D3 the deploy click shows every pending migration that changes client data and waits for the user to type YES - it replaces Claude's questions before a deploy. D4 work that must not ship is listed in `deploy/release-hold.txt` (git-ignored); the release leaves those paths out. D5 the gates live in one script plus `deploy/RELEASE_GATES.md`; a session that meets a release step the script missed adds it there in the same session (CLAUDE.md rule). D6 SSH bots: sshguard (C, ~2 MB RAM), not fail2ban (Python, ~30 MB) and not ufw `limit` (a deploy opens ~9 SSH connections in under a minute and would lock itself out).

#### Stage 30 — Usability & Manual Overhaul ✅ (from the 2026-07-30 layman audit; 30.1/30.2 closed 2026-07-31; 30.3, 30.4, 30.6, 30.7 and 30.8 closed 2026-08-01; **30.5.5 and 30.5.8 closed 2026-08-02 — Stage 30 is now complete**)

Backlog derived from a full end-to-end pass where the manual was read first and the live app driven against it as a first-time user. Full evidence, reproductions and scoring: **[docs/UX_MANUAL_AUDIT.md](audits/ux-manual-audit.md)**.

**Framing:** the engine tested well (45/46 catalog reports run; maker-checker, GST and the full PO→GRN→stock→sale chain all correct). The failures are concentrated in (a) one POS lookup defect that blocks the flagship flow, (b) a manual that has drifted badly out of date, and (c) empty/unguided dropdowns. Order below is deliberate: 30.1–30.2 first because nothing else matters if a new user can't ring up a sale; 30.3 next because wrong docs cause wrong actions.

##### 30.5 — App easiness: dropdowns, empty states, forms

- ~~**30.5.5 [needs design decision] Resolve `Stores` vs `Location`.**~~ *(original text, kept for context)* `Location` already has `type: Store,Warehouse,HO` and is what every transaction uses (103 records). `Stores` has **zero Link references and zero Go references** — verified inert — yet is promoted in the sidebar and documented in USER_GUIDE §3 / USER_SOP §21 as "your shop/warehouse locations". A user who follows the manual creates their shop somewhere nothing can select it. Options: retire `Stores` and fold its fields (address/city/phone/manager) into `Location`, or keep it and remove it from the menu + docs. Needs a call before touching data.
  - **Documented rather than decided (2026-08-01, part of 30.3).** The *doc* half of this was a false claim and was fixed independently of the schema decision: USER_GUIDE §8 and USER_SOP §21 both told users to set their shop up as a `Stores` record, which nothing reads. Both now carry an explicit warning to create the shop as a **Location with Type = Store**, and name this item as the open decision. A user following the manual today no longer creates their shop somewhere nothing can select it. **The schema decision itself is still open and still needs the user's call.**

##### 30.6 — Server-issued document numbers (user request, 2026-08-01)

User request, from the Purchase Orders screen: *"PO number will be auto created. I will create po sequence. Same of GRN and all other transaction."* Scope confirmed with the user before building: the ~12 doctypes whose create screens asked a human to type a number (not a blanket sweep of all 38 `document_type='Transaction'` doctypes — most of those are engine-created and already mint their own ids), and admin-configurable segments rather than a hardcoded format.

- **Deliberately not done:** an explicit `id` in the request body is still honored as an upsert. That is this API's long-standing contract (`handleGenericDoc` resolves its id from `payload["id"]` when the path has none; `ProductContent`'s composite-id save and Stage 29.8's transition test both depend on it). Numbering it would turn an update into a duplicate document. No create *screen* sends an id any more, so the user-facing guarantee is intact; only a deliberate API caller can still choose an id.
- **Verified**: `go build` / `go vet` / `node --check` / full `go test ./... -p 1` clean, 20 new tests (`engines/document_numbering_test.go`, `internal/server/document_numbering_api_test.go`). Live over real HTTP on a throwaway port against the dev DB: two identical PO submissions returned `PO/HO/26-27/000007` and `…000008` (the exact collision that used to overwrite); stored docs carry the number on `po_number` **and** `code`; reshaping the TO series to `TRF` / `-` / pad 4 / NEVER / no-store produced `TRF-0001` on the very next save; omitting `include_store` preserved the stored `false`; `auto_generated` flags confirmed correct per doctype over the wire (PO → both fields, ASN → `asn_number` only, Item → none). All live test documents and the temporary series edit were reverted afterward.

**Verification bar for this Stage:** each item is closed only after a live re-run of the exact reproduction in `UX_MANUAL_AUDIT.md`, not just a build/vet pass. Doc items (30.3/30.4) are closed only after walking the corrected steps literally against a running server, since every defect in 30.3 is a case of a doc that was written once and never re-driven.

User request, two parts explicitly framed as separate: *"All the configuration should be in the configuration page module to module. Nothing will be hardcoded. Analyse every module. See where it is hardcode give in config. Ex-PO edit days, GRN edit days, Pinelabs urls, Middleware url, etc etc, & If I change it should immediately change everywhere. Scope decisions taken with the user before building: **all four offer families** (core %/flat, spend thresholds, BOGO/bundles, coupon codes + customer tiers); and platform-safety limits are **exposed as settings with enforced Min/Max guardrails** rather than left in code — "do the proper actionable but it should not be hardcoded".

- **Verified**: `go build` / `go vet` / `node --check` clean; full `go test ./... -p 1` green (db + engines + internal/server); 21 new tests. Live over real HTTP on a throwaway port against the dev DB, including a full MFA/TOTP enrollment to obtain an HR/Admin session: **36 settings across 12 modules** returned by `GET /api/v1/admin/settings`; setting `platform.max_list_limit` to 2 changed a live list endpoint from 3 rows to 2 **in the same process with no restart**, and restoring it returned 3 (this is the "changes everywhere immediately" claim, actually demonstrated); out-of-range `999999` rejected by the guardrail with a specific message; the float type round-tripped `12.5` and rejected `abc`; an Offer created through the ERP applied at the POS preview on the very next call, with the spend threshold, coupon gating (case-insensitive), priority ordering and unmatched-code reporting all behaving as specified. All live test data was removed from the dev DB afterward.
- **Known non-blocking note:** `engines/doctype.go`'s `defaultFieldMaxLength` and `engines/import.go`'s `importBatchRows` constants were re-added by a concurrent session after their call sites had been moved to settings; both are now unused (Go permits unused consts, build is clean) and the live call sites read the settings. Worth deleting whenever that session's work settles.

##### 30.8 — Project brain map (user request, 2026-08-01)

User request: *"put in through graphify and create a graphify diagram about this current erp project. Create a folder under docs with a suitable name and plot there. It will explain the entire project in a diagram. It may behave like a brain. We will append if new is added. See how to add easily if any changes done."* Built in `docs/brain/`, generated by `cmd/brainmap`.

- **Verified**: `go build ./...` / `go vet ./cmd/brainmap` clean. All **7 Mermaid blocks parsed with the real mermaid@11 parser** in a headless browser (not eyeballed) — all render, `<small>` survives `securityLevel: strict`. `brain.html` rendered in headless Chromium in **both** light and dark: 35 region cards, 33 links, no console errors, no NaN geometry, no horizontal body overflow. Two real defects were caught this way and fixed: Go's nil slices serialise as `null` and broke every `.length` read on page load, and the lobe-band backgrounds were painting over the connection lines (three explicit z-layers now). Categorical lobe colours validated with the dataviz palette validator — all checks pass in both modes on the adjacent pairlist, which is the right model here because lobes render in a fixed left-to-right order.
- **Deliberately not done:** no CI hook wiring `-Check` into `.github/workflows/ci.yml`. It would fail the build for an unfiled *new* file, which is a docs concern, not a correctness one — flagging it in the run output and in BRAIN.md §6 is the right weight. Easy to add later if the brain starts drifting.

#### Stages 35-39 — Parity Master Plan ⏳ (opened 2026-08-09; **release train R1 = 35.1/35.2/35.3 built 2026-08-11**; **35 and 37 closed & archived 2026-09-27** — only Stage 38 (38.2d) and Stage 39 (39.18) remain open, each deliberately deferred)

Consolidated from four external benchmarks the user named — [Unicommerce OMS](https://unicommerce.com/products/multichannel-order-management-system/) + the [Uniware documentation portal](https://documentation.unicommerce.com/), the [Unbxd PIM help centre](https://help.pim.unbxd.com/help-documentation/), [SAP Help](https://help.sap.com/) and [Microsoft Dynamics 365](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics-365/) — each reconciled against real code. **Full per-item detail, sizing, sequencing, the 8 open decisions and the explicit out-of-scope list live in [docs/archive/legacy/parity-master-plan.md](legacy/parity-master-plan.md)**; this section is the tracker skeleton only, the same relationship Stage 26.12 has to `oms_master_blueprint_reference.md`.

**Total ≈118 items, ≈61-79 sessions (~3-4 months at this repo's cadence), organised into 7 release trains (R1-R7).** Honest framing carried over from the plan: Unicommerce and Unbxd parity are achievable; **SAP module-count parity is not a coherent goal and is explicitly not being attempted** — Business Central is the ERP benchmark, SAP is read only as a concept checklist.

**The three structural debts R1 exists to clear** (all are existing deliberate deferrals, not new scope): channel orders still land as `POSCart` rather than `SalesOrder` (26.12.1's explicit carve-out), there is no OMS console at all, and the order→shipment→invoice chain is unwired for `SalesOrder` (26.12.3's explicit carve-out).

> ✅ **RESOLVED 2026-08-13 — the dev databases are UTF-8 and the 20.6 defect is closed.** The problem, for the record: `migrations_stage37_1_currency_foundation.sql` seeds `₹`, the dev cluster was **WIN1252**, and SQLSTATE 22P05 stopped the migration runner dead — so every migration from Stage 37.1 onward (37.1.2, 38.2, 38.3, 35.3.7) was blocked. Fixed by dump-and-restore rather than by mangling the migration: `pg_dump --encoding=UTF8` → `CREATE DATABASE ... ENCODING 'UTF8' LOCALE_PROVIDER icu ICU_LOCALE 'en-US' TEMPLATE template0` → restore → rename. **ICU `en-US`, not `C`**, so linguistic sort order matches the old `English_United States.1252` collation instead of silently switching every `ORDER BY` on text to byte order. Verified lossless before the swap: 127 tables identical exact row counts and a matching `md5` content checksum over `tenant_default.documents`. Both `custom_erp` (62 MB) and `custom_erp_test` (the restore-drill target, which would have hit the identical wall) were converted. All 5 blocked migrations then applied, `₹` stored correctly (1 char / 3 bytes), CJK/Arabic/emoji now storable, and `go test ./... -p 1` is green against the converted database. **The originals are retained as `custom_erp_win1252_backup` and `custom_erp_test_win1252_backup`** — nothing was dropped, so the swap is reversible with two `ALTER DATABASE ... RENAME`. Drop them once you are satisfied. Production was always UTF-8 and was never affected.
> - **Finished at the cluster level 2026-08-13**: `template1` — what a bare `CREATE DATABASE` copies, and therefore what was still minting broken databases after the two application databases were converted — was recreated from `template0` as UTF8 + ICU `en-US`. It was pristine, so no user data was involved, and the clause was proven on a throwaway first so the cluster was never left without a `template1`. A database created with no encoding clause at all now comes out UTF-8. `template0` stays WIN1252 **by design** (it is the one template a differing encoding may be copied from); the `postgres` maintenance DB stays WIN1252 by decision, as it mints nothing and holds only retired-WMS debris.
> - **The conversion also exposed how much the 35.3.7 sweeper had to clean**: `custom_erp` held **5,395 orphaned reservations** — stock held out of the sellable pool against lines that were cancelled or gone — which the sweeper drained to 0 with no negative `reserved` counts. That is the leak 35.3.7 was written for, measured on real accumulated data.
>
> ⚠️ **The three "not applied" migrations below ARE APPLIED TO PRODUCTION as of 2026-08-11 16:47:34Z. The safety boundary they were written against no longer exists.** 36.1, 37.1 and 38.2 each record their migration as deliberately unapplied (`BEGIN`/`ROLLBACK`-tested only). That was true when written, and it stopped being true the moment they were committed: `db/migrate.go` does `//go:embed *.sql`, so every `.sql` file sitting in `db/` is embedded and applied by any `erp-server -migrate` or `deploy.ps1` run, with no further decision and no way to scope it. A deploy attempt on 2026-08-11 applied all three to the live droplet. **The existing §6 guard — `git status --porcelain db/` — cannot catch this**, because it only detects *untracked* `.sql` files and these are tracked. Nothing broke (all three are additive and idempotent; 38.2's keys were unusable at the time because no `/api/public/v1` route was registered — **that is no longer true as of the 2026-08-13 `20a8878` deploy**, which registered the four read-only routes and applied the remaining three migrations, `35_3_7`, `37_1_2` and `38_3_5_9`, so an issued key now reaches a live scoped surface), but the lesson generalises: **"unapplied" is never a durable property of a committed migration, and must not be used as the safety boundary for anything.** Verify with `erp-server -migrate-status` rather than inferring from a stage's own notes.

#### Stages 35-39 — Parity Master Plan — Stage 39 — Knowledge Center — ≈7-9 sessions ⏳ (39.1-39.17 + 39.13's 10 handbooks + 39.8/39.9/39.10/39.14/39.15 all closed 2026-09-03; only 39.18 remains, deliberately deferred as its own reviewed unit) — closed items (see docs/micro_checklist.md for this section's remaining open item(s))

**39.2-39.7 built as one unit 2026-08-12**, as planned: the generator, the shell and the access model had to land together or the content would be reachable before it was gated.

outeExists; locked by a new TestDriftGuardsMethodlessRouteIsAWildcard.
**39.11 + 39.12 + 39.16 + 39.17 were authored as one pass on 2026-08-17**, taking the Centre from its 6 seed articles to **23**. Two enabling code changes came first, because every article in this pass cross-references others and the seed content had already got this wrong:
  - **Cross-article links were dangling, and nothing caught it.** `first-login.md` linked `first-order.md`, which rendered as a *relative* href — from `/help/first-login` the browser resolved it to `/help/first-order.md`, a slug that does not exist. `error-codes.md` pointed at `../../guides/ERROR_CODES.md`, which is not reachable from inside the app at all. Fixed at the renderer, not by hand-writing `/help/<slug>` in every article: `articleURL` in `markdown.go` rewrites any scheme-less, host-less `*.md` link to `/help/<basename>`, mirroring `slugFromPath`. Sources stay readable as plain Markdown on disk, and an author cannot get the app's URL shape wrong because they never type it. Fragment preserved; `http(s)` links to some other project's `.md` left alone; the rewrite runs *after* `safeURL`, so it cannot smuggle a scheme past it (pinned by test). `app.js` additionally intercepts in-body `/help/` clicks so a cross-reference is as fast as a sidebar click, leaving modified clicks alone so ctrl/middle-click still opens a tab.
  - **`HeadingSlug` exported** from `internal/kb`, because the generators below write their own contents lists and have to predict the anchor the renderer will emit. A second implementation would have produced a table of contents whose links silently stop resolving — GitHub's anchor rule and this renderer's differ on runs of punctuation (`data-import--excel-upload` vs `data-import-excel-upload`), which is exactly how that goes unnoticed.

#### Stage 48 — Documentation architecture, governance, controlled migration and deletion ⏳ (in progress; started 2026-09-06, reviewed/rebuilt 2026-09-10)

Source of record: [`audits/DOCUMENTATION_ARCHITECTURE_PLAN_2026-09-01.md`](audits/documentation-architecture-plan-2026-09-01.md). Evidence inputs: the [deep persona audit](audits/erp-deep-persona-audit-2026-09-01.md), the [lightweight smoothness plan](audits/lightweight-smoothness-plan-2026-09-01.md), the current 98-file/78-Markdown inventory, and the failed `docs/guides/update-guides.ps1 -Check` audit run that proved `cmd/gendocs` still writes to default live KB/OpenAPI paths behind a staged guide check.

**Purpose:** make every reader—CEO, product owner, normal/floor user, implementer, developer, SRE, security reviewer, auditor and legal reviewer—reach one authoritative, owned, current document for their question. This Stage reorganizes knowledge; it does not use folder movement to hide unresolved product defects or rewrite historical evidence.

**Non-negotiable rules:** plain Markdown + existing Go/PowerShell generators; no Docusaurus/MkDocs/Node documentation build/hosted docs database/new runtime service. The full `docs/` tree is not shipped to production; only the intentionally embedded Knowledge Center output/assets enter the binary/static release budget. No bulk delete, no `git add -A`, no path migration while another session is editing the same documents. Audit/UAT/incident/restore/decision/legal evidence is archived, never casually deleted.

**Dependency rule:** 48.0/48.1 may start independently once the shared worktree settles. Support/capability statements in 48.2 depend on 47.0 evidence. Security/POS/returns/WMS/audit user and normative documents must describe the real current limitation or wait for the applicable 47.x/49.x remediation—never document the intended fix as already built. Stage 47.15 closes only after 48.0, 48.2, 48.7 and the applicable 48.11 gates pass.

**Execution status (2026-09-10): implementation expanded and verified; Stage 48 is not fully accepted.** The isolated recovery capture preserves 889 hash-verified files at `fed51b4`; approval of a baseline commit/tag remains pending. The canonical drafts, 14-domain/42-FR traceability, 199-doctype/1,542-field dictionary, canonical OpenAPI projection, 49 KB topics covering all 56 registered screens, two generated manuals, strict offline lint and cached monthly external checks are built. A 24-path/five-batch migration is prepared in an isolated review checkout with retained published-path stubs; main-workspace paths and evidence are preserved. All 14 live development screenshot captures pass the repaired harness. These are technical observations, not customer, legal, product or physical-device acceptance. The [dated verification and findings](audits/stage48-verification-2026-09-10.md) and [concrete migration review](readme.md) record scope and remaining gates. Checked authoring/tooling items below do not imply approval of their draft policies.

(`erp_qa57_20261004` for suites, `erp_qa57_live_20261004` for the live server - the shared

with no Authorization header, which shared the IP-keyed "default" bucket (60/min) - several tills
